The set $\{\textrm{Peter}, \textrm{Paul}\}$ occupies a location in virtue of the fact that its concrete elements, Peter and Paul, together occupy that location. The set does not occupy the location *in its own right*. With that in mind, it might be said that:
zh: 化解这一困难的一种方式是指出：即使非纯集合占据空间，它们是以派生的方式这样做的。集合 $\{\textrm{Peter}, \textrm{Paul}\}$ 占据某个位置，凭的是其具体元素彼得与保罗共同占据那个位置。这个集合并不是 ** 凭自身权利 ** 占据那个位置的。有鉴于此，可以说：

en: An object is abstract (if and) only if it either fails to occupy space at all, or does so only in virtue of the fact some other items—in this case, its urelements—occupy that region.
zh: 一个对象是抽象的，当且仅当：它要么全然不占据空间，要么只是凭某些其他项——在此即其本元——占据该区域这一事实而占据空间。

en: But of course Peter himself occupies a region in virtue of the fact that his *parts*—his head, hands, etc.—together occupy that region. So a better version of the proposal would say:
zh: 但当然，彼得本人占据一个区域，凭的是其 ** 部分 **——他的头、手等等——共同占据那个区域。所以这一提案更好的版本会说：

en: An object is abstract (if and) only if it either fails to occupy space at all, or does so of the fact that some other items *that are not among its parts* occupy that region.
zh: 一个对象是抽象的，当且仅当：它要么全然不占据空间，要么只是凭某些 ** 不属于其部分 ** 的其他项占据该区域这一事实而占据空间。

en: This approach appears to classify the cases fairly well, but it is somewhat artificial. Moreover, it raises a number of questions. What are we to say about the statue that occupies a region of space, not because its *parts* are arrayed in space, but rather because its constituting *matter* occupies that region? And what about the unobserved electron, which according to some interpretations of quantum mechanics does not really *occupy* a region of space at all, but rather stands in some more exotic relation to the spacetime it inhabits? Suffice it to say that a philosopher who regards ‘non-spatiality’ as a mark of the abstract, but who allows that some abstract objects may have non-trivial spatial properties, owes us an account of the *distinctive relation* to spacetime, space, and time that sets paradigmatic concreta apart.
zh: 这一进路似乎把这些案例分得相当好，但略显人工。此外，它引出许多问题。对那座占据空间区域的雕像——它占据空间不是由于其 ** 部分 ** 在空间中排布，而是由于其构成的 ** 质料 ** 占据那个区域——我们该怎么说？还有未被观察的电子：按量子力学的某些诠释，它其实根本不 ** 占据 ** 空间区域，而是与其栖居的时空处于某种更奇异的关系中？无须赘言：一位把“非空间性”视为抽象之标志、却又允许某些抽象对象可以拥有非平凡空间性质的哲学家，欠我们一个对独特关系的说明——正是这种与时空、空间和时间的关系把典型的具体物区分开来。

en: Perhaps the crucial question about the ‘non-spatiality’ criterion concerns the classification of the parts of space itself. If they are considered concrete, then one might ask where the spatiotemporal points or regions are located. And a similar question arises for spatial points and regions, and for temporal instants or intervals. So, the ontological status of spatiotemporal locations, and of spatial and temporal locations, is problematic. Let us suppose that space, or spacetime, exists, not just as an object of pure mathematics, but as the arena in which physical objects and events are somehow arrayed. It is essential to understand that the problem is not about the numerical coordinates that represent these points and regions (or instants and intervals) in a reference system; the issue is about the points and regions (or instants and intervals). Physical objects are located ‘in’ or ‘at’ regions of space; as a result, they count as concrete according to the non-spatiality criterion. But what about the points and regions of space itself? There has been some debate about whether a commitment to spacetime substantivalism is consistent with the nominalist’s rejection of abstract entities (Field 1980, 1989; Malament 1982)[^field-1980][^malament-1982]. If we define the abstract as the ‘non-spatial’, this debate amounts to whether space itself is to be reckoned ‘spatial’. To reject that these points, regions, instants, and intervals, are concrete because they are not *located*, entails featuring them as abstract. However, to think about them as abstract sounds a bit weird, given their role in causal processes. Perhaps, it is easier to treat them as concrete if we want to establish that concrete entities are spatiotemporal—or spatial and temporal.
zh: 也许关于“非空间性”判准的关键问题，关乎空间自身之部分的归类。如果它们被视为具体的，那么人们可以问：时空点或区域位于哪里。对空间点与区域、时间瞬间与区间，类似的问题也会出现。所以时空位置以及空间与时间位置的存在论地位是成问题的。让我们假定空间或时空存在——不只是作为纯数学的对象，而是作为物理对象与事件以某种方式排布于其中的舞台。必须理解：问题不在于在参考系中代表这些点与区域（或瞬间与区间）的数值坐标；问题在于点与区域（或瞬间与区间）本身。物理对象被定位于空间的区域“之中”或“之上”；因此按非空间性判准它们算具体的。但空间自身的点与区域呢？关于“承诺时空实体论是否与唯名论者对抽象实体的拒斥相容”已有一些争论（Field 1980, 1989; Malament 1982）[^field-1980][^malament-1982]。如果我们把抽象定义为“非空间的”，这场争论就等于问：空间本身是否要算作“空间的”。拒绝承认这些点、区域、瞬间与区间是具体的（因为它们不被 ** 定位 **），就等于把它们列为抽象。然而把它们想成抽象的有点怪，鉴于它们在因果过程中的角色。也许，如果我们想确立“具体实体是时空的——或既在空间又在时间中的”，把它们当作具体的会更容易些。

en: The philosopher who believes that there is a serious question about whether the parts of space-time count as concrete would thus do well to characterize the abstract/concrete distinction in other terms. Still—as mentioned above—the philosopher who thinks that it is defensible that parts of space are concrete might use non-spatiality to draw the distinction if she manages to provide a way of accounting for how impure sets relate to space differs from the way concreta do.
zh: 认为时空部分是否算具体确有严重问题的哲学家，因此最好用别的术语刻画抽象/具体之分。不过——如上所述——认为空间部分为具体可以辩护的哲学家，如果她设法说明非纯集合与空间的关系如何不同于具体物，仍可以用非空间性来划这条线。

en: #### 3.5.3 The Causal Inefficacy Criterion
zh: #### 3.5.3 因果无效性判准

en: According to the most widely accepted versions of the *way of negation*:
zh: 按 ** 否定之路 ** 最广为接受的版本：

en: An object is abstract (if and) only if it is causally inefficacious.
zh: 一个对象是抽象的，当且仅当它在因果上无效力。

en: Concrete objects, whether mental or physical, have causal powers; numbers and functions and the rest make nothing happen. There is no such thing as causal commerce with the game of chess itself (as distinct from its concrete instances). And even if impure sets do in some sense exist in space, it is easy enough to believe that they make no *distinctive* causal contribution to what transpires. Peter and Paul may have effects individually. They may even have effects together that neither has on his own. But these joint effects are naturally construed as effects of two concrete objects acting jointly, or perhaps as effects of their mereological aggregate (itself usually regarded as concretum), rather than as effects of some set-theoretic construction. Suppose Peter and Paul together tip a balance. If we entertain the possibility that this event is caused by a set, we shall have to ask which set caused it: the set containing just Peter and Paul? Some more elaborate construction based on them? Or is it perhaps the set containing the molecules that compose Peter and Paul? This proliferation of possible answers suggests that it was a mistake to credit sets with causal powers in the first place. This is good news for those who wish to say that all sets are abstract.
zh: 具体对象——无论心理的还是物理的——拥有因果力；数、函数以及其余诸物不使任何事发生。与国际象棋这项游戏本身（区别于其具体实例）不存在因果往来。即使非纯集合在某种意义上存在于空间中，也容易相信它们对发生之事没有做出任何 ** 独特的 ** 因果贡献。彼得与保罗可以各自有效果；他们甚至可以有两人独自都没有的共同效果。但这些共同效果自然应被理解为两个具体对象共同作用的效果，或其部分学聚合体（其本身通常被视为具体物）的效果，而不是某个集合论构造的效果。设想彼得与保罗一起压下天平。如果我们考虑这一事件由一个集合引起的可能性，我们将不得不问：是哪个集合引起的？只含彼得与保罗的那个集合？某个基于他们的更精致构造？还是由构成彼得与保罗的分子组成的集合？这种可能答案的增殖表明：起初把因果力归于集合就是个错误。这对想主张一切集合皆抽象的人是个好消息。

en: (Note, however, that some writers identify ordinary physical events—causally efficacious items par excellence—with sets. For David Lewis, for example, an event like the fall of Rome is an ordered pair whose first member is a region of spacetime, and whose second member is a set of such regions (Lewis 1986b)[^lewis-1986b]. On this account, it would be disastrous to say both that impure sets are abstract objects, and that abstract objects are non-causal.)
zh: （然而要注意，一些作者把寻常物理事件—— *par excellence* 的因果有效项——等同于集合。例如对大卫·刘易斯而言，罗马陷落这样的事件是一个有序对，其第一成员是一个时空区域，第二成员是一组这样的区域（Lewis 1986b）[^lewis-1986b]。按这种说明，既说非纯集合是抽象对象、又说抽象对象是非因果的，将是灾难性的。）

en: The biggest challenge to characterizing abstracta as causally inefficacious entities is that *causality* itself is a notoriously problematic and difficult to define idea. It is undoubtedly one of the most controversial notions in the history of thought, with all kinds of views having been put forward on the matter. Thus, *causally efficacious* inherits any unclarity that attaches to *causality*. So, if we are to move the discussion forward, we need to take the notion of causation—understood as a relation among events—as sufficiently clear, even though in fact it is not. Having acknowledged this no doubt naïve assumption, several difficulties arise for the suggestion that abstract objects are precisely the causally inefficacious objects.
zh: 把抽象物刻画为因果上无效力的实体所面临的最大挑战在于：** 因果性 ** 本身是一个出了名的成问题、难以定义的观念。它无疑是思想史上最有争议的概念之一，各种观点层出不穷。于是，“因果上无效力”继承了附着于“因果性”的一切不明。所以，若要推进讨论，我们需要把因果概念——理解为事件之间的关系——当作足够清楚的，尽管实际上并非如此。在承认这个无疑天真的假定之后，“抽象对象恰恰就是因果上无效力的对象”这一提议便浮现出若干困难。

en: The idea that causal inefficacy constitutes a *sufficient* condition for abstractness is somewhat at odds with standard usage. Some philosophers believe in ‘epiphenomenal qualia’: objects of conscious awareness (sense data), or qualitative conscious states that may be caused by physical processes in the brain, but which have no downstream causal consequences of their own (Jackson 1982; Chalmers 1996)[^chalmers-1996][^jackson-1982]. These items are causally inefficacious if they exist, but they are not normally regarded as abstract. The proponent of the causal inefficacy criterion might respond by insisting that abstract objects are distinctively neither causes *nor effects*. But this is perilous. Abstract artifacts like Jane Austen’s novels (as we normally conceive them) come into being *as a result* of human activity. The same goes for impure sets, which come into being when their concrete urelements are created. These items are clearly *effects* in some good sense; yet they remain abstract if they exist at all. It is unclear how the proponent of the strong version of the causal inefficacy criterion (which views causal inefficacy as both necessary and sufficient for abstractness) might best respond to this problem.
zh: “因果无效力构成抽象性的 ** 充分 ** 条件”这一想法与标准用法有些不合。一些哲学家相信“副现象感受质”（epiphenomenal qualia）：意识觉知的对象（感觉材料），或可以被大脑中的物理过程引起、却自身没有下游因果后果的定性意识状态（Jackson 1982; Chalmers 1996）[^chalmers-1996][^jackson-1982]。这些项目如果存在，是因果上无效力的，但通常不被视为抽象的。因果无效性判准的拥护者可以回应说：抽象对象独特地既非原因 ** 也非结果 **。但这是危险的。像简·奥斯汀的小说（按我们通常的构想）这样的抽象人工物，是 ** 作为 ** 人类活动 ** 的结果 ** 而出现的。非纯集合亦然——它们在其具体本元被创造时出现。这些项目在某种好的意义上显然是 ** 结果 **；然而只要它们存在，它们就仍是抽象的。因果无效性判准强版本（视因果无效力为抽象性的既必要又充分条件）的拥护者该如何最好地回应这一问题，并不清楚。

en: Apart from this worry, there are no decisive intuitive counterexamples to this account of the abstract/concrete distinction. The chief difficulty—and it is hardly decisive—is rather conceptual. It is widely maintained that causation, strictly speaking, is a relation among events or states of affairs. If we say that the rock—an object—caused the window to break, what we mean is that some event or state (or fact or condition) *involving* the rock caused the break. If the rock itself is a cause, it is a cause in some derivative sense. But this derivative sense has proved elusive. The rock’s hitting the window is an event in which the rock ‘participates’ in a certain way, and it is because the rock participates in events in this way that we credit the rock itself with causal efficacy. But what is it for an object to *participate* in an event? Suppose John is thinking about the Pythagorean Theorem and you ask him to say what’s on his mind. His response is an event—the utterance of a sentence; and one of its causes is the event of John’s thinking about the theorem. Does the Pythagorean Theorem ‘participate’ in this event? There is surely *some* sense in which it does. The event consists in John’s coming to stand in a certain relation to the theorem, just as the rock’s hitting the window consists in the rock’s coming to stand in a certain relation to the glass. But we do not credit the Pythagorean Theorem with causal efficacy simply because it participates in this sense in an event which is a cause.
zh: 除这一担忧外，这一抽象/具体之分说明没有决定性的直观反例。主要的困难——它也谈不上是决定性的——倒是概念性的。人们普遍认为，严格说来，因果是事件或事态之间的关系。如果我们说岩石——一个对象——造成了窗户破碎，我们的意思是：** 涉及 ** 岩石的某个事件或状态（或事实或条件）造成了破碎。如果岩石本身是一个原因，它是在某种派生的意义上是原因。但这种派生意义一直难以捉摸。岩石击中窗户是一个事件，岩石以某种方式“参与”其中；正是因为岩石以这种方式参与事件，我们才把因果效力归于岩石本身。但一个对象 ** 参与 ** 一个事件是怎么回事？设想约翰正在思考毕达哥拉斯定理，你请他说出他在想什么。他的回应是一个事件——一句话的发出；其原因之一是约翰思考该定理的事件。毕达哥拉斯定理“参与”了这一事件吗？它确实 ** 在某种 ** 意义上参与了。该事件在于约翰开始与该定理处于某种关系，正如岩石击中窗户在于岩石开始与玻璃处于某种关系。但我们并不因为毕达哥拉斯定理在这一意义上参与了一个作为原因的事件，就把它算作因果上有效力的。

en: The challenge is therefore to characterize the distinctive manner of ‘participation in the causal order’ that distinguishes the concrete entities. This problem has received relatively little attention. There is no reason to believe that it cannot be solved, though the varieties of philosophical analysis for the notion of *causality* make the task full of pitfalls. Anyway, in the absence of a solution, this standard version of the *way of negation* must be reckoned a work in progress.
zh: 因此，挑战在于刻画那种把具体实体区分出来的“参与因果秩序”的独特方式。这个问题相对少受关注。没有理由相信它不可解决，尽管 ** 因果性 ** 概念的诸种哲学分析使这项任务充满陷阱。无论如何，在缺乏解决方案的情况下，** 否定之路 ** 的这一标准版本必须被视为一项未竟之作。

en: #### 3.5.4 The Discernibility / Non-Duplication Criteria
zh: #### 3.5.4 可辨别性/不可复制性判准

en: Some philosophers have supposed that, under certain conditions, there are numerically different but indiscernible concrete entities, i.e., that there are distinct concrete objects $x$ and $y$ that exemplify the same properties. If this can be sustained, then one might suggest that distinct abstract objects are always discernible or, in a weaker formulation, that distinct abstract objects are never duplicates.
zh: 一些哲学家曾设想：在某些条件下，存在数值上不同却不可辨别（indiscernible）的具体实体，即存在例示同样性质的不同具体对象 $x$ 与 $y$。如果这一点可以成立，那么可以提出：不同的抽象对象总是可辨别的，或者以较弱的表述：不同的抽象对象绝不互为复本。

en: Cowling (2017, 86–89) analyzes whether the abstract/concrete distinction thus rendered is fruitful, though criteria in this line are normally offered as glosses on the universal/particular distinction. As part of his analysis, he deploys two pairs of (not uncontroversial) distinctions: (i) between qualitative and non-qualitative properties, and (ii) between intrinsic and extrinsic properties. Roughly, a non-qualitative property is one that involves specific individuals (e.g., *being the teacher of Alexander the Great*, *being Albert Einstein*, etc.), while qualitative properties are not (e.g., *having mass*, *having a shape*, *having a length*, etc.). Intrinsic properties are those an object has regardless of what other objects are like and regardless of its relationships with other objects (e.g., *being made of copper*). By contrast, an object’s extrinsic properties are those that depend on other entities (e.g., *being the fastest car*).[^note-9]
zh: Cowling（2017, 86–89）分析了如此呈现的抽象/具体之分是否有成果，尽管这一路线的判准通常被当作对共相/殊相之分的注解来提供。作为其分析的一部分，他动用了两对（并非无可争议的）区分：(i) 定性与非定性性质之分；(ii) 内在性质与外在性质之分。粗略地说，非定性性质是涉及特定个体的性质（如“是亚历山大大帝的老师”“是阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦”等），而定性的性质则不然（如“有质量”“有形状”“有长度”等）。内在性质是一个对象不管其他对象如何、也不管它与其他对象的关系如何都拥有的性质（如“由铜制成”）。相比之下，对象的外在性质是依赖于其他实体的性质（如“是最快的汽车”）。[^note-9]

en: With these distinctions in mind, it seems impossible that there be distinct abstract entities which are qualitatively indiscernible; each abstract entity is expected to have a unique, distinctive qualitative intrinsic nature (or property), which is giving reason for its metaphysical being. This wouldn’t be the case for any concrete entity given the initial assumption in this section. Therefore, the following criterion of discernability could be pondered:
zh: 带着这些区分，似乎不可能存在定性上不可辨别的不同抽象实体；每个抽象实体都应当拥有一个唯一的、独特的定性内在本性（或性质），它为其形而上学存在给出理由。而鉴于本节开头的假定，这对任何具体实体都不成立。因此，可以斟酌如下可辨别性判准：

en: $x$ is an abstract object iff it is impossible for there to be an object which is qualitatively indiscernible from $x$ but distinct from $x$.
zh: $x$ 是一个抽象对象，当且仅当：不可能存在一个在定性上与 $x$ 不可辨别、却不同于 $x$ 的对象。

en: However, one can develop a counterexample to the above proposal, by considering two concrete objects that are indiscernible with respect to their intrinsic qualitative properties. Cowling (2017) considers the case of a possible world with only two perfectly spherical balls, $A$ and $B$, that share the same intrinsic qualitative properties and that are floating at a certain distance from each other. So $A$ and $B$ are distinct concrete objects but indiscernible in terms of their intrinsic qualitative properties.[^note-10] But Lewis has pointed out that “if two individuals are indiscernible then so are their unit sets” (1986a, 84). If this is correct, $\{A\}$ and $\{B\}$ would be indiscernible, but (at least for some philosophers) distinct abstract objects, contrary to the discernibility criterion.[^note-11] It is possible to counter-argue that we could happily accept impure sets as concrete; after all, it was always a bit unclear how they should be classified. Obviously, this has the problematic consequence of having some sets—pure sets—as abstract and other sets—impure sets—as concrete. But the idea that abstract objects have distinctive intrinsic natures allows one to establish a criterion less strong than that of discernibility; if an entity has a distinctive intrinsic nature, it cannot have a duplicate. So, the next criterion of non-duplication can be put forward:
zh: 然而，可以构造一个针对上述提案的反例：考虑两个在其内在定性性质上不可辨别的具体对象。Cowling（2017）考虑了一个只有两个完全球体 $A$ 与 $B$ 的可能世界，它们共享同样的内在定性性质，并彼此悬浮一定距离。于是 $A$ 与 $B$ 是不同的具体对象，但在内在定性性质上不可辨别。[^note-10] 但刘易斯指出：“如果两个个体不可辨别，那么它们的单元集也不可辨别”（1986a, 84）。如果这是对的，$\{A\}$ 与 $\{B\}$ 将不可辨别，但（至少对一些哲学家而言）是不同的抽象对象——与可辨别性判准相悖。[^note-11] 可以反过来论证：我们完全可以接受非纯集合为具体的；毕竟它们的归类一直有些含糊。显然，这有一个成问题的后果：一些集合——纯集合——是抽象的，另一些集合——非纯集合——却是具体的。但“抽象对象拥有独特的内在本性”这一想法，使人得以确立一个弱于可辨别性的判准：如果一个实体有独特的内在本性，它就不能有复本。于是，可以提出如下的不可复制性判准：

en: $x$ is an abstract object iff it is impossible for there to be an object which is a duplicate of $x$ but distinct from $x$.
zh: $x$ 是一个抽象对象，当且仅当：不可能存在一个是 $x$ 的复本、却不同于 $x$ 的对象。

en: But there is a more serious counterexample to this criterion, namely, immanent universals. These are purportedly concrete objects, for they are universals wholly present where their instances are. But this criterion renders them abstract. Take the color scarlet; it is a universal wholly present in every scarlet thing. Each of the scarlets in those things is an immanent universal. These are non-duplicable, but at least according to Armstrong (1978, I, 77, though see 1989, 98–99), they are paradigmatically concrete: spatiotemporally located, causally efficacious, etc. Despite how promising they initially seemed, the criteria of discernibility and non-duplicability do not appear to capture the abstract/concrete distinction.
zh: 但存在一个针对这一判准的更严重的反例，即内在共相。它们据称是具体的对象，因为它们完全存在于其实例所在之处的共相。但这一判准把它们划为抽象的。拿猩红色来说：它是一个完全存在于每件猩红之物中的共相。那些东西中的每一处猩红都是一个内在共相。它们不可复制，但至少按 Armstrong（1978, I, 77；另见 1989, 98–99）的看法，它们是典型的具体物：位于时空中、因果上有效力，等等。尽管起初颇有希望，可辨别性与不可复制性判准似乎都未能抓住抽象/具体之分。

en: 3.6 The Way of Encoding
zh: 3.6 编码之路

en: One of the most rigorous proposals about abstract objects has been developed by Zalta (1983, 1988, and in a series of papers). It is a formal, axiomatic metaphysical theory of objects (both abstract and concrete), and also includes a theory of properties, relations, and propositions. The theory explicitly defines the notion of an *abstract object* but also implicitly characterizes them using axioms.[^note-12] There are three central aspects to the theory: (i) a predicate $E!$ which applies to concrete entities and which is used to define a modal distinction between *abstract* and *ordinary* objects; (ii) a distinction between *exemplifying* relations and *encoding* properties (i.e., encoding 1-place relations); and (iii) a comprehension schema that asserts the conditions under which abstract objects exist.
zh: 关于抽象对象最严格的提案之一由 Zalta（1983, 1988 及一系列论文）发展。它是一个关于对象（抽象与具体）的形式化、公理化的形而上学理论，还包含性质、关系与命题的理论。该理论显式定义了 ** 抽象对象 ** 的概念，但也借助公理隐式地刻画它们。[^note-12] 理论有三个核心方面：(i) 一个适用于具体实体的谓词 $E!$，用于界定 ** 抽象 ** 对象与 ** 普通 ** 对象之间的模态区分；(ii) ** 例示 ** （exemplifying）关系与 ** 编码 ** （encoding）性质（即编码一元关系）之分；(iii) 一个断言抽象对象存在条件的概括图式。

en: (i) Since the theory has both a quantifier $\exists$ and a predicate $E!$, Zalta offers two interpretations of his theory (1983, 51–2; 1988, 103–4). On one interpretation, the quantifier $\exists$ simply asserts *there is* and the predicate $E!$ asserts *existence*. On this interpretation, a formula such as $\exists x \neg E!x$, which is implied by the axioms described below, asserts “there is an object that fails to exist”. So, on this interpretation, the theory is Meinongian because it endorses non-existent objects. But there is a Quinean interpretation as well, on which the quantifier $\exists$ asserts *existence* and the predicate $E!$ asserts *concreteness*. On this interpretation, the formula $\exists x \neg E!x$ asserts “there exists an object that fails to be concrete”. So, on this interpretation, the theory is Platonist, since it doesn’t endorse non-existents but rather asserts the existence of non-concrete objects. We’ll henceforth use the Quinean/Platonist interpretation.
zh: (i) 由于该理论既有一个量词 $\exists$ 又有一个谓词 $E!$，Zalta 给出其理论的两种解读（1983, 51–2; 1988, 103–4）。按一种解读，量词 $\exists$ 仅断言 ** 有 **，而谓词 $E!$ 断言 ** 存在 **。在这种解读下，$\exists x \neg E!x$ 这样一个由下文公理蕴含的公式断言“有一个不存在的对象”。于是，按这种解读，理论是迈农式的，因为它承认非存在对象。但也有一种奎因式的解读：量词 $\exists$ 断言 ** 存在 **，而谓词 $E!$ 断言 ** 具体性 **。在这种解读下，公式 $\exists x \neg E!x$ 断言“存在一个不具体的对象”。于是，按这种解读，理论是柏拉图主义的，因为它不承认非存在者，而是断言非具体对象的存在。下文我们采用奎因式/柏拉图主义的解读。

en: In the more expressive, modal version of his theory, Zalta defines *ordinary* objects $(O!)$ to be those that might be concrete. The reason is that Zalta holds that possible objects (i.e., like million-carat diamonds, talking donkeys, etc.) are not concrete but rather possibly concrete. They exist, but they are not abstract, since abstract objects, like the number one, couldn’t be concrete. Indeed, Zalta’s theory implies that abstract objects $(A!)$ aren’t possibly concrete, since he defines them to be objects that aren’t ordinary (1993, 404):
zh: 在其更具表达力的模态版本中，Zalta 把 ** 普通 ** 对象（$O!$）定义为可能是具体的东西。理由是：Zalta 认为可能对象（如百万克拉的钻石、会说话的驴子等）不是具体的，而只是可能具体。它们存在，但不是抽象的，因为像数一这样的抽象对象不可能是具体的。的确，Zalta 的理论蕴含：抽象对象（$A!$）不可能具体，因为他把它们定义为非普通的对象（1993, 404）：

en: $$\begin{align} O!x &=_\mathit{df} \Diamond E!x \\ A!x &=_\mathit{df} \neg O!x \end{align}$$
zh: $$\begin{align} O!x &=_\mathit{df} \Diamond E!x \\ A!x &=_\mathit{df} \neg O!x \end{align}$$

en: Thus, the ordinary objects include all the concrete objects (since $E!x$ implies $\Diamond E!x$), as well as possible objects that aren’t in fact concrete but might have been. On this theory, therefore, *being abstract* is not the negation of *being concrete*. Instead, the definition validates an intuition that numbers, sets, etc., aren’t the kind of thing that could be concrete. Though Zalta’s definition of *abstract* seems to comport with the *way of primitivism*—take *concrete* as primitive, and then define *abstract* as *not possibly concrete*—it differs in that (a) axioms are stated that govern the conditions under which abstract objects exist (see below), and (b) the features commonly ascribed to abstract objects are *derived* from principles that govern the property of being concrete. For example, Zalta accepts principles such as: necessarily, anything with causal powers is concrete (i.e., $\Box \forall x(Cx \to E!x)$). Then since abstract objects are, by definition, concrete at no possible world, they necessarily fail to have causal powers.
zh: 于是，普通对象包括所有具体对象（因为 $E!x$ 蕴含 $\Diamond E!x$），也包括事实上不具体但可能具体的可能对象。因此在这一理论中，** 是抽象的 ** 并非 ** 是具体的 ** 之否定。相反，这个定义印证了这样一种直觉：数、集合等不是那种可能具体的东西。虽然 Zalta 的 ** 抽象 ** 定义似乎与 ** 素朴主义之路 ** 相合——取 ** 具体 ** 为素朴，再把 ** 抽象 ** 定义为 ** 不可能具体 **——但不同的是：(a) 该理论陈述了支配抽象对象存在条件的公理（见下文），(b) 常归于抽象对象的那些特征是从支配“具体性”这一性质的原则 ** 推导 ** 出来的。例如，Zalta 接受这样的原则：必然地，任何拥有因果力的东西都是具体的（即 $\Box \forall x(Cx \to E!x)$）。于是，既然抽象对象按定义在任何可能世界都不具体，它们就必然没有因果力。

en: (ii) The distinction between *exemplifying* and *encoding* is a primitive one and is represented in the theory by two atomic formulas: $F^nx_1\ldots x_n$ $(x_1,\ldots ,x_n$ *exemplify* $F^n$) and $xF^1$ $(x$ *encodes* $F^1).$ While both ordinary and abstract objects exemplify properties, only abstract objects encode properties;[^note-13] it is axiomatic that ordinary objects necessarily fail to encode properties $(O!x \to \Box \neg \exists FxF).$ Zalta’s proposal can be seen a positive metaphysical proposal distinct from all the others we have considered; a positive proposal that uses encoding as a key notion to characterize abstract objects. On this reading, the definitions and axioms of the theory convey what is meant by *encoding* and how it works. Intuitively, an abstract object *encodes* the properties by which we define or conceive of it, but exemplifies some properties contingently and others necessarily. Thus, the number 1 of Dedekind-Peano number theory encodes all and only its number-theoretic properties, and whereas it contingently exemplifies the property *being thought about by Peano*, it necessarily exemplifies properties such as *being abstract*, *not having a shape*, *not being a building*, etc. The distinction between exemplifying and encoding a property is also used to define identity: ordinary objects are identical whenever they necessarily exemplify the same properties while abstract objects are identical whenever they necessarily encode the same properties.
zh: (ii) ** 例示 ** 与 ** 编码 ** 之分是素朴的，在理论中由两个原子公式表示：$F^nx_1\ldots x_n$（$​x_1,\ldots ,x_n$ ** 例示 ** $F^n$）与 $xF^1$（$​x$ ** 编码 ** $F^1$）。普通对象与抽象对象都例示性质，但只有抽象对象编码性质；[^note-13] 以下是公理：普通对象必然不编码性质（$O!x \to \Box \neg \exists FxF$）。Zalta 的提案可以看作一个有别于我们迄今考察的所有提案的正面形而上学提案：一个以编码为关键概念来刻画抽象对象的正面提案。按这一读法，理论的定义与公理传达了 ** 编码 ** 的含义及其运作方式。直观地说，一个抽象对象 ** 编码 ** 我们借以定义或构想它的那些性质，但偶然地例示一些性质、必然地例示另一些性质。于是，戴德金-皮亚诺数论中的数一编码且仅编码其数论性质；它偶然地例示“被皮亚诺思考”这一性质，却必然地例示“是抽象的”“没有形状”“不是建筑物”等性质。例示性质与编码性质之分也被用来定义同一性：普通对象同一，当且仅当它们必然例示相同的性质；抽象对象同一，当且仅当它们必然编码相同的性质。

en: (iii) The comprehension principle asserts that for each expressible condition on properties, there is an abstract object that *encodes* exactly the properties that fulfill (satisfy) that condition. Formally: $\exists x(A!x \:\&\: \forall F(xF \equiv \phi))$, where $\phi$ has no free $x$s. Each instance of this schema asserts the existence of an abstract object of a certain sort. So, for example, where ‘$s$’ denotes Socrates, the instance $\exists x(A!x \:\&\: \forall F(xF \equiv Fs))$ asserts that there is an abstract object that encodes exactly the properties that Socrates exemplifies. Zalta uses this object to analyze the complete individual concept of Socrates. But any condition $\phi$ on conditions on properties with no free occurrences of $x$ can be used to form an instance of comprehension. In fact, one can prove that the object asserted to exist is unique, since there can’t be two distinct abstract objects that encode exactly the properties satisfying $\phi$.
zh: (iii) 概括原则断言：对每个可表达的关于性质的条件，都存在一个恰好 ** 编码 ** 满足（符合）该条件的那些性质的抽象对象。形式化地：$\exists x(A!x \:\&\: \forall F(xF \equiv \phi))$，其中 $\phi$ 无自由 $x$。这一图式的每个实例都断言某类抽象对象的存在。例如，设“$s$”指称苏格拉底，实例 $\exists x(A!x \:\&\: \forall F(xF \equiv Fs))$ 断言：存在一个恰好编码苏格拉底所例示之性质的抽象对象。Zalta 用这个对象来分析苏格拉底的完全个体概念。但任何关于性质之条件且无 $x$ 自由出现的条件 $\phi$，都可以用来构成概括的一个实例。事实上，可以证明被断言存在的对象是唯一的，因为不可能有两个不同的抽象对象恰好编码满足 $\phi$ 的那些性质。

en: The theory that emerges from (i)–(iii) is further developed with additional axioms and definitions. One axiom asserts that if an object encodes a property, it does so necessarily $(xF \to \Box xF).$ So the properties that an object encodes are not relative to any circumstance. Moreover, Zalta supplements his theory of abstract objects with a theory of properties, relations, and propositions. Here we describe only the theory of properties. It is governed by two principles: a comprehension principle for properties and a principle of identity. The comprehension principle asserts that for any condition on objects expressible without encoding subformulas, there is a property $F$ such that necessarily, an object $x$ exemplifies $F$ if and only if $x$ is such that $\phi$, i.e., $\exists F\Box \forall x(Fx \equiv \phi)$, where $\phi$ has no encoding subformulas and no free $F\text{s}$. The identity principle asserts that properties $F$ and $G$ are identical just in case $F$ and $G$ are necessarily encoded by the same objects, i.e., $F\! =\! G =_\mathit{df} \Box \forall x(xF \equiv xG)$. This principle allows one to assert that there are properties that are necessarily equivalent in the classical sense, i.e., in the sense that $\Box \forall x(Fx \equiv Gx)$, but which are distinct.[^note-14]
zh: 由 (i)–(iii) 产生的理论还借助额外的公理与定义得到发展。一条公理断言：如果一个对象编码一个性质，它是必然地如此编码（$xF \to \Box xF$）。所以，一个对象所编码的性质不相对于任何境况。此外，Zalta 为其抽象对象理论补充了性质、关系与命题的理论。这里只描述性质的理论。它由两条原则支配：性质的概括原则与同一性原则。概括原则断言：对任何可以不用编码子公式表达的对象条件，存在一个性质 $F$，使得必然地，对象 $x$ 例示 $F$ 当且仅当 $x$ 满足 $\phi$，即 $\exists F\Box \forall x(Fx \equiv \phi)$，其中 $\phi$ 无编码子公式且无自由 $F\text{s}$。同一性原则断言：性质 $F$ 与 $G$ 同一，当且仅当 $F$ 与 $G$ 被同样的对象必然地编码，即 $F\! =\! G =_\mathit{df} \Box \forall x(xF \equiv xG)$。这一原则使人可以断言：存在一些性质，它们在经典意义上——即在 $\Box \forall x(Fx \equiv Gx)$ 的意义上——必然等值，却彼此不同。[^note-14]

en: Since $\alpha\! =\! \beta$ is defined both when $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are both individual variables or both property variables, Zalta employs the usual principle for the substitution of identicals. Since all of the terms in his system are rigid, substitution of identicals preserves truth even in modal contexts.
zh: 由于 $\alpha\! =\! \beta$ 在 $\alpha$ 与 $\beta$ 同为个体变项或同为性质变项时都有定义，Zalta 采用通常的同一者替换原则。由于其系统中所有词项都是刚性的，同一者替换在模态语境中也保真。

en: The foregoing principles implicitly characterize both abstract and ordinary objects. Zalta’s theory doesn’t postulate any concrete objects, though, since that is a contingent matter. But his system does include the Barcan formula (i.e., $\Diamond \exists xFx \to \exists x\Diamond Fx$), and so possibility claims like “there might have been talking donkeys” imply that there are (non-concrete) objects at our world that are talking donkeys at some possible world. Since Zalta adopts the view that ordinary properties like being a donkey necessarily imply concreteness, such *contingently nonconcrete* objects are ordinary.
zh: 上述诸原则隐式地刻画了抽象对象与普通对象两者。不过，Zalta 的理论并不设定任何具体对象，因为那是偶然之事。但他的系统确实包含巴坎公式（即 $\Diamond \exists xFx \to \exists x\Diamond Fx$），因此“本可能有会说话的驴子”这类可能性主张蕴含：在我们的世界存在一些（非具体的）对象，它们在某个可能世界是会说话的驴子。由于 Zalta 采纳“像“是驴子”这样的普通性质必然蕴含具体性”的看法，这类 ** 偶然不具体 ** 的对象是普通的。

en: Zalta uses his theory to analyze Plato’s Forms, concepts, possible worlds, Fregean numbers and Fregean senses, fictions, and mathematical objects and relations generally. However, some philosophers see his comprehension principle as too inclusive, for in addition to these objects, it asserts that there are entities like *the round square* or *the set of all sets which are not members of themselves*. The theory doesn’t assert that anything *exemplifies* being round and being square—the theory preserves the classical form of predication without giving rise to contradictions. But it does assert that there is an abstract object that encodes being round and being square, and that there is an abstract object that encodes the property of being a set that contains all and only non-self-membered sets. Zalta would respond by suggesting that such objects are needed not only to state truth conditions, and explain the logical consequences, of sentences involving expressions like “the round square” and “the Russell set”, but also to analyze the fictional characters of inconsistent stories and inconsistent theories (e.g., Fregean extensions).
zh: Zalta 用他的理论分析柏拉图的形式、概念、可能世界、弗雷格式的数与弗雷格式涵义、虚构物，以及一般的数学对象与关系。然而，一些哲学家认为他的概括原则过于宽泛：因为除这些对象外，它还断言存在像 ** 圆的方 ** 或 ** 所有不属于自己的集合的集合 ** 这样的实体。该理论并不断言有任何东西 ** 例示 ** 着是圆的与是方的——理论保持了经典谓述的形式而不产生矛盾。但它确实断言：存在一个编码“是圆的”与“是方的”的抽象对象，也存在一个编码“是一个包含且仅包含非自属成员的集合”这一性质的抽象对象。Zalta 会回应说：这类对象不仅是陈述诸如“圆的方”“罗素集”之类表达式的句子的真值条件、解释其逻辑后果所必需的，也是分析不一致故事与不一致理论（如弗雷格式外延）的虚构角色所必需的。

en: It should be noted that Zalta’s comprehension principle for abstract objects is unrestricted and so constitutes a *plenitude* principle. This allows the theory to provide objects for arbitrary mathematical theories. Where $\tau$ is a term of mathematical theory $T$, the comprehension principle yields a unique object that encodes all and only the properties $F$ that are attributed to $\tau$ in $T$ (Linsky & Zalta 1995, Nodelman & Zalta 2014)[^linsky-1995][^nodelman-2014].[^note-15] Zalta’s theory therefore offers significant explanatory power, for it has multiple applications and advances solutions to a wide range of puzzles in different fields of philosophy.[^note-16]
zh: 应当注意：Zalta 的抽象对象概括原则是不受限制的，因而构成一个 ** 充盈 ** 原则。这使理论可以为任意的数学理论提供对象。设 $\tau$ 是数学理论 $T$ 的一个词项，概括原则产生一个唯一的对象，它编码且仅编码在 $T$ 中被归于 $\tau$ 的那些性质 $F$（Linsky & Zalta 1995, Nodelman & Zalta 2014）[^linsky-1995][^nodelman-2014]。[^note-15] 因此，Zalta 的理论提供了可观的说服力：它有多种应用，并为不同哲学领域的一系列难题提供了方案。[^note-16]

en: 3.7 The Ways of Weakening Existence
zh: 3.7 弱化存在之路

en: Many philosophers have supposed that abstract objects exist in some thin, deflated sense. In this section we consider the idea that the abstract/concrete distinction might be *defined* by saying that abstract objects exist in some less robust sense than the sense in which concrete objects exist.
zh: 许多哲学家设想抽象对象以某种薄的、紧缩的意义存在。本节考虑这样一种想法：抽象/具体之分可以这样来 ** 定义 **——抽象对象以一种不如具体对象之存在那么强健的意义存在。

en: The traditional platonist conception is a realist one: abstract objects exist in just the same full-blooded sense that objects in the natural world exist—they are mind-independent, rather than artifacts of human endeavor or dependent on concrete objects in any way. But a number of deflationary, metaontological views, now established in the literature, are based on the idea that the problems traditional platonists face have to do with “some very general preconceptions about what it takes to specify an object” rather than with “the abstractness of the desired object” (Linnebo 2018, 42)[^linnebo-2018]. These views suggest that abstract objects exist in some weaker sense. Various approaches therefore articulate what may be called the ways of weakening existence. One clear precedent is due to Carnap 1950 [1956], whose deflationary approach may go the furthest; Carnap rejects the metaphysical pursuit of what “really exists” (even in the case of concrete objects) since he maintains that the question “Do $X\text{s}$ really exist?” are pseudo-questions (if asked independently of some linguistic framework).
zh: 传统的柏拉图主义构想是一种实在论构想：抽象对象以与自然世界中的对象完全同样十足的意义存在——它们独立于心灵，而非人类努力的产物，也不以任何方式依赖于具体对象。但文献中已确立的许多紧缩的、元存在论的观点，其根据是这样一个想法：传统柏拉图主义者面临的困难与“关于如何指定一个对象的某些非常一般的前见”有关，而与“所欲对象的抽象性”无关（Linnebo 2018, 42）[^linnebo-2018]。这些观点提出，抽象对象以某种较弱的意义存在。因此，各种进路阐明了可称为弱化存在之路的东西。一个明确的先例来自 Carnap 1950 [1956]，其紧缩进路也许走得最远：卡尔纳普拒斥对“什么真正存在”的形而上学追求（即使在具体对象的情形下），因为他主张“X 真的存在吗？”这类问题是假问题（若独立于某个语言框架被提出）。

en: But there are other ways to suggest that abstract objects have existence conditions that demand little of the world. For example, Linsky & Zalta (1995, 532) argued that the mind-independence and objectivity of abstract objects isn’t like that of physical objects: abstract objects aren’t subject to an appearance/reality distinction, they don’t exist in a ‘sparse’ way that requires discovery by empirical investigation, and they aren’t complete objects (e.g., mathematical objects are defined only by their mathematical properties). They use this conception to *naturalize* Zalta’s comprehension principle for abstract objects.
zh: 但还有其他方式可以表明：抽象对象的存在条件对世界所求甚少。例如，Linsky 与 Zalta（1995, 532）论证：抽象对象的独立于心灵与客观性不同于物理对象的：抽象对象不受表象/实在之分的约束，它们不以需要经验研究来发现的“稀疏”方式存在，它们不是完全的对象（例如，数学对象仅由其数学性质定义）。他们用这一构想 ** 自然化 ** Zalta 的抽象对象概括原则。

en: Other deflationary accounts develop some weaker sense in which abstract objects exist (e.g., as ‘thin’ objects). We further describe some of these proposals below and try to unpack the ways in which they characterize the weakened, deflationary sense of existence (even when such characterizations are not always explicit).
zh: 其他紧缩说明发展出抽象对象存在的某种较弱意义（如作为“薄”对象）。下文进一步描述其中一些提案，并尝试解析它们刻画这种弱化的、紧缩的存在意义的方式（即使这类刻画并不总是显式的）。

en: #### 3.7.1 The Criterion of Linguistic Rules
zh: #### 3.7.1 语言规则判准

en: Carnap held that claims about the “real” existence of entities (concrete or abstract) do not have cognitive content. They are pseudo-statements. However, he admitted: (a) that there are sentences in science that use terms that designate mathematical entities (such as numbers); and (b) that semantic analysis seems to require entities like properties and propositions. Since mathematical entities, properties, and propositions are traditionally considered abstract, he wanted to clarify how it is possible to accept a language referring to abstract entities without adopting what he considered pseudo-sentences about such entities’ objective reality. Carnap’s famous paper (1950 [1956]) contained an attempt to show that, without embracing Platonism, one can use a language referring to abstract entities.
zh: 卡尔纳普主张：关于实体（具体或抽象）之“实在”存在的断言没有认知内容。它们是假陈述。但他承认：(a) 科学中有使用指称数学实体（如数）的词项的句子；(b) 语义分析似乎需要性质与命题之类的实体。既然数学实体、性质与命题传统上被视为抽象的，他想澄清：怎么可能接受一种指称抽象实体的语言，而不接受他所认为的关于这类实体之客观实在的假陈述。卡尔纳普那篇著名的论文（1950 [1956]）就试图表明：不拥抱柏拉图主义，也可以使用指称抽象实体的语言。

en: To achieve these goals, Carnap begins by noting that before one can ask existence questions about entities of a determinate kind, one first has to have a language, or a *linguistic framework*, that allows one to speak about the kinds of entity in question. He then distinguishes ‘internal’ existence questions expressed within such a linguistic framework from ‘external’ existence questions about a framework. Only the latter ask whether the entities of that framework are objectively real. As we’ll see below, Carnap thought that internal existence questions within a framework can be answered, either by empirical investigation or by logical analysis, depending on the kind of entity the framework is about. By contrast, Carnap regards external questions (e.g., ‘Do $X\text{s}$ exist?’, expressed either about, or independent of, a linguistic framework) as pseudo-questions: though they appear to be theoretical questions, in fact they are merely practical questions about the utility of the linguistic framework for science.
zh: 为实现这些目标，卡尔纳普首先指出：在对某一确定种类的实体提出存在之问之前，首先必须有一种语言，或一个 ** 语言框架 **，使人们能够谈论所论的那类实体。他接着区分：在此类语言框架 ** 之内 ** 表达的“内部”存在之问，与关于框架本身的“外部”存在之问。只有后者才问：该框架的实体是否客观实在。如下文所见，卡尔纳普认为框架内的内部存在之问可以回答——或者靠经验研究，或者靠逻辑分析，取决于框架所关于的实体的种类。相比之下，卡尔纳普把外部问题（如“X 存在吗？”，无论针对框架提出还是独立于框架提出）视为假问题：它们看似理论问题，实际上只是关于语言框架对科学之效用性的实践问题。

en: Carnap’s paper (1950 [1956]) considers a variety of linguistic frameworks, such as those for: observable things (i.e., the spatiotemporally ordered system of observable things and events), natural numbers and integers, propositions, thing properties, rational and real numbers, and spatiotemporal coordinate systems. Each framework is established by developing a language that typically includes expressions for one or more kinds of entities in question, expressions for properties of the entities in question (including a general category term for each kind of entity in question), and variables ranging over those entities. Thus, a framework for the system of observable things has expressions that denote such things (‘the Earth’, ‘the Eiffel Tower’, etc.), expressions for properties of such things (‘planet’, ‘made of metal’, etc.), and variables ranging over observables. The framework for natural numbers has expressions that denote them (‘0’, ‘2+5’), expressions for properties of the numbers (‘prime’, ‘odd’), including the general category term ‘number’), and variables ranging over numbers.
zh: 卡尔纳普的论文（1950 [1956]）考虑了多种语言框架，例如关于：可观察物（即可观察物与事件之时空有序系统）、自然数与整数、命题、事物性质、有理数与实数、以及时空坐标系的框架。每个框架都通过发展一门语言而确立，该语言通常包括：指称所论实体中一种或多种的表达式、表达这些实体之性质的表达式（包括每类所论实体的一般范畴词），以及在这些实体上取值的变项。于是，可观察物系统的框架有指称这类东西的表达式（“地球”“埃菲尔铁塔”等）、表达这类东西之性质的表达式（“行星”“金属制的”等），以及在可观察物上取值的变项。自然数的框架有指称它们的表达式（“0”、“2+5”）、表达数之性质的表达式（“素数”“奇数”），包括一般范畴词“数”，以及在数上取值的变项。

en: For Carnap, each statement in a linguistic framework should have a truth value that can be determined either by analytical or empirical methods. A statement’s truth value is analytically determinable if it is logically true (or false), or if it’s truth is determinable exclusively from the rules of the language or on the basis of semantic relationships among its component expressions. A statement is empirically determinable when it is confirmable (or disconfirmable) in the light of the perceived evidence. Note that the very attempt to confirm an empirical statement about physical objects on the basis of the evidence requires that one adopt the language of the framework of things. Carnap warns us, however, that “this must not be interpreted as if it meant … acceptance of a *belief* in the reality of the thing world; there is no such belief or assertion or assumption because it is not a theoretical question” (1950 [1956, 208]). For Carnap, to accept an ontology “means nothing more than to accept a certain form of language, in other words to accept rules for forming statements and for testing, accepting, or rejecting them” (1950 [1956, 208]).
zh: 对卡尔纳普而言，语言框架中的每个陈述都应有一个真值，且该真值要么可由分析方法、要么可由经验方法确定。一个陈述的真值是分析可定的，如果它在逻辑上为真（或假），或其真值可以完全从语言的规则、或基于其成分表达式之间的语义关系来确定。一个陈述是经验可定的，当它可以在被感知的证据之光下得到确证（或否证）。注意：基于证据确证一个关于物理对象的经验陈述这一尝试本身，就要求人们采纳事物框架的语言。但卡尔纳普提醒我们，“这不得被解读为好像它意味着……接受对事物世界实在性的 ** 信念 **；不存在这样的信念、断言或假定，因为它不是一个理论问题”（1950 [1956, 208]）。对卡尔纳普来说，接受一种存在论“只不过意味着接受某种语言形式，换句话说，接受用于构造陈述以及检验、接受或拒斥陈述的规则”（1950 [1956, 208]）。

en: Carnap takes this approach to every linguistic framework, no matter whether it is a framework about physical, concrete things, or a framework about abstract entities such as numbers, properties, concepts, propositions, etc. For him, the pragmatic reasons for accepting a given linguistic framework are that it has explanatory power, unifies the explanation of disparate kinds of data and phenomena, expresses claims more efficiently, etc. And we often choose a framework for a particular explanatory purpose. We might therefore choose a framework with expressions about abstract entities to carry out an *explication* (i.e., an elucidation of concepts), or to develop a semantics for natural language. For Carnap, the choice between platonism or nominalism is not a legitimate one; both are inappropriate attempts to answer an external pseudo-question.
zh: 卡尔纳普对每一个语言框架都采取这一进路，无论它是关于物理的、具体的东西的框架，还是关于数、性质、概念、命题等抽象实体的框架。对他来说，接受一个给定语言框架的实用性理由在于：它有解释力，统一了对不同种类数据与现象的解释，更高效地表达主张，等等。我们常为某个特定的解释目的选择框架。因此，我们可能会选择一个含抽象实体表达式的框架来做 ** 显明 ** （explication，即概念的阐明），或为自然语言发展语义学。对卡尔纳普来说，在柏拉图主义与唯名论之间做选择不是一个合法的选择：两者都是回答一个外部假问题的不适当尝试。

en: As sketched earlier, the truth of such existence claims as ‘there are tables’ and ‘there are unicorns’, which are expressed within the framework for observable entities, is to be determined empirically, since empirical observations and investigations are needed. These statements are not true in virtue of the rules of the language. By contrast, existence claims such as ‘there are numbers’ (‘$\exists xNx$’) expressed within the framework of number theory, or ‘there is a property $F$ such that both $x$ and $y$ are $F$’ (‘$\exists F(Fx \:\&\: Fy)$’) expressed within the framework of property theory, can be determined analytically. For these statements either form part of the rules of the language (e.g., expressed as axioms that govern the terms of the language) or are derivable from the rules of the language. When these statements are part of the rules that make up the linguistic framework, they are considered *analytic*, as are the existential statements that follow from those rules.[^note-17]
zh: 如前文粗描的，“有桌子”“有独角兽”这类在可观察实体框架 ** 之内 ** 表达的存在主张的真值，要由经验来确定，因为需要经验观察与研究。这些陈述不凭语言规则为真。相比之下，在数论框架内表达的“有数”（“$\exists xNx$”）这类存在主张，或在性质论框架内表达的“有性质 $F$ 使得 $x$ 与 $y$ 都是 $F$”（“$\exists F(Fx \:\&\: Fy)$”），可以分析地确定。因为这些陈述或者构成语言规则的一部分（例如作为支配语言词项的公理表达），或者可从语言规则导出。当这些陈述是构成语言框架的规则的一部分时，它们被视为 ** 分析的 **，从那些规则导出的存在陈述亦然。[^note-17]

en: All of the existence assertions just discussed are therefore *internal* to their respective linguistic frameworks. Carnap thinks that the only sense that can be given to talk of “existence” is an internal sense. Internal questions about the existence of things or abstract objects are not questions about their real metaphysical existence.[^note-18] Hence, it seems more appropriate to describe his view as embodying a deflationary notion of object. For Carnap concludes “the question of the admissibility of entities of a certain type or of abstract entities in general as designata is reduced to the question of the acceptability of the linguistic framework for those entities” (1950 [1956, 217]).
zh: 刚才讨论的所有存在断言因此都是 ** 内部 ** 于其各自的语言框架的。卡尔纳普认为，能赋予“存在”之谈的唯一意义是内部意义。关于事物或抽象对象存在的内部问题，不是关于其实际形而上学存在的问题。[^note-18] 因此，把他的观点描述为体现一种紧缩的对象概念似乎更恰当。因为卡尔纳普的结论是：“某类实体或一般抽象实体作为指称对象的容许性问题，被还原为那些实体的语言框架的可接受性问题”（1950 [1956, 217]）。

en: Thus, for each framework (no matter whether it describes empirical objects, abstract objects, or a mix of both), one can formulate both simple and complex existential statements. According to Carnap, each simple existential statement is either empirical or analytic. If a simple statement is empirical, its truth value can be determined by a combination of empirical inquiry and consideration of the linguistic rules governing the framework; if the simple existential statement is analytic, then its truth value can be determined simply by considering the linguistic rules governing the framework. Whereas the simple existential statements that require empirical investigation assert the existence of possible concrete entities (like ‘tables’ or ‘unicorns’), the simple existential statements that are analytic assert the existence of abstract entities. Let us call this criterion for asserting the existence of abstract objects the *criterion of linguistic rules*.
zh: 于是，对每个框架（无论它描述经验对象、抽象对象还是两者的混合），人们都可以构造简单与复杂的存在陈述。按卡尔纳普的看法，每个简单存在陈述要么是经验的，要么是分析的。如果一个简单陈述是经验的，其真值可以由经验探究与支配框架的语言规则的考量相结合来确定；如果这个简单存在陈述是分析的，其真值可以仅由考虑支配该框架的语言规则来确定。需要经验研究的简单存在陈述断言可能的具体实体（如“桌子”或“独角兽”）的存在，而分析的简单存在陈述断言抽象实体的存在。让我们把这个断言抽象对象存在之判准称为 ** 语言规则判准 **。

en: The case of mixed frameworks poses some difficulties for the view. According to the Criterion of Linguistic Rules,
zh: 混合框架的情形给这一观点带来一些困难。按语言规则判准：

en: $x$ is abstract iff “$x$ exists” is analytic in the relevant language.
zh: $x$ 是抽象的，当且仅当“$x$ 存在”在相关语言中是分析的。

en: But this criterion suggests that *impure* sets, object-dependent properties, abstract artifacts, and the rest are not abstract. For this criterion appears to draw a line between certain pure abstract entities and everything else. The truth of simple existence statements about $\{\textrm{Bob Dylan}\}$ or Dickens’ *A Christmas Carol*, which usually are considered abstract entities, does not depend solely on linguistic rules. The same goes for simple and complex existential statements with general terms such as ‘novel’, ‘legal statute’, etc.
zh: 但这一判准暗示：** 非纯 ** 集合、依赖于对象的性质、抽象人工物等都不是抽象的。因为这一判准似乎在若干纯抽象实体与其余一切之间划线。关于 $\{\textrm{Bob Dylan}\}$ 或狄更斯的《圣诞颂歌》的简单存在陈述——它们通常被视为抽象实体——之真值并不单靠语言规则。对含“小说”“法令”等一般词项的简单与复杂存在陈述亦然。

en: In the end, though, Carnap doesn’t seem to be either a realist or nominalist about objects (abstract or concrete). Carnap rejects the question whether these objects are real in a metaphysical sense. But, contrary to the nominalist, he rejects the idea that we can truly deny the real existence of abstract objects (i.e., a denial that is external to a linguistic framework). This attitude, which settles the question of which framework to adopt on pragmatic grounds (e.g., which framework best helps us to make sense of the data to be explained), is the reason why we’ve labeled his view as a *way of weakening existence*. See the entry on Carnap for further details.
zh: 归根结底，卡尔纳普似乎既不是关于对象（抽象或具体）的实在论者，也不是唯名论者。卡尔纳普拒斥“这些对象在形而上学意义上是否实在”的问题。但与唯名论者相反，他拒绝“我们可以真正否认抽象对象的实在存在（即一种外在于语言框架的否认）”这一观念。这种以实用理由（例如哪个框架最有助于我们理解有待解释的数据）裁定采用哪个框架的态度，就是我们把他的观点称为一种 ** 弱化存在之路 ** 的原因。进一步细节见卡尔纳普词条。

en: Proposals by other philosophers are related to Carnap’s view. Resnik (1997, Part Two) has put forward a *postulational epistemology* for the existence of mathematical objects. According to this view, all one has to do to ensure the existence of mathematical objects is to use a language to posit mathematical objects and to establish a consistent mathematical theory for them.[^note-19] Nevertheless, their existence does not result from their being posited. Instead, we recognize those objects as existent because a consistent mathematical theory for them has been developed. Resnik requires both a linguistic stipulation for considering mathematical objects and a coherency condition for recognizing them as existent. Thomasson (2015, 30–34) advocates for an approach which she takes to be inherited from Carnap. She calls it *easy ontology*. Since she is not trying to find ultimate categories or a definitive list of basic (abstract or concrete) objects, she prefers a simpler kind of realism (see Thomasson 2015, 145–158)[^thomasson-2015]. She argues that everyday uses of existential statements provide acceptable ontological commitments when those assertions are supported either by empirical evidence or merely by the rules of use that govern general terms (e.g., sortal terms); in both cases she says that “application conditions” for a general term are fulfilled (see Thomasson 2015, 86, 89–95)[^thomasson-2015]. She, too, therefore offers a *criterion of linguistic rules* for accepting abstract objects. Given her defense of simple realism, it appears that she takes both observable objects and theoretical entities in science as concrete.
zh: 其他哲学家的提案与卡尔纳普的观点相关。Resnik（1997, 第二部分）为数学对象的存在提出了一个 ** 公设认识论 **。按这种看法，确保数学对象存在所需的一切，就是使用一种语言去公设数学对象，并为它们建立一个一致的数学理论。[^note-19] 尽管如此，它们的存在并非源于它们被公设。毋宁说，我们认它们为存在，是因为一个关于它们的一致的数学理论已被发展出来。雷斯尼克要求：既要有把数学对象纳入考虑的语言设定，也要有把它们认作存在的一致性条件。Thomasson（2015, 30–34）提倡一种她认为承自卡尔纳普的进路，她称之为 ** 轻易存在论 ** （easy ontology）。由于她并不试图找出终极范畴或基本（抽象或具体）对象的确切清单，她偏好一种更简单的实在论（见 Thomasson 2015, 145–158）[^thomasson-2015]。她论证：存在陈述的日常使用提供了可接受的存在论承诺，当那些断言要么得到经验证据的支持、要么仅由支配一般词项（如种类词）的使用规则所支持时；在两种情形下她都说，一般词项的“适用条件”得到了满足（见 Thomasson 2015, 86, 89–95）[^thomasson-2015]。因此她也提供了一个接受抽象对象的 ** 语言规则判准 **。鉴于她对简单实在论的辩护，看来她把科学中的可观察对象与理论实体都视为具体的。

en: #### 3.7.2 The Criterion of Minimalism
zh: #### 3.7.2 极简主义判准

en: In what follows, two ways of formulating criteria for the abstract/concrete distinction are considered. The views start with the idea that our concept of an object allows for objects whose existence places very few demands on reality over and above the demands imposed by claims that do not mention abstract objects. Those philosophers who maintain this philosophical thesis are what Linnebo (2012) calls metaontological *minimalists*. Their proposals are typically put forward in connection with issues in the philosophy of mathematics, but then applied to other domains.
zh: 下文考虑构造抽象/具体之分判准的两种方式。这些观点的出发点是：我们关于对象的概念，容许这样一些对象——它们的存在对实在所提的要求，很少超过那些不提抽象对象的断言所强加的要求。坚持这一哲学论题的哲学家，就是 Linnebo（2012）所称的元存在论 ** 极简主义者 ** （minimalists）。他们的提案通常与数学哲学中的问题相联提出，然后应用于其他领域。

en: Parsons (1990), Resnik (1997), and Shapiro (1997) contend that, in the case of mathematical theories, coherence suffices for the existence of the objects mentioned in those theories.[^note-20] They do not offer an explicit criterion for distinguishing abstract and concrete objects. Nevertheless, their proposals implicitly draw the distinction; abstract objects are those objects that exist in virtue of the truth of certain modal claims. In particular, the existence of mathematical objects is “grounded in” pure modal truths. For example, numbers exist “in virtue of” the fact that there could have been an $\omega$-sequence of objects; sets exist because there might be entities that satisfy the axioms of one or another set theory, etc. Since these pure modal truths are necessary, this explains why pure abstract objects exist necessarily. It also explains a sense in which they are insubstantial: their existence is grounded in truths that do not (on the face of it) require the actual existence of anything at all.[^note-21]
zh: Parsons（1990）、Resnik（1997）与 Shapiro（1997）主张：就数学理论而言，融贯就足以保证那些理论所提及对象的存在。[^note-20] 他们没有给出区分抽象与具体对象的显式判准。不过，他们的提案隐式地划出了这条线：抽象对象是凭某些模态主张之真而存在的对象。特别地，数学对象的存在“奠基于”纯模态真理。例如，数“凭”如下事实而存在：本可以有一个对象的 $\omega$-序列；集合存在，是因为可能有实体满足这一或那一集合论的公理，等等。既然这些纯模态真理是必然的，这就解释了为何纯抽象对象必然存在。它也解释了它们在何种意义上无实体：其存在奠基于那些（表面上）根本不要求任何东西实际存在的真理。[^note-21]

en: Linnebo (2018) advances a proposal about how to conceive abstract objects by revising our understanding of Fregean biconditional principles of abstraction (see subsection3.4). Some philosophers take these Fregean abstraction principles to be analytic sentences. For example, Hale & Wright (2001; 2009) consider the two sides of an abstraction principle as equivalent as a matter of meaning; they ‘carve up content’ in different ways (to use Frege’s metaphor). But Linnebo (2018, 13–14) rejects this view and the view that such biconditional principles are analytic.
zh: Linnebo（2018）通过修正我们对弗雷格式双条件抽象原则的理解（见 §3.4），提出了一个关于如何构想抽象对象的提案。一些哲学家把这些弗雷格式抽象原则当作分析句子。例如 Hale 与 Wright（2001; 2009）把抽象原则的两边视为凭意义等价；用弗雷格的比喻说，它们以不同方式“切分内容”。但 Linnebo（2018, 13–14）拒绝这一看法，也拒绝这类双条件原则是分析的的看法。

en: He suggests instead that we achieve reference to abstract (and other objects) by means of a *sufficiency operator*, $\Rightarrow$, which he takes to be a strengthening of the material conditional. He starts with *conditional* principles of the form “if $Rab$, then $f(a) \! =\! f(b)$” (e.g., “if $a$ and $b$ are parallel, then the direction of $a$ = the direction of $b$”) and takes the right-hand side to be reconceptualization of the left-hand side. He represents these claims as $\phi \Rightarrow \psi$, where the new operator ‘$\Rightarrow$’ is meant to capture the intuitive idea that $\phi$ *is* (*conceptually*) *sufficient for* $\psi$, or *all that is required for* $\psi$ *is* $\phi$. For $\phi$ to be sufficient for $\psi$, sufficiency must be stronger than *metaphysically implies* but weaker than *analytically implies* (see Linnebo 2018, 15)[^linnebo-2018]. The notion Linnebo considers is a ‘species of metaphysical grounding’.[^note-22] Hence, sufficiency statements allow us to conceptualize statements mentioning abstract objects (or other problematic objects) in terms of metaphysically less problematic or non-problematic objects.
zh: 他转而建议：我们借助一个 ** 充足算子 ** （sufficiency operator）$\Rightarrow$ 达成对抽象（及其他）对象的指称；他认为它是对实质条件句的强化。他从如下形式的 ** 条件 ** 原则出发：“如果 $Rab$，那么 $f(a) \! =\! f(b)$”（例如“如果 $a$ 与 $b$ 平行，那么 $a$ 的方向 = $b$ 的方向”），并把右边取为对左边的再概念化。他把这些主张表示为 $\phi \Rightarrow \psi$，其中新算子“$\Rightarrow$”意在捕捉如下直观想法：$\phi$ 对 $\psi$ ** 是（概念上）充足的 **，或 ** 为 $\psi$ 所需的全部就是 $\phi$**。为使 $\phi$ 对 $\psi$ 充足，充足必须强于 ** 形而上学地蕴含 **，但弱于 ** 分析地蕴含 ** （见 Linnebo 2018, 15）[^linnebo-2018]。林内博考虑的这个概念是“形而上学奠基的一种”。[^note-22] 因此，充足陈述使我们得以用形而上学上较少问题或无问题的对象，来概念化那些提及抽象对象（或其他问题对象）的陈述。

en: It is important for Linnebo that sufficiency be asymmetric. He wouldn’t accept mutual sufficiency, i.e., principles of the form $Rab \Leftrightarrow f(a) \! =\! f(b)$, since these would imply that both sides are equivalent as a matter of meaning. Instead, the point is that the seemingly unproblematic claim $Rab$ renders the claim $f(a) \! =\! f(b)$ unproblematic, and this is best expressed by sufficiency statements of the form $Rab \Rightarrow f(a) \! =\! f(b)$, on which the left side *grounds* the right side. So Linnebo’s notion of reconceptualization is not the Fregean notion of recarving of content.
zh: 对林内博重要的是：充足是非对称的。他不会接受相互充足，即形如 $Rab \Leftrightarrow f(a) \! =\! f(b)$ 的原则，因为那将蕴含两边凭意义等价。相反，要点是：看似无碍的主张 $Rab$ 使主张 $f(a) \! =\! f(b)$ 变得无碍；这最好由形如 $Rab \Rightarrow f(a) \! =\! f(b)$ 的充足陈述表达，其左侧 ** 奠基 ** 右侧。所以，林内博的再概念化概念不是弗雷格式的内容再刻划概念。

en: Moreover, in a sufficiency statement, Linnebo doesn’t require that the relation $R$ be an equivalence relation; he requires only that $R$ be symmetric and transitive. It need not be reflexive, for the domain might contain entities $x$ such that $\neg Rxx$ (e.g., in the case of the sufficiency statement for directions, not every object $x$ in the domain is such that $x$ is parallel with $x$—being parallel is restricted to lines). Linnebo calls such symmetric and transitive relations *unity* relations. When a sufficiency statement—$Rab \Rightarrow f(a) \! =\! f(b)$—holds, then new objects are identified. The new objects are specified in terms of the less problematic entities related by $R$; for example, directions become specified by lines that are parallel. According to Linnebo, the parallel lines become *specifications* of the new objects. A unity relation $R$ is therefore the starting point for developing a sufficient (but not necessary and sufficient) condition for reference.
zh: 此外，在充足陈述中，林内博并不要求关系 $R$ 是等价关系；他只要求 $R$ 对称且传递。它不必自返，因为论域可能包含满足 $\neg Rxx$ 的实体 $x$（例如，在方向的充足陈述中，并非论域中的每个对象 $x$ 都与 $x$ 平行——平行只限于直线）。林内博称这类对称且传递的关系为 ** 统一 ** （unity）关系。当一条充足陈述——$Rab \Rightarrow f(a) \! =\! f(b)$——成立时，新对象被识别出来。新对象由经 $R$ 相关的较少问题的实体来规定；例如，方向由平行的直线来规定。按林内博的说法，平行的直线成为新对象的 ** 规定者 ** （specifications）。因此，统一关系 $R$ 是发展一个充分（但不充分必要）的指称条件的起点。

en: Sometimes the new objects introduced by conditional principles do not make demands on reality; when that happens, they are said to be *thin* (for example, directions only require that there be parallel lines). However, when the new objects introduced by sufficiency statements make more substantial demands on reality, the objects are considered *thick*. Suppose $Rab$ asserts $a$ and $b$ are spatiotemporal parts of the same cohesive and naturally bounded whole. Then $a$ and $b$ become specifications for physical bodies via the following principle: $Rab \Rightarrow \mathrm{Body}(a) \! =\! \mathrm{Body}(b)$. In this case, the principle “makes a substantial demand on the world” because it requires checking that there are spatiotemporal parts *constituting a continuous stretch of solid stuff* (just looking at the spatiotemporal parts does not suffice to determine whether they constitute to a body; see Linnebo 2018, 45)[^linnebo-2018].
zh: 有时，由条件原则引入的新对象不对世界提出要求；出现这种情况时，这些对象被称为 ** 薄的 ** （thin）（例如，方向只要求存在平行的直线）。然而，当由充足陈述引入的新对象对世界提出更实质的要求时，这些对象被视为 ** 厚的 ** （thick）。设想 $Rab$ 断言 $a$ 与 $b$ 是同一个内聚且自然有界的整体之时空部分。于是，$​a$​ 与 $​b$​ 借如下原则成为物理身体的规定者：$Rab \Rightarrow \mathrm{Body}(a) \! =\! \mathrm{Body}(b)$。在此情形中，该原则“对世界提出了实质要求”，因为它要求检验存在 ** 构成一段连续坚固之物 ** 的时空部分（只看时空部分不足以确定它们是否构成一个身体；见 Linnebo 2018, 45）[^linnebo-2018]。

en: However, Linnebo does not identify being abstract with being thin (2012, 147), for there are thin objects in a relative sense that are not abstract, namely those that make no substantial demands on the world beyond those introduced in terms of some antecedently given objects. The mereological sum of your left hand and your laptop makes no demand on the world beyond the demands of its parts.[^note-23] Instead, he suggests that abstract objects are those that are thin and that *have a shallow nature*. The notion of *shallow nature* is meant to capture “the intuitive idea that any question that is solely about $F\text{s}$ has an answer that can be determined on the basis of any given specifications of these $F\text{s}$” (2018, 192–195). For example, directions have a shallow nature because any question about directions (e.g., are they orthogonal, etc.?) can be determined solely on the basis of the lines that specify them. Shapes have a shallow nature because any question about them (e.g., are they triangular, circular, etc.?) can be determined solely on the basis of their underlying concrete figures. By contrast, mereological sums of concrete objects are *not* shallow because there are questions about them that cannot be answered solely on the basis of their specifications; for instance, the weight of the mereological sum of your laptop and your left hand depends not only on their combination but also on the gravitational field in which they are located.[^note-24]
zh: 然而，林内博并不把是抽象等同于薄（being thin）（2012, 147），因为存在相对意义上薄但不抽象的对象，即那些除了以某些先行给定的对象引入的要求之外不再对世界提出实质要求的东西。你的左手与你的笔记本的部分学和，除其部分的要求之外对世界别无所求。[^note-23] 相反，他提出：抽象对象是那些 ** 薄 ** 且 ** 有浅层本性 ** 的对象。** 浅层本性 ** （shallow nature）这一概念意在捕捉“如下直观想法：任何仅仅关于 $F\text{s}$ 的问题，都有一个可以基于这些 $F\text{s}$ 的任何给定规定者而确定的答案”（2018, 192–195）。例如，方向有浅层本性，因为任何关于方向的问题（如它们是否正交等）都可以仅凭规定它们的直线来确定。形状有浅层本性，因为任何关于它们的问题（如它们是否三角形、圆形等）都可以仅凭其底层具体图形来确定。相比之下，具体对象的部分学和 ** 不是 ** 浅层的，因为有一些关于它们的问题无法仅凭其规定者回答；例如，你的笔记本与左手的部分学之和的重量，不仅取决于它们的组合，还取决于它们所处的引力场。[^note-24]

en: Linnebo thus contrasts abstract objects, which are thin and have a shallow nature, with concrete objects, which do not have a shallow nature. Linnebo extends this view in several ways. He constructs an account of mathematical objects that goes beyond the *way of abstraction principles* by providing a reconstruction of set theory in terms of ‘dynamic abstraction’ (2018, ch. 3). This form of minimalism also allows for abstract objects of a mixed nature; namely, those that are *thin relative to* other objects. For example, the type of the letter ‘A’ is abstract because it is thin and has a shallow nature, but it is thin with respect the tokens of the letter ‘A’.
zh: 于是，林内博把抽象对象——薄且有浅层本性——与具体对象——没有浅层本性——相对照。林内博以数种方式扩展了这一看法。他构造了一个超出 ** 抽象原则之路 ** 的数学对象说明：以“动态抽象”重构集合论（2018, 第三章）。这种极简主义还容许混合本性的抽象对象，即 ** 相对于 ** 其他对象薄的对象。例如，字母“A”的类型是抽象的，因为它薄且有浅层本性；但它相对于字母“A”的殊型是薄的。

en: This view, as Linnebo himself admits, faces some problems. One of them is that the methodologies used by working mathematicians, such as classical logic, impredicative definitions, and taking arbitrary subcollections of infinite domains, seem to presuppose objects that are more independent, i.e., objects that don’t have a shallow nature (2018, 197; for a discussion of independence, see Section 4.1 of the entry on platonism in mathematics). Another problem (2018, 195) is that in order for an object to count as having a *shallow nature*, an *intrinsic* unity relation has to be available. An investigation is required to establish that there is such an intrinsic unity relation in each case. It is far from clear that a conditional principle with an *intrinsic* unity relation is available for each of problematic cases mentioned in this entry, such as chess, legal institutions or the English language. Finally, Linnebo doesn’t discuss the question of whether sets of concrete urelements are themselves abstract or concrete. At present, there may be an important question left open by his theory that other theories of abstract objects answer.
zh: 正如林内博本人承认的，这一看法面临一些问题。其一是：执业数学家使用的方法论，如经典逻辑、非直谓定义、对无穷论域取任意子集合，似乎预设了更独立的对象，即没有浅层本性的对象（2018, 197；关于独立性的讨论，见数学中的柏拉图主义词条第 4.1 节）。另一个问题（2018, 195）是：为使一个对象算作有 ** 浅层本性 **，必须有一个 ** 内在的 ** 统一关系可得。需要一项研究来确立每一情形中都存在这样的内在统一关系。远远不清楚的是：对本文提到的每个问题案例——如国际象棋、法律制度或英语——是否都有一条带 ** 内在 ** 统一关系的条件原则可得。最后，林内博没有讨论具体本元的集合本身是抽象还是具体的问题。目前，他的理论可能留下了一个其他抽象对象理论给出了答案的重要问题。

en: 3.8 Eliminativism
zh: 3.8 取消主义

en: We come finally to proposals that reject the abstract/concrete distinction. We can consider three cases. First, there are the nominalists who both reject abstract entities and reject the distinction as illegitimate. They focus on arguing against the formulations of the distinction proposed in the literature. A second group of eliminativists reject real objects of any kind, thereby dismissing the distinction as irrelevant; these are the ontological nihilists. A final group of eliminativists agree that there are prototypical cases of concrete objects and abstract objects, but conclude that a rigorous philosophical distinction can’t be made clearly enough to have any explanatory power (see Sider 2013, 287)[^sider-2013]. This recalls Lewis’ pessimism (1986a, 81–86) about the possibility of establishing a distinction that is sufficiently clear to be theoretically interesting.
zh: 最后来看拒绝抽象/具体之分的提案。可以考虑三种情形。第一，有些唯名论者既拒绝抽象实体，也拒绝把这一区分视为正当的。他们着力于反驳文献中提出的区分表述。第二类取消主义者拒绝任何种类的实在对象，从而把这一区分斥为无关；这些是存在论虚无主义者。最后一类取消主义者同意存在典型的具体对象与抽象对象，但得出结论：一个严格的哲学区分无法清晰到足以具有解释力（见 Sider 2013, 287）[^sider-2013]。这令人回想起刘易斯（1986a, 81–86）对建立一条清晰到足以在理论上有意思的区分之可能性的悲观。

en: 4. Further Reading
zh: 4 延伸阅读

en: Berto & Plebani (2015) provide an useful introduction to ontology and metaontology. Liggins (2024) provides a systematic presentation of platonist and nominalist positions—focused primarily on mathematical objects, but extendable to propositions and properties—using as a guiding thread the assumption that most arguments in favor of the existence of abstract objects share a common argumentative pattern. Van Inwagen & Craig (2024) offer a debate on the existence of abstract objects—particularly numbers—exploring various arguments, including theological considerations. Putnam (1971) makes the case for abstract objects on scientific grounds. Bealer (1993) and Tennant (1997) present *a priori* arguments for the necessary existence of abstract entities. Fine (2002) systematically studies of abstraction principles in the foundations of mathematics. Wetzel (2009) examines the type-token distinction, argues that types are abstract objects while the tokens of those types are their concrete instances, and shows how difficult it is to paraphrase away the many references to types that occur in the sciences and natural language. Zalta (2020) develops a type-theoretic framework for higher-order abstract objects (which includes abstract properties and abstract relations in addition to ordinary properties and relations) and offers both comparisons to other type theories and applications in philosophy and linguistics. Moltmann (2013) investigates the extent to which abstract objects are needed when developing a semantics of natural language; in this book, and also in her article (2020), she defends a ‘core-periphery’ distinction and suggests that natural language ontology contains references to abstract objects only in its periphery. Falguera and Martínez-Vidal (2020) have edited a volume in which contributors present positions and debates about abstract objects of different kinds and categories, in different fields in philosophy.
zh: Berto 与 Plebani（2015）对存在论与元存在论提供了有用的导引。Liggins（2024）对柏拉图主义与唯名论立场——主要聚焦数学对象，但可扩展到命题与性质——做了系统呈现，其引导线索是这样一种假定：支持抽象对象存在的大多数论证共享一个共同的论证模式。Van Inwagen 与 Craig（2024）就抽象对象——特别是数——的存在展开了一场辩论，考察了各种论证，包括神学的考量。Putnam（1971）以科学为据为抽象对象立论。Bealer（1993）与 Tennant（1997）为抽象实体之必然存在提出 ** 先验 ** （*a priori*）论证。Fine（2002）系统研究了数学基础中的抽象原则。Wetzel（2009）考察了类型-殊型之分，论证类型是抽象对象而类型的殊型是其具体实例，并表明改写掉科学与自然语言中大量对类型的指称是何等困难。Zalta（2020）发展了一个高阶抽象对象的类型论框架（在普通性质与关系之外还包括抽象性质与抽象关系），并提供了与其他类型理论的比较以及在哲学与语言学中的应用。Moltmann（2013）考察了发展自然语言语义学时在何种程度上需要抽象对象；在这本书及其文章（2020）中，她辩护了一种“核心-边缘”之分，并建议自然语言存在论只在边缘处才包含对抽象对象的指涉。Falguera 与 Martínez-Vidal（2020）编辑了一部文集，其撰稿人呈现了不同哲学领域中关于不同种类与范畴之抽象对象的立场与论辩。

en: [^note-24]: Linnebo does attempt to make the notion of *having a shallow nature* precise. He appeals to the notion of an *intrinsic* relation and the notion of a relation being *reducible on* a sortal $F$. *Intrinsic* relations are similar to intrinsic properties (which were discussed earlier, in Section 3.5.4); they are relations that things bear to one another in virtue of how they are and how they are related to each other, as opposed to how they are related to things outside of them and how things outside of them are (see the entry on intrinsic vs. extrinsic properties). (For example, the relation of *being parallel* is intrinsic because of how the lines are related to each other, and the relation of *similarity*, which may hold between concrete geometrical figures, is intrinsic because of the shape of the figures.) The definition of a relation being reducible on a sortal $F$ occurs in 2018, 192–195, and we omit the explanation here. But with these notions, Linnebo says that an object $x$ has a *shallow nature* if and only if there is a sortal $F$, such that $x$ is an $F$ and all the intrinsic relations on $x$ are reducible on $F$.
