However, it has been argued that such views also suffer from problems, and fail to avoid counterexamples with the same structure as Davidson’s carbon copier, even though they are explanatorily weaker (Bratman 1991; Paul 2009a; 2009b; Levy 2018)[^bratman-1991][^levy-2018][^paul-2009a]. Since authors like Setiya see the avoidance of counterexamples as a central payoff of the weakenings, it is unclear whether they are worth the costs in explanatory value.
zh: 属于 (ii) 的观点已被多位作者有影响地辩护（Grice 1971; Harman 1986; 1997; Setiya 2007; 2008; 2009; 2012; Velleman 2001; Tenenbaum 2007; Ross 2009; Clark 2020）[^clark-2020][^grice-1971][^ross-2009][^setiya-2007][^tenenbaum-2007]。这类观点的一个流行版本以信念条件取代知识条件（Setiya 2007; Velleman 2001; Ross 2009; Clark 2020）[^clark-2020][^ross-2009][^setiya-2007]：如果行动者有意地 φ［意欲 φ］，她相信自己在 φ-ing［相信她将 φ］。这样的观点 arguably 得到安斯康姆自己某些论证（如上文会话动力学论证）的更好支持；而且它似乎保住了行动的特殊地位——作为公共的发生，而我们的心灵与之处于特殊的认识关系。然而，有人论证这类观点同样有问题，而且尽管解释力较弱，仍未能避免与戴维森复写者同结构的反例（Bratman 1991; Paul 2009a; 2009b; Levy 2018）[^bratman-1991][^levy-2018][^paul-2009a]。既然像 Setiya 这样的作者把避免反例视为弱化的核心收益，这些弱化在解释价值上的代价是否值得，就不清楚了。

en: Finally, views that fall under (iii) aim to show that even if there isn’t a relation of *entailment* between action and practical knowledge, there might yet be an interesting connection between them. For instance, some authors have argued that agents *normally* or *generally* know what they are doing (Peacocke 2003; O’Brien 2007; Gibbons 2010; Schwenkler 2015; 2019; Piñeros Glasscock 2020b)[^gibbons-2010][^o’brien-2007][^peacocke-2003][^piñeros-2020b][^schwenkler-2015]; or that the kind of knowledge that agents have of their intentional action has special properties, such as being first-personal knowledge (Dunn 1998; Moran 2001; 2004; O’Brien 2007; Marcus 2012; Schwenkler 2019)[^dunn-1998][^marcus-2012][^o’brien-2007][^schwenkler-2019].
zh: 最后，属于 (iii) 的观点力图表明：即便在行动与实践知识之间没有 ** 蕴含 ** 关系，两者之间可能仍有有意思的联系。例如，一些作者论证行动者 ** 通常 ** 或 ** 一般 ** 知道自己在做什么（Peacocke 2003; O'Brien 2007; Gibbons 2010; Schwenkler 2015; 2019; Piñeros Glasscock 2020b）[^gibbons-2010][^o'brien-2007][^peacocke-2003][^piñeros-2020b][^schwenkler-2015]；或者行动者对其有意行动具有的那种知识有特殊性质，如第一人称性（Dunn 1998; Moran 2001; 2004; O'Brien 2007; Marcus 2012; Schwenkler 2019）[^dunn-1998][^marcus-2012][^o'brien-2007][^schwenkler-2019]。

en: 4.5 The possibility of practical knowledge
zh: 4.5 实践知识的可能性

en: Regardless of whether one adheres to the knowledge condition (or some weakened version of the view), it is generally agreed that agents *can* have a special kind of knowledge by exercising their practical capacities in intentional action. However, what makes our practical capacities suitable source of knowledge? Anscombe devoted little attention to this question, but an answer to it could be the key to working out a version of (iii) in the previous section.
zh: 无论是否坚持知识条件（或其某种弱化版本），人们普遍同意：行动者 ** 能够 ** 通过在有意行动中施行其实践能力而获得一种特殊的知识。然而，是什么使我们的实践能力成为知识的合宜来源？安斯康姆很少关注这个问题，但对它的回答可能是落实上一节 (iii) 的关键。

en: Here is a simple answer: A person can know that *p* (e.g. that she (herself) is walking), on the basis of exercising her will, because when she does so successfully *p* is true. Two related problems immediately arise for this simple account. First, truth is insufficient for knowledge. Minimally, epistemic warrant is also needed, but the simple account does not give even a hint as to how such warrant could be acquired through agency (Newstead 2006)[^newstead-2006]. Second, there are notorious cases that seem to meet the conditions provided by the simple answer, but where there isn’t knowledge. One case is lucky wishful thinking (Langton 2004)[^langton-2004], e.g., if partly on the basis of optimistic thinking I luckily pull off a jump I would not normally make. Another is pessimistic thinking (Harman 1986; 1997)[^harman-1986], e.g., if I trip partly on the basis of thinking that I will trip. In neither case do I possess knowledge on the basis of my thoughts, despite the thoughts bringing about the truth of their contents. At best, therefore, the simple answer is incomplete, and must be supplemented with a story that explains how it is that the characteristic thoughts of the agent differ from wishful and pessimistic thoughts, such as to provide epistemic warrant.
zh: 一个简单答案是：一个人可以知道 *p*（例如她［自己］正在走路），凭的是施行其意志，因为当她成功地这样做时，*p* 为真。这个简单说明立刻引出两个相关问题。第一，真不足以构成知识。最低限度还需要认识辩护，而简单说明对这种辩护如何能通过能动性获得只字未提（Newstead 2006）[^newstead-2006]。第二，存在一些臭名昭著的情形，似乎满足简单答案的条件，但其中没有知识。一个情形是幸运的一厢情愿（Langton 2004）[^langton-2004]：例如，部分基于乐观的想法，我幸运地完成了一次平时做不出的跳跃。另一个是悲观的想法（Harman 1986; 1997）[^harman-1986]：例如，部分基于“我会绊倒”的想法，我真的绊倒了。在这两种情形中，我都不因我的想法而拥有知识，尽管这些想法使其内容成真。因此，简单答案至多是不完整的，必须辅以一个说明：行动者的特征性想法如何不同于一厢情愿的想法与悲观的想法，从而提供认识辩护。

en: An influential account of this sort was provided in foundational work by Velleman (1989). Simplifying somewhat, Velleman argues that human beings have a core desire to know themselves. Like any desire, this one will motivate agents to satisfy it. In addition, they have the capacities to (a) have thoughts about what they are doing and will do, and (b) have thoughts that are self-referential, e.g. <this very thought won’t make me famous>. Suppose, then, that someone has the thought <I will go to the store in virtue of this thought>. Then, given the desire to know herself, the agent will be motivated to make this thought true. Hence, thought structures of this sort (‘intentions’) will give the agent reasons to believe that what she intends will be true.
zh: Velleman（1989）在奠基性工作中提供了此类有影响的说明。略作简化，Velleman 论证人类有一种认识自己的核心欲望。像任何欲望一样，这一欲望会促使行动者满足它。此外，他们具备如下能力：(a) 拥有关于自己正在做什么与将要做什么的想法，(b) 拥有自我指涉的想法，如〈这个想法本身不会使我成名〉。那么，设想某人有这样的想法：〈我将凭这个想法去商店〉。于是，鉴于认识自己的欲望，行动者会被推动使这个想法成真。因此，这类思想结构（“意图”）会给行动者理由去相信其所意欲的将会成真。

en: Several worries have been raised against Velleman’s view. One is that it makes dubious empirical claims, theorizing about the mind from the armchair. In response, Velleman (2000a) has provided empirical support for his more contentious psychological claim, that humans have a deep desire for self-knowledge. Another worry is that this epistemic mechanism still looks too much like wishful thinking, believing that something is the case just because one wants it to be so (Langton 2004; see Setiya 2008; Velleman 2014 for replies)[^langton-2004][^setiya-2008][^velleman-2014]. Finally, it is unclear why, if an agent realizes that the content of her intention is not realized, she must make it true that it is, rather than simply give up the belief (that she will act in a certain way). After all, we can pursue the aim of knowing ourselves both by ensuring that beliefs about ourselves are true *and* by giving up beliefs about ourselves that are false.
zh: 对 Velleman 的观点已提出几个担忧。其一，它做了可疑的经验断言，从扶手椅上对心灵进行理论化。作为回应，Velleman（2000a）为其较有争议的心理学主张——人类对自我认识有深层欲望——提供了经验支持。另一个担忧是：这一认识机制看起来仍太像一厢情愿——仅仅因为想要某事为真就相信它为真（Langton 2004；回应见 Setiya 2008; Velleman 2014）[^langton-2004][^setiya-2008][^velleman-2014]。最后，不清楚的是：如果行动者意识到其意图的内容未实现，她为什么必须使它成真，而不是干脆放弃信念（她将以某种方式行动的信念）。毕竟，我们可以通过确保关于自己的信念为真 ** 以及 ** 放弃关于自己的假信念，来追求认识自己这一目的。

en: Worries of this sort led Velleman to distinguish “directive” from “receptive” cognition (Velleman 2000, ch.7); but it has led others to consider the alternative view that practical knowledge is a standard form of inferential knowledge (Grice 1971; O’Shaughnessy 1980, 2003; Paul 2009a)[^grice-1971][^o’shaughnessy-1980][^paul-2009a]. On the most sophisticated inferentialist account, due to Paul (2009a), agents take advantage of the special knowledge they have of their intentions to make inferences about what is happening and will happen. Given that intentions are reliably executed, such inferences reliably yield knowledge. A more radical inferentialist alternative, suggested by authors like Carruthers (2011) on the basis of empirical evidence, is that we know our actions on the basis of the same processes by which we know others’ minds: we essentially predict what actions are most likely to happen, given what else we know about others’ motives and beliefs—it’s just that we know a lot more about our own minds. (Similar views about self-knowledge in general are defended by Gopnik 1993, and have their origin in Ryle 1949. For criticisms, see Boyle 2022; Levy 2022.)[^boyle-2022][^gopnik-1993][^levy-2022][^ryle-1949]
zh: 这类担忧促使 Velleman 区分“引导性”与“接受性”认知（Velleman 2000, ch.7）；但也使另一些人考虑另一种观点：实践知识是一种标准的推理知识（Grice 1971; O'Shaughnessy 1980, 2003; Paul 2009a）[^grice-1971][^o'shaughnessy-1980][^paul-2009a]。在最精致的推理论说明——Paul（2009a）提出——中，行动者利用其对意图的特殊知识来推理正在发生与将要发生的事。鉴于意图被可靠地执行，这类推理可靠地产生知识。一个更激进的推理论替代方案——由 Carruthers（2011）等基于经验证据提出——是：我们对自己的行动的认识，凭的是我们认识他人心灵的同一过程：我们本质上是在预测哪些行动最可能发生——依据我们对他人动机与信念的所知；只不过我们对自身心灵知道得多得多。（关于一般自我认识的类似观点由 Gopnik 1993 辩护，其源头在 Ryle 1949。批评见 Boyle 2022; Levy 2022。）[^boyle-2022][^gopnik-1993][^levy-2022][^ryle-1949]

en: Inferentialist accounts give up on a feature that was central to Anscombe’s understanding of practical knowledge, its immediate character (see e.g. O’Brien 2007)[^o’brien-2007]. However, Paul (2009a) argues that the appearance of immediacy can be explained by the fact that inferences “can take place rapidly and automatically at a non-conscious level, without the mindful entertaining of premises or feeling of drawing a conclusion” (p.10). Yet, several challenges have been raised against inferentialist accounts, including: (i) that they can’t explain the tight nexus between intentional action and practical knowledge (Setiya 2007, 2008, 2009)[^setiya-2007]; (ii) that they can’t explain the first-personal character of practical knowledge (Wilson 2000; Schwenkler 2012)[^schwenkler-2012][^wilson-2000]; and (iii) that they at best give us alienated, observational knowledge (Piñeros Glasscock 2021)[^piñeros-2021].
zh: 推理论说明放弃了安斯康姆实践知识理解的一个核心特征：其直接性（如 O'Brien 2007）[^o'brien-2007]。不过，Paul（2009a）论证：直接性的表象可以由如下事实解释——推理“可以在非意识的层面快速而自动地发生，无需有意识地考虑前提或得出结论的感受”（p.10）。然而，推理论说明已遭到若干挑战，包括：(i) 它们无法解释有意行动与实践知识之间的紧密联系（Setiya 2007, 2008, 2009）[^setiya-2007]；(ii) 它们无法解释实践知识的第一人称性（Wilson 2000; Schwenkler 2012）[^schwenkler-2012][^wilson-2000]；(iii) 它们至多给我们异化的、观察性的知识（Piñeros Glasscock 2021）[^piñeros-2021]。

en: There are, finally, several non-inferentialist stories about how practical knowledge is possible. Some accounts appeal to knowledge-how or skill as the state by which an intention ensures that its content is not only true but also justified, so as to amount to knowledge (Setiya 2012; Small 2012; Valaris 2021)[^setiya-2012][^small-2012][^valaris-2021]. Another view, due to O’Brien (2007), explains practical knowledge in terms of the exercise of deliberative capacities. The agent knows what she is doing because the selection of an action is done via the exercise of capacities that narrow options in terms of the practical possibilities of the agent. Others take practical knowledge to be inferential, but the inference in question is practical inference. On this view, practical knowledge is warranted by the practical considerations that constitute the agent’s practical reasoning (Harman 1997; Tenenbaum 2007; Ross 2009; Marušić and Schwenkler 2018; Campbell 2018; Frey 2019)[^campbell-2018][^harman-1997][^marušić-2018][^ross-2009][^tenenbaum-2007]. Finally, some have tried to show that accounts of epistemic warrant or entitlement designed to explain how we can directly believe on the basis of perception might explain how we can directly believe on the basis of our wills (Peacocke 2003; Newstead 2006; Piñeros Glasscock 2020a)[^newstead-2006][^peacocke-2003][^piñeros-2020a]. As this brief and incomplete summary indicates, there is not yet anything close to a consensus about how best to explain the epistemic standing for practical knowledge.
zh: 最后，还有若干非推理论的说明，解释实践知识如何可能。一些说明诉诸知道如何或技能，作为意图确保其内容不仅为真、而且有辩护（从而构成知识）的状态（Setiya 2012; Small 2012; Valaris 2021）[^setiya-2012][^small-2012][^valaris-2021]。另一观点由 O'Brien（2007）提出，以慎感能力的施行解释实践知识。行动者知道自己在做什么，因为行动的选择是通过那些按行动者的实践可能性收窄选项的能力的施行而完成的。另一些人认为实践知识是推理性的，但所涉推理是实践推理。按这种看法，实践知识由构成行动者实践推理的实践考量提供辩护（Harman 1997; Tenenbaum 2007; Ross 2009; Marušić and Schwenkler 2018; Campbell 2018; Frey 2019）[^campbell-2018][^harman-1997][^marušić-2018][^ross-2009][^tenenbaum-2007]。最后，一些人试图表明：为解释我们如何能直接基于知觉而相信而设计的认识辩护或权利说明，或许能解释我们如何能直接基于我们的意志而相信（Peacocke 2003; Newstead 2006; Piñeros Glasscock 2020a）[^newstead-2006][^peacocke-2003][^piñeros-2020a]。正如这一简短而不完整的总结所示，关于如何最好地解释实践知识的认识地位，尚无接近共识的东西。

en: 5. The Ontology of Actions
zh: 5 行动的存在论

en: What are actions? The traditional answer is: they are *events* of a certain sort (e.g. events with a distinctive causal history). That, at any rate, is the letter of the views found in Anscombe (1957), Davidson (1963; 1967a; 1967b; 1985), and much subsequent literature. However, some scholars have recently argued that Anscombe’s position is better captured by the claim that actions are *processes*, and that there are philosophical advantages to this view. Yet, others take actions to be something else altogether. This section explains what this dispute is about, and explores some of its implications for other ontological debates such as the individuation of action. It then considers further important questions about the metaphysics of action, such as whether there must be basic actions, and whether *Action* constitutes a unified category.
zh: 行动是什么？传统答案是：它们是某种 ** 事件 ** （（例如具有独特因果史的事件）。无论如何，这是 Anscombe（1957）、Davidson（1963; 1967a; 1967b; 1985）以及大量后续文献中观点的字面。然而，一些学者近来论证：安斯康姆的立场更好地被“行动是 ** 过程 **”这一主张所捕捉，而且这种看法有哲学上的优点。还有人则认为行动完全是别的东西。本节解释这场争论是关于什么的，并探讨其对行动个别化等其他存在论争论的一些蕴含。然后它考虑关于行动形而上学的更重要的进一步问题：例如，是否必须有基本行动，以及 **行动** 是否构成一个统一的范畴。

en: 5.1 Events, processes, and more
zh: 5.1 事件、过程及更多

en: There are several reasons to categorize actions as events. A central one concerns their connection to causation (Davidson 1967a; Goldman 1970)[^davidson-1967a][^goldman-1970]. Actions are directly implicated in causal relations: modifying Davidson’s example (pp.4–5), the burglar’s entering my house might cause me to turn on the light, which in turn might cause him to be startled. On the widespread assumption that events are the primary causal relata, it would follow that actions, such as my turning on of the light, are events.
zh: 把行动归类为事件有几个理由。一个中心理由关乎它们与因果性的联系（Davidson 1967a; Goldman 1970）[^davidson-1967a][^goldman-1970]。行动直接牵涉因果关系中：修改戴维森的例子（pp.4–5），窃贼进入我家可能引起我开灯，而这又可能使他受惊。在“事件是基本的因果关系项”这一广泛假定下，就可以推出：像我开灯这样的行动是事件。

en: Another argument for the event view is that it explains common inference patterns. As Davidson (1967b) noted, sentences attributing actions to agents admit of adjectival drop. Thus, a sentence like (3) entails (4), which in turn entails (5):
zh: 事件观的另一个论证是：它解释了常见的推理模式。正如 Davidson（1967b）指出的，把行动归于行动者的句子允许形容词脱落。因此，像 (3) 这样的句子蕴含 (4)，后者又蕴含 (5)：

en: Donald buttered the toast in the bathroom at 12am.
zh: 唐纳德午夜 12 点在浴室里给吐司抹了黄油。

en: Donald buttered the toast in the bathroom.
zh: 唐纳德在浴室里给吐司抹了黄油。

en: Donald buttered the toast.
zh: 唐纳德给吐司抹了黄油。

en: Davidson suggested that the best way to account for these inferential relations is to assume that at the level of logical form these sentences quantify over events. So understood, the logical form of (3)–(5) would be as follows:[^note-6]
zh: 戴维森提出：解释这些推理关系的最好办法，是假定在逻辑形式层面这些句子量化事件。如此理解，(3)–(5) 的逻辑形式如下：[^note-6]

en: $\exists x(\textrm{Buttering}(x) \amp \textrm{By}(x, \textrm{Donald}) \amp \textrm{Object}(x, \textrm{toast})\ \amp $ $\textrm{Location}(x, \textrm{bathroom}) \amp \textrm{Time}(x, \textrm{12am}))$
zh: $\exists x(\textrm{Buttering}(x) \amp \textrm{By}(x, \textrm{Donald}) \amp \textrm{Object}(x, \textrm{toast})\ \amp $ $\textrm{Location}(x, \textrm{bathroom}) \amp \textrm{Time}(x, \textrm{12am}))$

en: $\exists x(\textrm{Buttering}(x) \amp \textrm{By}(x, \textrm{Donald}) \amp \textrm{Object}(x, \textrm{toast})\ \amp$ $\textrm{Location}(x, \textrm{bathroom}))$
zh: $\exists x(\textrm{Buttering}(x) \amp \textrm{By}(x, \textrm{Donald}) \amp \textrm{Object}(x, \textrm{toast})\ \amp$ $\textrm{Location}(x, \textrm{bathroom}))$

en: $\exists x(\textrm{Buttering}(x) \amp \textrm{By}(x, \textrm{Donald}) \amp \textrm{Object}(x, \textrm{toast}))$
zh: $\exists x(\textrm{Buttering}(x) \amp \textrm{By}(x, \textrm{Donald}) \amp \textrm{Object}(x, \textrm{toast}))$

en: The entailment relations are then easily explained through the classical rules for conjunction and existential quantification. This analysis, which has been highly influential in formal semantics, appears to entail that actions are events, entities with a spatiotemporal location (since they admit of spatiotemporal modifiers), that possess the properties denoted by adverbial modifiers (such as who was engaged in them, or what the object of the action was).
zh: 于是，蕴含关系通过合取与存在量化的经典规则得到轻易解释。这一分析——它在形式语义学中影响巨大——似乎蕴含：行动是事件，是具有时空定位的实体（因为它们容许时空修饰语），拥有状语修饰语所指称的性质（如谁在从事它、行动的对象是什么）。

en: Finally, perhaps the most straightforward reason to hold that actions are events, is that this fits naturally with the way we speak about them. For instance, we say, “The event we observed last night turned out to be a theft”, or “The murder of that woman was a sad event”.
zh: 最后，主张行动是事件的最直白理由也许是：这自然契合我们谈论它们的方式。例如，我们说“我们昨晚观察到的事件原来是一桩盗窃”，或“那位妇女之死是一件令人悲伤的事”。

en: Against this view, a number of scholars have recently argued that actions (in the sense of concern for philosophy of action) are instead *processes* (Mourelatos 1978; Stout 1997; Hornsby 2012; Steward 2012; Charles 2018)[^charles-2018][^hornsby-2012][^mourelatos-1978][^stout-1997]. To understand this claim, we first need to explain what the distinction amounts to. We can introduce it at an intuitive level in terms of the aspectual distinction between the following two sentences:
zh: 反对这一看法，近来不少学者论证：（行动哲学所关心的意义上的）行动毋宁是 ** 过程 ** （（Mourelatos 1978; Stout 1997; Hornsby 2012; Steward 2012; Charles 2018）[^charles-2018][^hornsby-2012][^mourelatos-1978][^stout-1997]。为理解这一主张，我们首先需要说明该区分是什么。我们可以在直观层面借以下两句之间的体貌区分来引入它：

en: Donald is *buttering* the toast.
zh: 唐纳德 ** 正在给 ** 吐司抹黄油。

en: Donald *has buttered* the toast.
zh: 唐纳德 ** 已经给 ** 吐司抹了黄油。

en: (6) refers to an ongoing occurrence in the midst of development. As such, many of its properties are still indeterminate and may change over time. It may be happening in the bathroom in a matter of seconds if Donald stays there; but he could take a break, forget about it, and continue on with it several minutes later in the kitchen. Moreover, the manner in which it takes place can change as it occurs: it may speed up (if Donald is suddenly in a hurry) or slow down (if Donald is distracted by a noise), and he may start doing it more mindfully, or distractedly. Indeed, however Donald is *doing* the buttering, it may happen that he never ends up *having buttered* the toast (a nearby scream might cause him to drop it in the toilet halfway through). This is sometimes called the “imperfective paradox”: in general, ⌜*x* is φ-ing⌝ does not entail ⌜*x* has φ’d⌝. By contrast, the event itself, denoted by (7), cannot speed up or slow down, nor change the manner in which it is done, since it is already complete. This is why it has a determinate temporal-spatial location in terms of which some have sought to individuate it (Lemmon 1967; Quine 1985; Davidson 1985)[^davidson-1985][^lemmon-1967][^quine-1985]. By contrast, processes do not have an essential temporal-spatial location: the same process of buttering that is now taking place at 12:01 could culminate in a minute or in an hour.
zh: (6) 指称一个正处于展开之中的进行事件。因此，它的许多性质仍不确定，并可能随时间改变。如果唐纳德待在浴室里，它可能在几秒内就发生在浴室里；但他也可能停下来、忘掉它，几分钟后在厨房里继续。此外，它发生的方式可以在发生过程中改变：它可能加速（如果唐纳德突然着急）或减速（如果唐纳德被一个响声分神），他可能开始做得更专注，或更心不在焉。的确，无论唐纳德 ** 正在 ** 如何抹黄油，都可能发生：他最终永远没能 ** 抹完 ** （（一声尖叫可能使他在半途把它掉进马桶）。这有时被称为“未完成体悖论”：一般而言，⌜*x* 正在 φ-ing⌝ 不蕴含 ⌜*x* 已经 φ 过⌝。相比之下，由 (7) 指称的事件本身不能加速或减速，也不能改变其进行的方式，因为它已经完成。这就是为什么它有一个确定的时空定位——有人试图据此个别化它（Lemmon 1967; Quine 1985; Davidson 1985）[^davidson-1985][^lemmon-1967][^quine-1985]。相比之下，过程没有一个本质性的时空定位：现在 12:01 正在进行的同一个抹黄油过程，可能在一分钟后或一小时后达成。

en: The most straightforward reason to think that actions are processes is that actions appear to have these properties, as is indicated by the examples used in the previous paragraph (Stout 1997; Steward 2012; Charles 2015; 2018)[^charles-2015][^stout-1997]. Thus, one’s action can speed up or slow down, be done in one way or another at different times in its history, and may culminate at different times. Indeed, an ongoing action may never be completed.
zh: 认为行动是过程的最直白理由是：行动似乎具有这些性质，如前一段所用例子所示（Stout 1997; Steward 2012; Charles 2015; 2018）[^charles-2015][^stout-1997]。因此，一个人的行动可以加速或减速，在其历史的不同时刻以不同方式进行，并可能在不同的时间达成。的确，一个进行中的行动可能永远不会完成。

en: The connection between imperfective aspect and processes provides further impetus for the view that actions are processes (the argument to follow is based on Michael Thompson’s ideas (2008, 122–30), though he rejects the view that actions are processes, understood as particulars (pp.134–7)). After all, it seems essential to actions that they can enter into rationalizing explanations (Anscombe 1957; Thompson 2008; Wiland 2013; Ford 2015; 2017)[^anscombe-1957][^ford-2015][^thompson-2008][^wiland-2013], and such explanations can easily be given in imperfective language. To see this, consider again Anscombe’s case of a man who operates a lever to pump poisoned water to a house, with the plan of killing the inhabitants (Anscombe 1957, §23)[^anscombe-1957]. We could represent his thoughts as follows: “I am moving the lever up and down *because* I am pumping water to the house *because* I am poisoning its inhabitants.” Indeed, such formulations seem to express canonical answers to Anscombe’s special question “Why?” (Thompson 2008; Wiland 2013; Ford 2015)[^ford-2015][^thompson-2008][^wiland-2013]. However, we cannot capture the same thoughts without imperfective expressions (Thompson 2008)[^thompson-2008]. The train of thought that goes, “I have moved the lever up and down *because* I have pumped the water *because* I have poisoned the inhabitants of the house” makes it sound like the man is acting on a conditional promise to move the lever if the men are killed by his hand. This suggests that whereas processes can directly enter into the kinds of rationalizing explanations definitive of intentional action, events cannot (except, perhaps, derivatively), which in turn suggests that actions are processes.
zh: 未完成体与过程之间的联系，为行动是过程的观点提供了进一步推动（以下论证基于 Michael Thompson 的想法（2008, 122–30），尽管他拒绝行动是过程——被理解为殊项——的观点（pp.134–7））。毕竟，行动的本质似乎是：它们能够进入合理化解释之中（Anscombe 1957; Thompson 2008; Wiland 2013; Ford 2015; 2017）[^anscombe-1957][^ford-2015][^thompson-2008][^wiland-2013]，而这类解释可以轻易用未完成体的语言给出。为看清这一点，再考虑安斯康姆那个操作杠杆给房子抽毒水、计划杀死屋中人的例子（Anscombe 1957, §23）[^anscombe-1957]。我们可以把他的想法表征如下：“我正在上下移动杠杆，** 因为 ** 我正在给房子抽水，** 因为 ** 我正在毒害屋里的人。”的确，这类表述似乎表达了安斯康姆“为什么？”之特殊问法的标准答案（Thompson 2008; Wiland 2013; Ford 2015）[^ford-2015][^thompson-2008][^wiland-2013]。然而，离开未完成体表达，我们无法捕捉同样的想法（Thompson 2008）[^thompson-2008]。“我已经移动了杠杆 ** 因为 ** 我已经抽了水 ** 因为 ** 我已毒死了屋里的人”这一思路，听起来像这个人在按一个条件承诺行动——如果那些人是死于他手的话。这表明：过程可以直接进入界定有意行动的那类合理化解释，而事件不能（或许除派生情形外）；这又暗示行动是过程。

en: Finally, it has been suggested that the process view can better accommodate the type of direct guidance that Frankfurt identified as essential to intentional action (see above, section 2.4). It seems attractive to explain the nature of this direct guidance in terms of how substances in general cause changes by engaging in certain processes (Hornsby 2012)[^hornsby-2012], or in terms of the different ways in which an agent can manifest her agency in a process (slower, faster, more or less skillfully) (Charles 2018)[^charles-2018]. And, as Steward (2012) suggests, this might give a substantial role to the agent in the explanation of action. By contrast, since events have settled natures and spatial-temporal properties, it seems that the agent can at best interact with them in the indirect way in which she interacts with other objects, such as a car.
zh: 最后，有人提出：过程观可以更好地容纳 Frankfurt 认定为有意行动之本质的那类直接引导（见上文第 2.4 节）。以实体一般如何通过从事某些过程而引起变化来解释这种直接引导的本性（Hornsby 2012）[^hornsby-2012]，或以行动者可以在过程中显现其能动性的不同方式（更慢、更快、更熟练或较不熟练）来解释（Charles 2018）[^charles-2018]，似乎是有吸引力的。而且，如 Steward（2012）所提示，这可能在行动解释中给行动者一个实质性的角色。相比之下，既然事件有定型的本性与时空性质，行动者至多只能以她与别的对象（如一辆车）互动的那种间接方式与之互动。

en: It is only recently that an alternative to the event view has been clearly formulated and defended. As such, much work remains to be done in this area, and even among defenders of the process view there are important disagreements. One important disagreement is over whether processes are particulars (Galton 2006; Steward 2012; Charles 2018)[^charles-2018][^galton-2006] or not (Stout 1997; Crowther 2011; Hornsby 2012; Crowther 2018; cf. Thompson 2008)[^crowther-2018][^crowther-2011][^hornsby-2012][^stout-1997][^thompson-2008]. Another disagreement is about whether a unique thing is a process and an event (at different times) (Steward 2012; Charles 2018)[^charles-2018], or whether the process and the event are distinct things (Stout 1997; Crowther 2011; Hornsby 2012; Charles 2015; Crowther 2018)[^charles-2015][^crowther-2018][^crowther-2011][^hornsby-2012][^stout-1997].
zh: 只是晚近，事件观的替代方案才被清楚地表述与捍卫。因此，这一领域仍有许多工作要做，即便在过程观的辩护者之间也存在重要分歧。一个重要分歧是：过程究竟是殊项（Galton 2006; Steward 2012; Charles 2018）[^charles-2018][^galton-2006]还是不是（Stout 1997; Crowther 2011; Hornsby 2012; Crowther 2018；参见 Thompson 2008）[^crowther-2018][^crowther-2011][^hornsby-2012][^stout-1997][^thompson-2008]。另一个分歧是：同一个东西是一个过程又是一个事件（在不同时间）（Steward 2012; Charles 2018）[^charles-2018]，还是过程与事件是不同的东西（Stout 1997; Crowther 2011; Hornsby 2012; Charles 2015; Crowther 2018）[^charles-2015][^crowther-2018][^crowther-2011][^hornsby-2012][^stout-1997]。

en: Regardless of how these questions are answered, a remaining challenge is to explain the *unity* between processes and events, the fact that there is a non-accidental connection between the process of buttering, and the event of one’s having buttered the toast that results if the action is successful (Haase 2022)[^haase-2022]. Moreover, it is worth noting that although the process-view is the most important alternative available to the events-view, other proposals have been advanced recently, including the view that actions are thoughts (Rödl 2007; 2011; Marcus 2012; Valaris 2020)[^marcus-2012][^rödl-2007][^valaris-2020]. For example, Marcus holds that to act intentionally just is to judge that the action is to be done.
zh: 无论这些问题如何回答，一个剩余的挑战是解释过程与事件之间的 ** 统一性 **：抹黄油的过程与行动成功时导致的那种“已经给吐司抹了黄油”的事件之间存在非偶然的联系（Haase 2022）[^haase-2022]。此外，值得注意的是：尽管过程观是事件观面前最重要的替代方案，近来还提出了其他提案，包括行动是思想的看法（Rödl 2007; 2011; Marcus 2012; Valaris 2020）[^marcus-2012][^rödl-2007][^valaris-2020]。例如，Marcus 主张：有意地行动，恰恰就是判断该行动应当被做。

en: 5.2 The Individuation of Action
zh: 5.2 行动的个别化

en: The example of the pumper displays another important Anscombean thesis (endorsed by Davidson, see section 2.2 above): that a single event can instantiate different properties in terms of which it can be described. Thus, the same action is at once a *moving of the hands*, a *pumping of water*, and *a poisoning*. This was important for Anscombe because she held that actions are intentional only under some descriptions: for instance, even if the pumper’s energetic moves scare a nearby squirrel, the action would not be intentional under the description *scaring of a squirrel*.
zh: 水泵工的例子展示了另一个重要的安斯康姆式论题（戴维森也接受，见上文第 2.2 节）：单一事件可以例示多种性质，依之它可以被描述。于是，同一个行动同时是一次“手的移动”、一次“抽水”和一次“下毒”。这对安斯康姆很重要，因为她主张行动只在某些描述下是有意的：例如，即便水泵工用力的动作吓到了附近一只松鼠，该行动在“吓到松鼠”的描述下也不是有意的。

en: The most influential alternative to this “coarse-grained” account is a “fine-grained” account that individuates actions (and events, more generally) in terms of their properties (Kim 1966; 1969; 1973; 1976; Goldman 1970)[^goldman-1970][^kim-1966]. On this view, *A* and *B* are the same action just in case *A* has all and only the properties that *B* has; and for each set of such properties, there is an event. Since moving one’s hands, pumping water, and poisoning are distinct properties, this view entails that the pumper’s moving of his hands, his pumping of the water, and his poisoning of the inhabitants are distinct actions.
zh: 对这一“粗颗粒”说明最有影响的替代方案，是按性质个别化行动（以及更一般的事件）的“细颗粒”说明（Kim 1966; 1969; 1973; 1976; Goldman 1970）[^goldman-1970][^kim-1966]。按这种看法，*A* 与 *B* 是同一个行动，当且仅当 *A* 拥有且仅拥有 *B* 拥有的那些性质；而每一组这样的性质都对应一个事件。既然移动自己的手、抽水与下毒是不同的性质，这种看法蕴含：水泵工的移动他的手、他的抽水与他的毒害屋中人，是不同的行动。

en: Anscombe complained that treating these as different actions would be like treating the author of *David Copperfield* and the author of *Bleak House* as different men, rather than a single author, Dickens (Anscombe 1979, 222)[^anscombe-1979]. Indeed, the fine-grained view has similar counterintuitive implications. Consider: the properties of pumping water, pumping water while smiling, and pumping water at noon, are all different properties. So, the man who pumped water at noon while smiling would have engaged in three different pumpings according to the fine-grained view.
zh: 安斯康姆抱怨说：把它们当作不同的行动，就像把《大卫·科波菲尔》的作者与《荒凉山庄》的作者当作不同的人，而非同一位作者狄更斯（Anscombe 1979, 222）[^anscombe-1979]。的确，细颗粒观有类似的反直觉蕴含。考虑：抽水、微笑着抽水、正午抽水，是三个不同的性质。于是，按细颗粒观，那个正午微笑着抽水的人就从事了三次不同的抽水。

en: Moreover, the view threatens to undermine some basic inferences we are inclined to make about actions (Katz 1978)[^katz-1978]. For instance, it seems obvious that from:
zh: 此外，这种看法有可能破坏我们对行动倾向于做的一些基本推理（Katz 1978）[^katz-1978]。例如，从：

en: The table in the room is brown.
zh: 屋里那张桌子是棕色的。

en: We can infer:
zh: 我们显然可以推出：

en: The table in the room = the brown table.
zh: 屋里那张桌子 = 那张棕色的桌子。

en: But, similarly, it seems that from:
zh: 但类似地，似乎从：

en: The man’s pumping occurred at noon.
zh: 那人的抽水发生在正午。

en: We can infer:
zh: 我们可以推出：

en: The man’s pumping = The man’s pumping at noon.
zh: 那人的抽水 = 那人在正午的抽水。

en: However, on the fine-grained view the inference to (11) is invalid since the two descriptions in (11) must refer to distinct events. Hence the defender of the fine-grained view is forced to reject a seemingly innocuous inference pattern.
zh: 然而，按细颗粒观，向 (11) 的推理是无效的，因为 (11) 中的两个描述必须指称不同的对象。因此，细颗粒观的辩护者被迫拒斥一个看似无害的推理模式。

en: These are serious problems, and it is not clear that defenders of the fine-grained view can do more than bite the bullets. However, it has been argued that the coarse-grained account has similarly counterintuitive implications (Goldman 1970; Thomson 1971)[^goldman-1970][^thomson-1971]. To see why, consider the following two sentences (true of the imagined pumper):
zh: 这些是严肃的问题，而细颗粒观的辩护者除了咬子弹似乎别无他法。不过，有人论证：粗颗粒说明也有类似反直觉的蕴含（Goldman 1970; Thomson 1971）[^goldman-1970][^thomson-1971]。为看清原因，考虑关于假想水泵工为真的两个句子：

en: The man moved his hands before he poisoned the inhabitants.
zh: 那人在毒害屋中人之前移动了他的手。

en: The man caused the poisoning of the inhabitants by moving his hands.
zh: 那人通过移动他的手引起了屋中人的中毒。

en: We can paraphrase them using gerundival expressions as follows:
zh: 我们可以用动名词表达式把它们改写为：

en: The man’s moving of his hands happened before the poisoning of the inhabitants.
zh: 那人的手的移动发生在屋中人的中毒之前。

en: The man’s moving of his hands caused the poisoning of the inhabitants.
zh: 那人的手的移动引起了屋中人的中毒。

en: Now, suppose we assume the claim that:
zh: 现在，假设我们接受：

en: The man’s moving of his hands = the man’s poisoning of the inhabitants.
zh: 那人的手的移动 = 那人的毒害屋中人。

en: Then, by substitution, we arrive at the absurd:
zh: 那么，经替换我们得到荒谬的：

en: The man’s moving of his hands happened before the man’s moving of his hands.
zh: 那人的手的移动发生在那人的手的移动之前。

en: The man’s moving of his hands caused his moving of his hands.
zh: 那人的手的移动引起了那人的手的移动。

en: It is natural to think that (14) is the culprit; but to hold that claims such as (14) are false seems to amount to rejecting the coarse-grained view of action individuation.
zh: 自然的想法是 (14) 是罪魁祸首；但主张 (14) 这样的主张为假，似乎等于拒斥行动个别化的粗颗粒观。

en: One possible response would be to hold that the contexts ⌜φ happens* before ψ⌝ and ⌜φ causes* ψ⌝ (the * marks tenselessness) are intensional in the φ and ψ positions (Anscombe 1969)[^anscombe-1969]. If so, substitution of co-referents may change truth value in these contexts. Alternatively, one could attempt to explain these results pragmatically: the sentences sound odd in the same way as it sounds odd to say that “a man married his widow”, even though it is true (the man married her *before* she was a widow, of course!) (cf. Anscombe 1979)[^anscombe-1979]. However, these are controversial semantic theses (for further intensionalist treatments, see Achinstein 1975; McDermott 1995; Wasserman 2004; for extensionalist treatments, see e.g., Davidson 1967a; Strawson 1985; Rosenberg and Martin 1979; Schaffer 2005; for an excellent review of research on causal contexts more generally, including pragmatic effects, see Swanson 2012).
zh: 一种可能的回应是主张：语境⌜φ 发生在＊ ψ 之前⌝与⌜φ 引起＊ ψ⌝（＊ 标记无时态性）在 φ 与 ψ 位置上是内涵的（Anscombe 1969）[^anscombe-1969]。若如此，同指者的替换在这些语境中可能改变真值。或者，人们可以尝试用语用学解释这些结果：这些句子听起来奇怪，就像“一个人娶了他的遗孀”听起来奇怪一样——尽管它是真的（这个人是在她成为遗孀 ** 之前 ** 娶的她，当然！）（参见 Anscombe 1979）[^anscombe-1979]。然而，这些是有争议的语义论题（进一步的内涵论处理见 Achinstein 1975; McDermott 1995; Wasserman 2004；外延论处理见 Davidson 1967a; Strawson 1985; Rosenberg and Martin 1979; Schaffer 2005；对包括语用效应在内的因果语境研究的优秀综述，见 Swanson 2012）。

en: A different response is suggested by the view that actions are processes. That view enables us to treat action descriptions as sometimes characterizing the different stages of the action (cf. Russell 2018)[^russell-2018]. Then, appealing to Anscombe’s insight that we should treat claims about actions in parallel with claims about persons, we could say that the moving of one’s hands precedes and causes the poisoning in an analogous way as the acorn precedes and causes the oak. But just as there is a single organism in the latter case, there is a single action in the former, even though it seems at best paradoxical to say that I caused myself to exist, or that the oak caused the acorn.
zh: 另一种回应由行动是过程的看法提示。那种看法使我们能够把行动描述有时视为刻画行动的不同阶段（参见 Russell 2018）[^russell-2018]。然后，诉诸安斯康姆的洞见——关于行动的主张应当与关于人的主张平行处理——我们可以说：手的移动先于并引起中毒，正如橡果先于并引起橡树。但正如在后一情形中只有一个有机体，在前一情形中也只有一个行动，即便说“我引起了我自己的存在”或“橡树引起了橡果”至多是悖论性的。

en: Finally, the coarse- and fine-grained views obviously do not exhaust the conceptual landscape. A number of philosophers have offered individuation principles stricter than those advanced by coarse-grained theorists, but laxer than those advanced by fine-grained theorists (e.g. Ginet 1990)[^ginet-1990]. Charles (1984), for example, argues that Aristotle would individuate actions in terms of capacities. This allows us to say that the moving of one’s hands is the same action as the moving of one’s hands quickly (since a single capacity is thereby actualized), even though it is a different action from the poisoning, which actualizes a different set of capacities. The challenge for this view is to provide an account of the individuation of capacities independent of the account of the individuation of actions.
zh: 最后，粗颗粒观与细颗粒观显然并未穷尽概念版图。不少哲学家提出了个别化原则，比粗颗粒理论家提出的更严格，又比细颗粒理论家提出的更宽松（如 Ginet 1990）[^ginet-1990]。例如 Charles（1984）论证：亚里士多德会按能力来个别化行动。这使我们可以说：手的移动与快速地移动手是同一个行动（因为由此实现的是单一能力），尽管它与下毒是不同的行动——后者实现的是另一组能力。这一观点的挑战在于：给出一个独立于行动个别化说明的能力个别化说明。

en: 5.3 The Debate Over Basic Action
zh: 5.3 关于基本行动的争论

en: Consideration of cases like that of the pumper naturally raises a question about their *structure*: what kind of shape could such a rationalizing explanation take? Could it go on forever? To answer this, consider the pumper once more, and suppose he poisons the inhabitants of the house. It is true, then, that he poisoned the inhabitants of the house by pumping water, and he did this by moving his hands. Because the poisoning and the pumping are done by doing something else, they are called “non-basic” actions. However, it has been argued that there must be at least some actions that are “basic’”, done not by doing anything else. Otherwise, we appear to be caught in various forms of a vicious regress.
zh: 对水泵工这类案例的考虑，自然引出关于其 ** 结构 ** 的问题：这样一种合理化解释可能具有什么样的形状？它能永远继续下去吗？为回答这一点，再次考虑水泵工，并设想他毒害了屋里的人。为真的是：他通过抽水毒害了屋里的人，而他又通过移动自己的手这样做。因为下毒与抽水是通过做别的事完成的，它们被称为“非基本”行动。然而，有人论证：必须至少有一些“基本”行动——不通过做任何别的事而完成的行动。否则，我们似乎陷入各种形式的恶性倒退。

en: For example, if to do *A* one must do *B*, and to do *B* one must do *C*, and so on *ad infinitum,* doing anything would seem to require doing an infinite number of things. More worrying, the beginning of action seems to be “logically out of reach” for the agent, since there is always something else that she would have to do before she begins to do anything (Danto 1979, 471)[^danto-1979]. Again, it seems that for an agent to know what she is currently doing, she needs to know how to do the things by which she does it; but unless there is something that she can know how to do just by doing it, it will be impossible for her to know what she is doing at all (Hornsby 2013)[^hornsby-2013].
zh: 例如，如果做 *A* 必须先做 *B*，做 *B* 必须先做 *C*，如此 *ad infinitum*，那么做任何事似乎都需要做无限多件事。更令人担忧的是，行动的开端对行动者而言似乎“在逻辑上不可及”：在开始做任何事之前，总有另一件她必须先做的事（Danto 1979, 471）[^danto-1979]。再者，行动者要知道自己现在在做什么，似乎就需要知道她借以做此事的那些事怎么做；但除非有某种她仅仅通过做它就知道怎么做的东西，她就不可能知道自己在做什么（Hornsby 2013）[^hornsby-2013]。

en: Arguments of this sort convinced most scholars that there must be basic actions (though see Baier 1971 and Sneddon 2001 for early dissent)[^baier-1971][^sneddon-2001]. The debate then centered on *which* actions are basic. Many scholars held that simple bodily movements, like moving a finger or raising an eyebrow, were basic, while others held that they could be more complex (tying one’s shoes), or that they must be simpler: perhaps only mental actions, or tryings were basic. After all, I move my finger by attempting to move it; and we need to distinguish between the attempt and the movement, since sometimes the attempt occurs without the movement (e.g. if my fingers are suddenly paralized) (Prichard 1945: Hornsby 1980; O’Shaughnessy 1980; see Cleveland 1997, ch.5 for criticism)[^cleveland-1997][^hornsby-1980][^o’shaughnessy-1980][^prichard-1945].
zh: 这类论证使大多数学者相信必须有基本行动（但早期异议见 Baier 1971 与 Sneddon 2001）[^baier-1971][^sneddon-2001]。争论于是聚焦于 ** 哪些 ** 行动是基本的。许多学者主张简单的身体移动——如移动一根手指或扬一下眉毛——是基本的；另一些人主张它们可以更复杂（系鞋带），或者必须更简单：或许只有心理行动，或尝试（tryings）才是基本的。毕竟，我通过试图移动手指而移动它；而且我们需要区分尝试与移动，因为有时尝试发生而移动没有发生（例如如果我的手指突然瘫痪）（Prichard 1945; Hornsby 1980; O'Shaughnessy 1980；批评见 Cleveland 1997, ch.5）[^cleveland-1997][^hornsby-1980][^o'shaughnessy-1980][^prichard-1945]。

en: As several scholars have noted, part of what is at issue in this debate are different notions of basicness, corresponding to different understandings of the clause “by doing something else” (Baier 1971; Annas 1978; Hornsby 1980)[^annas-1978][^baier-1971][^hornsby-1980]. It is common to draw a three-fold distinction: (i) know-how basicness; (ii) causal basicness; and (iii) teleological basicness. An action is know-how basic iff there is no other (type of) action by which the agent knows how to do the one in question. An action is causally basic iff there is no other (token) action that causes it. An action is teleologically basic iff there is no other (token) action by means of which the agent does it. To illustrate in a way that highlights the differences, consider pitching a baseball. Arguably, this action is know-how basic, since the pitcher may not know a more basic action by which to do it: of course, the agent may know how to move her hands independently, but she may be unable to move her hands in the particular way in which she does when she throws the baseball unless she were actually throwing the baseball. Whether the action is causally basic depends on whether we think there is another action that causes it, such as the pitcher’s moving of his hands. Finally, and independently of the question of causation, the action appears to be teleologically non-basic, since the moving of his hands is certainly both a means and an action by which the pitcher pitches. The consensus for many years was that there must be basic actions in all three senses.
zh: 正如多位学者指出的，这场争论的部分症结在于“基本性”的不同概念，对应于“通过做别的事”这一从句的不同理解（Baier 1971; Annas 1978; Hornsby 1980）[^annas-1978][^baier-1971][^hornsby-1980]。常见的三分是：(i) 知其如何的基本性；(ii) 因果的基本性；(iii) 目的论的基本性。一个行动是知其如何地基本的，当且仅当没有别的（类型的）行动，行动者借以知道如何做所论行动。一个行动是因果地基本的，当且仅当没有别的（个例）行动引起它。一个行动是目的论地基本的，当且仅当没有别的（个例）行动，行动者借以做它。为凸显差别而举例：考虑投掷棒球。可以说，这一行动是知其如何地基本的，因为投手可能不知道借以做它的更基本行动：当然，行动者可能知道如何独立地移动自己的手，但除非她真的在投球，她可能无法以投棒球时那种特定方式移动自己的手。该行动是否因果地基本，取决于我们是否认为有另一个行动引起它，如投手的手的移动。最后，独立于因果问题，该行动似乎是目的论上非基本的，因为手的移动无疑是投手投球的一个手段，也是一个借以投球的行动。多年的共识是：在所有三种意义上都必须有基本行动。

en: However, this widespread consensus about teleological basicness has recently been called into question by Michael Thompson and other defenders of “naive” action theory (Thompson 2008, 107–119)[^thompson-2008]. Thompson considers the case of a person, *P,* who has pushed a stone from point α to ω. Let β be the halfway point between α and ω. It seems that if *P* pushed the stone from α to ω intentionally, then he pushed the stone from α to β intentionally. Now, let γ be the halfway point between α and β. Once again, it seems that *P* pushed the stone from α to γ intentionally. And so on. It seems, then, that there will always be a further action by which *P* pushed the stone. In other words, there is no basic action. Moreover, as a number of authors have noted (Small 2012; Lavin 2013)[^small-2012], the argument can be generalized for virtually every action, since it can be presented in terms of a series of time-segments (instead of place-segments), and virtually every action takes place over time. (For critical discussion, see Ford 2018.)[^ford-2018]
zh: 然而，这一关于目的论基本性的广泛共识，近来受到 Michael Thompson 与其他“素朴”行动理论辩护者的质疑（Thompson 2008, 107–119）[^thompson-2008]。汤普森考虑了一个人 *P* 把一块石头从 α 点推到 ω 点的情形。设 β 是 α 与 ω 的中点。似乎，如果 *P* 有意地把石头从 α 推到 ω，那么他也有意地把石头从 α 推到了 β。再设 γ 是 α 与 β 的中点。又一次，似乎 *P* 有意地把石头从 α 推到了 γ。如此等等。看来，总会有 *P* 借以推石头的进一步行动。换言之，没有基本行动。此外，正如多位作者指出的（Small 2012; Lavin 2013）[^small-2012]，该论证可以推广到几乎每一个行动，因为它可以用一系列时间段（代替地点段）来呈现，而几乎每个行动都在时间中展开。（批判性讨论见 Ford 2018。）[^ford-2018]

en: Building on this argument, Lavin (2013) presents a further challenge to the view that there must be (teleological) basic action. Lavin’s argument centers on the relation of the agent to her actions. Consider first a non-basic action, like poisoning the inhabitants of the house. The agent’s relation to this action is itself an agential matter, since the agent poisons the inhabitants by doing something else intentionally (operating the pump). Now consider an arbitrary basic action, *A*. By definition, the agent doesn’t do *A* by doing anything else. However, this is an action that occurs through time, so, presumably there are happenings *h₁, h₂, …, hₙ* by which *A* takes place. But since *h₁, h₂, …, hₙ* are mere happenings, this means that the agent relates to *A* non-agentially. Now, Lavin grants that it may be possible sometimes for us to relate to our actions non-agentially; but it would be alarming if this was necessarily the case, as defenders of basic action are committed to hold. It would mean that agents are necessarily alienated from their actions, in the way labourers are alienated from their labour in Marx’s critique of capitalism. In turn, Lavin argues that this would make it impossible for agents to have self-knowledge of their own actions, since self-knowledge is grounded on our agential relation.
zh: 基于这一论证，Lavin（2013）对“必须有（目的论上）基本行动”提出了进一步的挑战。Lavin 的论证聚焦于行动者与其行动的关系。先考虑一个非基本行动，如毒害屋里的人。行动者与这一行动的关系本身就是行动者性的，因为行动者通过有意地做别的事（操作水泵）来毒害屋中人。现在考虑一个任意的基本行动 *A*。按定义，行动者不通过做任何别的事来 *A*。然而，这是一个在时间中展开的行动，所以，presumably 存在发生 *h₁, h₂, …, hₙ*，*A* 借之发生。但既然 *h₁, h₂, …, hₙ* 只是发生，这就意味着行动者以非行动者性的方式关联于 *A*。Lavin 承认，我们有时可能以非行动者性的方式关联于我们的行动；但基本行动的辩护者所承诺的是：这必然如此——这就令人警觉了。它将意味着：行动者必然与自己的行动异化，就像马克思对资本主义的批评中劳动者与劳动的异化。反过来，Lavin 论证：这将使行动者不可能拥有对自己行动的自我认识，因为自我认识奠基于我们的行动者性关系。

en: There is a growing literature responding to Thompson’s and Lavin’s challenges, both refining the arguments, or presenting objections to it (Setiya 2012; Hornsby 2013; Lynch 2017; Frost 2019; Small 2019)[^frost-2019][^hornsby-2013][^lynch-2017][^setiya-2012][^small-2019]. This is not surprising, since the debate about basic actions has important repercussions for other questions about the nature of intentional action. For example, Lavin (2013) holds that defenders of (teleologically) basic action are committed to a “decompositional account” of agency (see section 1). After all, if there are basic actions, we may be able to give an account of what makes something an action in terms of the non-agential relation an agent bears to her basic actions. Moreover, Ford (2017; 2018) notes that Thompson’s argument suggests a novel way to pursue action theory, one that defines action not in terms of *reasons for action* but, in the first instance, in terms of the means by which an action is pursued.The latter, Ford holds, better captures the agential perspective: in the context of deliberation, what the agent asks is *How* to pursue a particular course of action, rather than *Why* she is doing something. Finally, the debate may have repercussions for our understanding of the relation between skill and intentional action. For example, both Frost and Small suggest that at the most fundamental level, our agency depends on our exercise of practical *skills* by which we enter an instrumental order without consciously representing that order at the level of propositional thought (Small 2012; 2019; Frost 2019)[^frost-2019][^small-2012].
zh: 回应汤普森与 Lavin 挑战的文献在增长：或精炼论证，或提出反对（Setiya 2012; Hornsby 2013; Lynch 2017; Frost 2019; Small 2019）[^frost-2019][^hornsby-2013][^lynch-2017][^setiya-2012][^small-2019]。这并不奇怪，因为基本行动的论辩对关于有意行动本性的其他问题有重要反响。例如，Lavin（2013）主张（目的论上）基本行动的辩护者承诺了一种能动性的“分解式说明”（见第 1 节）。毕竟，如果有基本行动，我们也许能够以行动者与其基本行动之间的非行动者性关系，来说明是什么使某物成为行动。此外，Ford（2017; 2018）指出：汤普森的论证提示了一种追求行动理论的新方式——不以 ** 行动的理由 ** 定义行动，而首先以行动被追求的 ** 手段 ** 来定义。福特认为，后者更好地捕捉了行动者的视角：在慎思的语境中，行动者问的是 ** 如何 ** pursuing 某个特定的行动路线，而不是她 ** 为什么 ** 在做某事。最后，这场争论可能对我们理解技能与有意行动之关系有反响。例如，Frost 与 Small 都提出：在最根本的层面，我们的能动性依赖于我们对实践 ** 技能 ** 的施行——我们借此进入一个工具秩序，而不在命题思想的层面有意识地表象那个秩序（Small 2012; 2019; Frost 2019）[^frost-2019][^small-2012]。

en: 5.4 Making, Acting, and the Varieties of Agency
zh: 5.4 制作、行动与能动性的诸形态

en: Nearly all contemporary philosophers treat *intentional action* as a unified category. Despite the many differences between moving a finger, running, hammering a nail, fixing a fridge, eating a sandwich, acting justly, keeping a promise, and marrying someone, all of these are treated as equally belonging to a single type: acting. The assumption is supported by natural language. After all, these are all legitimate answers to the question ‘What are you doing?’.
zh: 几乎所有的当代哲学家都把 ** 有意行动 ** 当作统一的范畴。尽管移动一根手指、跑步、钉钉子、修冰箱、吃三明治、公正地行动、守约、与人结婚之间差异多多，所有这些都被当作同等地属于单一类型：行动。这一假定得到自然语言的支持。毕竟，对“你在做什么？”这一问题，这些都是合法的回答。

en: Aristotle provides us with an alternative view that has had immense influence in philosophy. Throughout his writings, Aristotle distinguishes between “making” or “producing” (*poíêsis)* on the one hand, and “acting proper” (*praxis*) on the other (an early version of the distinction appears in Plato’s *Charmides* 163a–c). The two are distinguished by their success conditions (*EE* 5.2/*NE* 6.2 1139b1–4; *EE* 5.5/*NE* 6.5 1140b6–7). The success conditions for makings are external to them: one succeeds at making insofar as something external to the making obtains (the product). By contrast, the success conditions for proper actions are the actions themselves. This is why we pursue them for their own sake (*ib.*). By this standard, the activities of hammering a nail, or fixing a fridge count as makings, because the hammering is successful insofar as something external takes place: a nail is hammered in a wall, or a fridge is fixed. Precisely because the success conditions are external, it is possible to succeed at making something by luck (*EE* 5.4/*NE* 6.4 1140a17–20). By contrast, Aristotle would regard acting justly, keeping a promise, or marrying someone as proper actions. To succeed at these actions consists in doing the actions well. A coerced marriage is not a successful marriage. Hence, these actions cannot be done by luck. This distinction underlies the aforementioned distinction between two forms of human excellence in the practical sphere: skill (*technê*) is excellence at making (*EE* 5.4; *NE* 6.4 1140a6–23), and practical wisdom (*phronêsis*) is excellence at acting proper (*EE* 5.5/ *NE* 6.5 1140a25–30 et passim).
zh: 亚里士多德为我们提供了一种在哲学中影响巨大的替代看法。在其著作中，亚里士多德区分“制作”（*poíêsis*）与“狭义行动”（*praxis*）（该区分的早期版本见于柏拉图《查米德斯》163a–c）。两者由其成功条件区分（*EE* 5.2/*NE* 6.2 1139b1–4; *EE* 5.5/*NE* 6.5 1140b6–7）。制作的成功条件外在于制作：制作的某物成功，在于某种外在于该制作的东西成立（产品）。相比之下，狭义行动的成功条件就是行动本身。这就是为什么我们为其自身之故而追求它们（同上）。按这一标准，钉钉子或修冰箱的活动算作制作，因为钉的成功在于某种外在的东西发生：一枚钉子被钉入墙，或一台冰箱被修好。正因为成功条件是外在的，靠运气做成制作是可能的（*EE* 5.4/*NE* 6.4 1140a17–20）。相比之下，亚里士多德会把公正地行动、守约、或与人结婚视为狭义行动。做成这些行动在于把这些行动做好。一场被胁迫的婚姻不是一场成功的婚姻。因此，这些行动不能靠运气完成。这一区分奠定了实践领域中两种人类卓越的区分：技艺（*technê*）是制作的卓越（*EE* 5.4; *NE* 6.4 1140a6–23），而实践智慧（*phronêsis*）是狭义行动的卓越（*EE* 5.5/ *NE* 6.5 1140a25–30 et passim）。

en: Although the distinction is barely mentioned in analytical philosophy, it has influenced other traditions, such as the Marxist one. From his earliest writings, Marx accepts an Aristotelian threefold analysis of labour in terms of the labourer, the process of labouring, and its product. Marx implicitly rejects the distinction between action proper and production, in favour of a dichotomy of his own between different forms of productions. This is because for Marx the characteristic activity of the human species is conscious free labouring: an activity that has no end beyond itself (it does not seek anything beyond the living activity that such labouring consists in) (Marx 1844a; 1844b; 1867)[^marx-1844a]. This is what Aristotle took as the distinguishing feature of proper actions, done for their own sake. One of Marx’s central criticisms of capitalist societies is that it prevents humans from engaging in such an activity. In capitalist societies, the labourer, the labour process, and the product all become commodities that serve as mere means for the enjoyment of the owner of labour and product (“the capitalist”). Members of capitalist societies are, in this sense, alienated (Marx 1844b; 1867)[^marx-1844b]. As such, capitalist societies make it impossible for humans to engage in their most fundamental life activity of free production, an activity that the Marxist tradition came to designate as “praxis” (Petrovic 1983)[^petrovic-1983], reappropriating the quite different Aristotelian notion.
zh: 虽然这一区分在分析哲学中很少被提及，它影响了别的传统，如马克思主义传统。从最早的著作起，马克思就接受了亚里士多德按劳动者、劳动过程与劳动产品对劳动的三分分析。马克思隐含地拒斥狭义行动与生产之分，代之以他自己关于不同生产形式的二分。这是因为对马克思而言，人类的特征性活动是自觉的自由劳动：一种没有超出自身之外的目的的活动（它不寻求超出这种劳动所构成的活的活∈之外的任何东西）（Marx 1844a; 1844b; 1867）[^marx-1844a]。这正是亚里士多德视为为其自身之故而做的狭义行动的标志性特征。马克思对资本主义社会的核心批评之一是：它阻止人类从事这类活动。在资本主义社会中，劳动者、劳动过程与产品都变成商品，只是劳动与产品之所有者（“资本家”）享乐的单纯手段。在这个意义上，资本主义社会的成员是异化的（Marx 1844b; 1867）[^marx-1844b]。如此，资本主义社会使人类无法从事其最根本的生命活动——自由生产；马克思主义传统后来重新占用亚里士多德那个颇不相同的观念，把这种活动称为“实践”（praxis）（Petrovic 1983）[^petrovic-1983]。

en: Perhaps the most influential modern version of a distinction among types of practical activity is drawn by Arendt (1998). Arendt distinguishes between three kinds of practical activities: labour, work, and action. The most basic of these is *labour*, which Arendt conceives as simply an extension of our animal lives: a “metabolism” (Marx’s phrase) between the human animal and the world, characterized by a cycle of consumption and the production of goods to be consumed, and aiming at meeting our basic biological needs (p.69). Since this is a cycle, Arendt suggests that there is no sense of speaking here of means and ends: there is no fact of the matter as to whether the production of goods is for the sake of consumption, or the consumption for the sake of production (p.145; 155). Means and ends enter at the next level of practical activity, *work* (the Aristotelian *poíêsis*). Like Aristotle, Arendt takes the aim of working to be the finished work, the product, whether it be a work of art, like a painting, a tool, like a knife, or a way to safeguard living, like a house. The central importance of work lies in its ability to produce lasting products that lie beyond the activity of the producer (p.136; 144). Arendt contends that these products can begin to shape an objective *world* of objects that stands against the humans who produce them. However, the world does not emerge in its fullness except by way of the third level of practical activity, *action* (the Aristotelian *praxis*). Action is the means by which humans reveal themselves in the public sphere, a revelation needed to give reality to a personality that otherwise remains entirely unactualized in subjectivity. It is thus essentially communicative, and depends on other humans to whom one might make herself known (pp.38–49; 95; 202–7); and it depends, given its essential ephemeral nature, for its permanence in the continued existence of a polity that may preserve words and deeds in more enduring forms, like sculptures and tales. Ungoverned by either the natural laws of labor, or by the norms arising from a particular aim, action is for Arendt unproductive, free, and unpredictable. It is the distinguishing activity of human beings as such (p.177; 204–6).
zh: 也许最有影响的现代版实践活动类型区分，由阿伦特（1998）做出。阿伦特区分三种实践活动：劳动、工作与行动。其中最基本的是 ** 劳动 **，阿伦特把它构想为我们的动物生命的单纯延伸：人类动物与世界之间的一种“新陈代谢”（马克思的用语），以消费与生产供消费之物品的循环为特征，旨在满足我们基本的生物需要（p.69）。既然这是一个循环，阿伦特提示：在这里谈论手段与目的是无意义的：物品的生产是为了消费、还是消费为了生产，并无事实可言（p.145; 155）。手段与目的进入实践活动的下一层次：** 工作 ** （（即亚里士多德的 *poíêsis*）。与亚里士多德一样，阿伦特认为工作的目标在于完成的作品，即产品——无论是一件艺术品（如一幅画）、一件工具（如一把刀），还是一种保障生活的方式（如一座房子）。工作的核心重要性在于：它能够产出持存的产品，超出生产者的活动之外（p.136; 144）。阿伦特主张，这些产品可以开始塑造一个客观的 ** 世界 **——一个与生产它们的人类相抗衡的对象世界。然而，世界只有通过第三层次的实践活动——** 行动 ** （（亚里士多德的 *praxis*）——才充分涌现。行动是人类在公共领域中显现自身的手段；这种显现是必要的，它赋予人格以实在性——否则人格将全然滞留于主观性中不得实现。因此行动在本质上是交往性的，依赖于其他人——人们可以向其显现自身（pp.38–49; 95; 202–7）；而且，鉴于其本质上的短暂性，行动的持存依赖于一个政体的延续存在——后者可以把言行保存于更耐久的形式，如雕塑与故事。行动不受劳动的自然规律支配，也不受来自特定目的的规范支配；对阿伦特而言，行动是无生产性的、自由的、不可预测的。它是人类作为人类的标志性活动（p.177; 204–6）。

en: The three-fold distinction serves as the basis for Arendt’s criticisms of both ancient writers, including Aristotle, and modern writers, including Marx. She criticizes Aristotle both for inconsistently assimilating action too much to work/production in his analysis of benefaction as producing a work (*ergon*) (p.196), and for subordinating it to theory (22–23). She criticizes Marx’s subsumption of practical activity in general under labour for its failure to provide meaning. She notes that Marx ends in the paradoxical position of concluding that that the aim of labour is freedom from labour, even though this is the activity he takes as definitive of humanity. In other words, Marx ends up concluding that the aim of human life is to do away with human life (p.89; 103; 105). For Arendt, however, this is not merely a theoretical deficiency, but a manifestation of a broader social tendency that goes back to Plato: the tendency to try to make action proper into that which is not—whether work or labour—to control what is essentially unpredictable and free.
zh: 这一三分区分是阿伦特批评古今作家的基础——包括亚里士多德与马克思。她批评亚里士多德在把善举分析为制作一件作品（*ergon*）时不一致地过度把行动同化于工作/生产（p.196），又批评他把行动置于理论之下（22–23）。她批评马克思把一般实践活动归并于劳动——因为这无法提供意义。她指出：马克思最终落入一个悖论性的立场——得出劳动的目的是从劳动中解放的结论，尽管劳动正是他视为规定人性的活动。换言之，马克思最终得出的结论是：人类生活的目的是废除人类生活（p.89; 103; 105）。对阿伦特而言，这不只是一个理论缺陷，而是一种更广的社会倾向的表现，这种倾向可回溯到柏拉图：试图把狭义行动变成其所不是的东西——无论是工作还是劳动——以控制本质上不可预测且自由的东西。

en: The problems of subsuming practical activity in general to making find echoes in some contemporary thinkers. For example, Thompson (2008), following Baier (1970) and Mueller (1979), criticizes attempts like Castañeda’s (1970) and Chisholm’s (1970) of construing actions in terms of a schemas such as ‘bringing it about that *p*’; such propositional complexes, according to critics, threaten to undermine the practical form of the thought they mean to capture (cf. Hornsby 2016, Wilson 1980, pp.111–117 for further discussion)[^hornsby-2016][^wilson-1980]. Arendt herself thought that this tendency underlay the attraction of utilitarianism, but she argued that, like Marxism, that view was incapable of ever giving further meaning to our practical endeavours (p.105). Korsgaard concludes with equal severity that given a distinction between praxis and poíêsis, “utilitarianism is not a moral theory, for utility is a property of [productions], not actions” (2009, p.18n26).
zh: 把一般实践活动归并于制作的诸问题，在一些当代思想家那里有回响。例如 Thompson（2008）跟随 Baier（1970）与 Mueller（1979），批评 Castañeda（1970）与 Chisholm（1970）以“使 *p* 得以发生”这类图式来解读行动的尝试；按批评者的说法，这类命题复合体有损于它们意欲捕捉的思想的实践形式（进一步讨论参见 Hornsby 2016, Wilson 1980, pp.111–117）[^hornsby-2016][^wilson-1980]。阿伦特本人认为这种倾向是功利主义之吸引力的基础，但她论证：与马克思主义一样，那一观点永远无法为我们的实践努力给出进一步的意义（p.105）。Korsgaard 以同样的严厉下结论说：鉴于 praxis 与 poíêsis 之分，“功利主义不是一种道德理论，因为效用是［产品］的属性，而非行动的属性”（2009, p.18n26）。

en: Regardless of what one thinks of these arguments, it is evident that the question whether practical activity comes in varieties, as Aristotle and Arendt thought, is potentially of enormous significance.
zh: 无论人们如何看待这些论证，显而易见的是：实践活动是否如亚里士多德与阿伦特所想的那样有类型之分，这一问题的潜在意义是巨大的。

en: 6. Constitutive Aim
zh: 6 构成性目的

en: The question of what, if anything, is the constitutive (or formal) aim (or end) of intentional actions is a question about whether there is anything that all actions necessarily pursue, irrespective of their particular ends. Some philosophers (Setiya 2016b)[^setiya-2016b] deny that there is a constitutive aim of acting or that there is something that every action as such aims at. On this view, there is no such thing as an aim contained in acting as such; each action just aims at its particular end. On the other hand, many philosophers try to derive important consequences for ethics from the idea that action or agency has a constitutive aim. However, we will leave aside the examinations of these claims and focus only on the question as it pertains to the characterization of agency. (Cf. Bagnoli 2017; 2022.)[^bagnoli-2017]
zh: 有意行动的构成性（或形式的）目的（或目标）是什么——如果有的话——这是一个关于是否存在任何一切行动都必然追求的东西的问题，不管它们的具体目的为何。一些哲学家（Setiya 2016b）[^setiya-2016b]否认行动有构成性目的、或存在每个行动 *qua* 行动都以之为目标的东西。按这种看法，不存在包含在行动本身之中的目的；每个行动只是以其特定目的为目标。另一方面，许多哲学家试图从“行动或能动性有一个构成性目的”这一观念为伦理学推出重要后果。不过，我们将把对这些主张的考察搁置一旁，只聚焦与能动性之刻画相关的问题。（参见 Bagnoli 2017; 2022。）[^bagnoli-2017]

en: 6.1 Motivations and Different Versions of the View
zh: 6.1 动机与该观点的不同版本

en: What could motivate the idea that actions have a constitutive aim above and beyond the particular ends they pursue? An important consideration is that, arguably, only by appealing to a constitutive aim, can we evaluate actions and have a proper standard of practical reason. Much in the same way that the aim of belief (generally thought to be “truth” or “knowledge”) might provide a standard for theoretical reasoning and correct belief, a constitutive aim of action would provide a standard for practical reasoning and successful action. More specifically, it seems that some actions are successful in achieving their particular ends and yet are cases of practical failures in some deeper way, exhibiting what appears like practical irrationality or at least some form of practical ignorance. Suppose I have dreamt all my life to move to Seattle, and I finally secured a position in the city. However, as I arrive in Seattle and try to arrange my life, my life in Seattle is a great disappointment; even though there is nothing important that I found out about Seattle that I didn’t know already, I completely regret having pursued this end. Although I achieved my aim of moving to Seattle, my actions seem to have failed in an important way; arguably, I manifested my agency in a defective way.
zh: 什么东西可以激发“行动有一个超出其所追求的具体目的之外的构成性目的”这一观念？一个重要的考量是：可以说，只有诉诸一个构成性目的，我们才能评价行动并拥有一个正当的实践理性标准。正如信念的目的（一般认为是“真”或“知识”）可以为理论推理与正确信念提供标准，行动的构成性目的将为实践推理与成功的行动提供标准。更具体地说，似乎有些行动在实现其特定目的上是成功的，却在某种更深的意义上是实践失败的案例，表现出看似实践上的不合理性、或至少某种形式的实践无知。设想我一生梦想搬到西雅图，而我终于在该城谋得一个职位。然而，当我抵达西雅图并开始安排我的生活时，西雅图的生活令我大失所望；即便没有任何关于西雅图的重要新发现——都是我早已知道的——我完全后悔追求这一目的。虽然我实现了搬去西雅图的目的，我的行动似乎以一种重要的方式失败了；可以说，我以有缺陷的方式显现了我的能动性。

en: Of course, one can explain my disappointment in many ways that do not seem to presuppose a constitutive aim of action: there were other ends that I had that conflict with moving to Seattle and I hadn’t fully appreciated this beforehand. Perhaps I no longer care about the things that made me want to move to Seattle; moving to Seattle was a means to ends I had abandoned and didn’t realize that it made no longer sense to pursue this end. But it is unclear that these observations will suffice; it seems that none of this might have happened and yet my move to Seattle was still a practical failure.
zh: 当然，可以用许多不预设行动之构成性目的的方式来解释我的失望：我有其他与搬去西雅图相冲突的目的，而我事先没有充分意识到这一点。也许我不再在意那些使我想搬去西雅图的东西；搬去西雅图是我已放弃的目的的手段，而我没有意识到追求它已不再有意义。但不清楚这些观察是否足够；似乎可能这一切都没有发生，而我搬去西雅图仍然是一次实践失败。

en: Let us take a concrete example: suppose the constitutive aim of action is happiness (see Frey 2019 for an argument that this is a view held by Aquinas). On this view, then, every action (directly or indirectly) aims at happiness, and the realization of an end that does not result in happiness is a shortcoming of my agency. Therefore, if my going to Seattle did not contribute to my happiness, or if, worse, it contributed to undermining it, then it was a defective case of agency. This failure is often thought to parallel the kind of internal failure involved in false beliefs: such beliefs supposedly fail to meet a standard internal to theoretical cognition.
zh: 让我们取一个具体例子：设想行动的构成性目的是幸福（关于阿奎那持此看法的论证见 Frey 2019）。按这种看法，每个行动（直接或间接）都以幸福为目标，而实现一个不导致幸福的目的，就是我的能动性的一个缺陷。因此，如果我搬去西雅图没有增进我的幸福，或者更糟，损害了它，那么它就是一个有缺陷的能动性案例。这种失败常被认为平行于假信念所涉的那种内在失败：这类信念据说未能满足理论认知内在固有的标准。

en: Another, related, way to motivate the idea that action has a constitutive aim focuses on the standpoint of deliberation. When deliberating about what to do, it seems that I need to find an answer to the question “what to do” or “whether to φ” (Hieronymi 2005; 2006; Shah 2008)[^hieronymi-2005][^shah-2008]; in the good case, my action expresses an adequate answer to this question. But how could I go about answering these questions if action did not have a constitutive aim; if there’s nothing that could count as the correct way of answering this question? Similarly, from the point of view of action explanation, some answers seem to provide an intelligible explanation of action while others seem to invite the question “but why would you aim at (want) *that*?” If you ask me “Why are we eating the jello?”, “Because it is blue” seems to invite further questions, while “Because I find the taste pleasant” brings the inquiry to an end. Anscombe argues that the search for further explanations ends when we hit a “desirability characterization”, something that is not just conceived as good but “*really* … one of the many forms of the good” (Anscombe 1957, §40)[^anscombe-1957].
zh: 激发“行动有构成性目的”的另一条相关路径，聚焦于慎思的立场。当慎思要做什么时，似乎我需要找到“做什么”或“是否 φ”的问题的答案（Hieronymi 2005; 2006; Shah 2008）[^hieronymi-2005][^shah-2008]；在良好的情形中，我的行动表达了对该问题的充分回答。但如果行动没有构成性目的——如果没有任何东西可以算作回答这一问题的正确方式——我怎么能着手回答这些问题？类似地，从行动解释的观点看，有些答案似乎给出对行动的可理解的解释，而另一些则似乎引出“可你为什么会以（想要）** 那个 ** 为目标？”的问题。如果你问我“我们为什么在吃果冻？”，“因为它是蓝色的”似乎会引出更多问题，而“因为我觉得味道好”则终结了追问。安斯康姆论证：对进一步解释的追寻，当我们碰到一个“可欲性刻画”时终结——某种不只是被想成好的东西，而是“** 实在地 **……善的众多形式之一”（Anscombe 1957, §40）[^anscombe-1957]。

en: There seems to be a parallel structure in the case of belief: in deliberating about what to believe, it seems that I must be similarly guided by an ideal of correct belief (Shah and Velleman 2006)[^shah-2006]. In fact, philosophers who accept that there is a constitutive aim of action often compare action and belief (Velleman 1992; 1996; Tenenbaum 2007; 2012; 2018b; Schafer 2013)[^schafer-2013][^tenenbaum-2007]. Belief is supposed to have truth as its constitutive aim, and just as belief is held, at least in the good case, in accordance with this constitutive aim (as Hume 1748 said, “a wise man … proportions his belief to the evidence”)[^hume-1748], intentional agency is guided by its constitutive aim.
zh: 信念的情形似乎有平行的结构：在慎思该相信什么时，似乎我同样必须受正确信念之理想的引导（Shah and Velleman 2006）[^shah-2006]。事实上，接受行动有构成性目的的哲学家，常把行动与信念相比（Velleman 1992; 1996; Tenenbaum 2007; 2012; 2018b; Schafer 2013）[^schafer-2013][^tenenbaum-2007]。信念被设定以真为其构成性目的，而正如信念至少在良好情形中按这一构成性目的而被持有（如休谟 1748 所说，“一个明智的人……按证据来配比其信念”）[^hume-1748]，有意的能动性也受其构成性目的引导。

en: There are various proposals of what the constitutive aim of an action might be. Perhaps the most traditional version of this view is the idea that the good is the constitutive aim of agency, possibly going back to Socrates (*Protagoras* 351a–8e; *Gorgias* 467c–8d). The notion of “good” involved here can be very thin, meaning no more than “considering matters aright” (Williams 1981)[^williams-1981] in the realm of practical reason; such views are versions of the thesis often called “the guise of the good” (Tenenbaum 2007; Clark 2010; Schafer 2013)[^clark-2010][^schafer-2013][^tenenbaum-2007]. According to the guise of the good, if I φ intentionally, then I must take φ-ing to be good. Arguably some other versions of the constitutive aim of agency are specifications of the thin notion of “good” or “human good” (see Boyle and Lavin 2010)[^boyle-2010]. Other constitutive aims that have been defended in literature are self-understanding or autonomy (Velleman 1989; 1992; 1996; 2009)[^velleman-1989], self-constitution (Korsgaard 1996; 2008; 2009)[^korsgaard-1996], and the will to power (Katsafanas 2013)[^katsafanas-2013].
zh: 关于行动的构成性目的可能是什么，有各种提案。这一看法最传统的版本或许是：善是能动性的构成性目的——可能上溯到苏格拉底（*Protagoras* 351a–8e; *Gorgias* 467c–8d）。这里所涉的“善”概念可以很薄，在实践理性的领域里不外乎“恰当地考虑事情”（Williams 1981）[^williams-1981]；这类观点是常被称为“善之貌”（the guise of the good）的论题的版本（Tenenbaum 2007; Clark 2010; Schafer 2013）[^clark-2010][^schafer-2013][^tenenbaum-2007]。按善之貌，如果我有意地 φ，那么我必须把 φ-ing 当作好的。可以说，能动性之构成性目的的其他版本是“善”或“人类善”这一薄概念的细化（见 Boyle and Lavin 2010）[^boyle-2010]。文献中得到辩护的其他构成性目的还有：自我理解或自律（Velleman 1989; 1992; 1996; 2009）[^velleman-1989]、自我构成（Korsgaard 1996; 2008; 2009）[^korsgaard-1996]、以及权力意志（Katsafanas 2013）[^katsafanas-2013]。

en: 6.2 Objections
zh: 6.2 反对意见

en: A number of challenges have been raised in the literature to the claim that there must be a constitutive aim of action. First, suppose we accept the causal theory of action: an intentional action just is the effect of a “primary reason”. On such a view, it seems that an intentional action is constituted by its causal antecedents, rather than by a necessary aim that one has in acting. However, causal theories are not incompatible with constitutivism. Since on these views, some of the causal antecedents of the action will be conative states (like an intention), the question of whether intentional action has a constitutive aim will depend on whether the conative state has a constitutive aim or whether a specific conative state must always figure on the genesis of intentional action. For instance, in Velleman’s early work (for instance, Velleman 1989)[^velleman-1989], intentional action was an action that was caused by a desire for self-knowledge, and the content of such a desire was thus the constitutive aim of agency. Smith (2013; 2015; 2019) also develops a form of constitutivism that endorses the standard story of action.
zh: 文献中已对“行动必须有构成性目的”提出若干挑战。第一，设想我们接受行动的因果理论：有意行动恰恰就是“原初理由”的结果。按这种看法，有意行动由其因果前项构成，而非由行动中的一个必然目的构成。不过，因果理论与构成论并不不相容。既然按这些看法，行动的某些因果前项将是意动状态（如意图），有意行动是否有构成性目的的问题，就取决于意动状态是否有构成性目的、或是否一个特定的意动状态必须总是出现在有意行动的生成之中。例如，在 Velleman 的早期著作中（例如 Velleman 1989）[^velleman-1989]，有意行动是由对自我认识的欲望引起的行动，该欲望的内容因而就是能动性的构成性目的。Smith（2013; 2015; 2019）也发展了一种认可行动标准故事的构成论。

en: Setiya raises a couple of important challenges to the idea that action has a constitutive aim. According to Setiya (2007), any theory of action needs to account for the fact that practical knowledge (or a belief condition in his version; see section 4 of this entry) is essential to intentional action. However, the belief condition seems to be conceptually independent of any constitutive aim of action, and thus accepting that both are constitutive of intentional action amounts to postulating an unexplained necessary connection.
zh: Setiya 对“行动有构成性目的”的观念提出了几个重要挑战。按 Setiya（2007），任何行动理论都需要说明：实践知识（或在其版本中的信念条件；见本词条第 4 节）对有意行动是本质的。然而，信念条件似乎在概念上独立于行动的任何构成性目的；因而接受两者都对有意行动是构成的，就等于设定一个未经解释的必然联系。

en: Secondly, Setiya (2010) relies on the distinction between an explanatory reason and a normative reason to argue against the “guise of the good” (see Alvarez 2017 for a detailed account of the distinction)[^alvarez-2017]; his argument there could be extended to other proposals for the constitutive aim of action. An intentional action is an action done for an *explanatory* reason, namely, a reason that explains why the agent acted as she did, in Anscombe’s special sense of the question ‘Why’. However, Setiya points out that an explanatory reason need not be a *normative* reason; in fact, any reason that the agent believes to be her reason to act can be an explanatory reason, even if the object of such a reason is not good in any way. But since the reasons that explain intentional action need not be good in any way, it seems false that the agent must act only on reasons that she regards to be good in some way, and thus that she aims at the good in acting.
zh: 其次，Setiya（2010）借助解释性理由与规范性理由之分来反对“善之貌”（关于该区分的详细说明见 Alvarez 2017）[^alvarez-2017]；他在那里的论证可以扩展到行动之构成性目的的其他提案。有意行动是为 ** 解释性 ** 理由而做的行动——即在安斯康姆“为什么？”之特殊问法意义上，解释行动者为何如此行动的理由。然而，Setiya 指出：解释性理由不必是 ** 规范性 ** 理由；事实上，任何行动者相信是其行动理由的理由，都可以是解释性理由，即使这一理由的对象毫无善可言。但既然解释有意行动的理由不必有任何善，那么“行动者必须只按她以某种方式视为好的理由而行动、因而她在行动中以善为目标”就似乎是假的。

en: Philosophers have tried to answer these challenges. One can argue that a knowledge or belief condition, to the extent that it is valid, is explained by the constitutive aim of action. Moreover, perhaps the possibility of a third-person explanation of an action in terms of explanatory reasons whose objects are not good in any way is compatible with the fact that from the first-person point of view, these objects must have been regarded to be good in some way. So even if the fact that Rugen kills his father explains why Inigo Montoya killed Rugen without providing a normative reason for it, it still might be the case that avenging his father must have appeared good *to Inigo Montoya* in some way if he killed Rugen intentionally (see Tenenbaum 2012)[^tenenbaum-2012].
zh: 哲学家们试图回应这些挑战。人们可以论证：知识条件或信念条件，就其有效而言，是由行动的构成性目的解释的。此外，也许以对象毫无善可言的解释性理由给出行动的第三人称解释之可能，与如下事实相容：从第一人称的观点看，这些对象必定曾以某种方式被视为好的。因此，即便“鲁根杀了他的父亲”这一事实解释了英戈·蒙托亚为何杀了鲁根，而不为其提供规范性理由，但如果蒙托亚是有意杀鲁根的，为他父复仇这件事必定曾以某种方式对 ** 蒙托亚本人 ** 显得是好的，这仍可能成立（见 Tenenbaum 2012）[^tenenbaum-2012]。

en: Another well-known challenge to the idea that actions have a constitutive aim is David Enoch’s “schmagency” objection (Enoch 2006; 2011)[^enoch-2006]; in this context, the objection raises the possibility that for any purported constitutive aim, one could spurn such an aim and merely “schmact” or be a mere “schmagent”—someone who behaves just like an agent except for having the constitutive aim of agency. Enoch’s objection, however, is specifically concerned with attempts to derive normative consequences from the constitutive aim of action (for further discussion, see Bagnoli 2017; 2022)[^bagnoli-2017].
zh: 对“行动有构成性目的”的另一著名挑战是 David Enoch 的“施马能动性”（schmagency）异议（Enoch 2006; 2011）[^enoch-2006]；在这一语境中，该异议提出这样的可能：对任何号称的构成性目的，人们可以唾弃它，而只是“施马做”（schmact）、做一个纯粹的“施马行动者”（schmagent）——一个表现得与行动者一模一样、唯独没有能动性之构成性目的的存在者。不过，Enoch 的异议专门关切从行动的构成性目的导出规范性后果的尝试（进一步讨论见 Bagnoli 2017; 2022）[^bagnoli-2017]。

en: 7. Omission
zh: 7 不作为

en: 7.1 Different Ways of Not Acting
zh: 7.1 不行动的不同方式

en: The scope of our inactivity is vast; at each moment, there are many things I don’t do. Right now, I am not competing in the Olympics, not writing poetry, not swimming in the English Channel, not flying over the moon, or taking a journey to the center of the earth. However, none of the things could be plausibly described as cases of omissions or refrainings; it would be odd if I were told that I was refraining from competing in the Olympics or omitting to fly over the moon. Philosophers often describe cases of omissions as cases of my failing to do something that I was somehow “supposed to do” (Bach 2010)[^bach-2010]. Only some of my omissions are intentional or even voluntary: if my alarm does not go off and I miss my class because I overslept, I omitted to teach but not intentionally. On the other hand, if I fail to show up because I am protesting my university’s salary cuts, my omission was intentional. Intentional omissions and (intentional) refrainings are generally taken to be the only possible candidates for being instances of agency among not-doings (see Vermazen 1985 for an expression of this idea)[^vermazen-1985]. Thus, we will focus on these cases. The categories of intentional omissions and refraining are not necessarily identical. If I refrain from striking my opponent in a fit of anger, it seems wrong to say that I omitted to strike her as there is no sense in which I was “supposed to” strike my opponent.
zh: 我们无所作为的范围浩瀚：在每个时刻，都有许多事我不做。此刻，我没有在参加奥运会，没有在写诗，没有在游英吉利海峡，没有在飞越月球，也没有在去地心的旅途中。然而，这些事没有一件可以被合理地描述为不作为或克制的案例；如果有人告诉我，我正在克制不参加奥运会，或不作为地没有飞越月球，那会是很奇怪的。哲学家常把不作为的情形描述为我未能做某件我“被指望去做”的事（Bach 2010）[^bach-2010]。我的不作为中只有一些是有意的、甚至是自愿的：如果我的闹钟没响、我因睡过头而缺课，我不作为地没有去上课，但不是有意的。另一方面，如果我因抗议大学的减薪而未露面，我的不作为就是有意的。有意的不作为与（有意的）克制，一般被当作“不行动”中能动性实例的唯一可能候选（这一想法的表述见 Vermazen 1985）[^vermazen-1985]。因此我们将聚焦这些情形。有意不作为与克制这两个范畴并不必然同一。如果我在盛怒中克制不打对手，说我不作为地没打她似乎是错的，因为在任何意义上我都不是“被指望”打对手的。

en: 7.2 Agency, Omissions, and Refrainings
zh: 7.2 能动性、不作为与克制

en: Suppose all the Faculty at State University are upset about the recently announced cuts, and each of them express their dissatisfaction but in different ways: Mary wears a T-shirt that says “No More Cuts”, Terry writes a letter to the local paper, and Larry simply decides not to go to the department’s holiday party. It seems that in all these cases, the Faculty members are manifesting their agency—they are all equally expressing their dissatisfaction with the cuts—even if Larry does so by (intentionally) *not* doing something. Such cases of refrainings and intentional omissions seem paradigmatic instances of agency and yet they do not seem to be cases of action: after all, the agent did nothing. But how could the absence of an action be a manifestation of agency? One might be tempted to avoid any puzzling conclusions by simply denying that omissions are absences; by, for instance, proposing that Larry’s intentional omission consists in doing whatever acting he did *instead* of engaging in the omitted action. So if he goes to the bar instead of going to the holiday party, Larry omits to go to the party *by* going to the bar and so his going to the bar and his omitting to go to the party are the same event. However, this view immediately encounters difficulties as it seems that I can intentionally omit to do things without engaging in any positive act. I can refrain from laughing at my enemy’s jokes just by staying still and I can intentionally omit things even while asleep (Clarke 2014)[^clarke-2014]: indeed, instead of going to the bar, Larry could have omitted to go to the party by simply sleeping through it.
zh: 设想州立大学的全体教师都对新近宣布的裁员不满，每个人都以不同方式表达不满：玛丽穿着一件写着“不再裁员”的 T 恤，特里给本地报纸写信，而拉里只是决定不去系里的节日聚会。似乎在所有这些情形中，教师们都在显现其能动性——他们都同等地表达着对裁员的不满——即便拉里是靠（有意地）** 不 ** 做某事来表达的。这类克制与有意不作为的情形似乎是能动性的典范实例，然而它们似乎不是行动的情形：毕竟，行动者什么也没做。但一个行动的缺席怎么能是能动性的显现呢？人们可能想通过干脆否认不作为是缺席来避免任何令人困惑的结论：例如提出，拉里的有意不作为就在于去做他做的那件事，即作为被省略行动之 ** 替代 ** 的行动。于是，如果他去了酒吧而不是去节日聚会，拉里 ** 通过 ** 去酒吧而不作为地没去聚会，因此他去酒吧与他不作为地没去聚会是同一个事件。然而，这一看法立刻遭遇困难：似乎我可以有意地不做事而并不从事任何积极行动。我可以仅仅保持不动来克制不嘲笑我敌人的笑话；我甚至可以在睡觉时有意图地不做事（Clarke 2014）[^clarke-2014]：的确，拉里可以不去酒吧，而是通过在聚会期间睡过去来不作为地不参加聚会。

en: Early attempts to explain how an agent might intentionally *not* do something, without claiming that intentional omissions and refraining are actions, go back at least to Ryle (1973); Ryle argues that negative “actions” are not actions, but what he calls “lines of actions”, a category that also includes general policies such as “Take only cold baths”. More recently, Alvarez (2013) argues that the fact that omissions and refrainings can also manifest agency is a consequence of the fact that the power to act (intentionally) is a two-way power: a power to either do or *not* do something. Thus, when I refrain from driving my car, I manifest my agency not by engaging in an action, but rather by settling on *not* driving it (See Steward 2012; 2020 for further defense of the idea of agency as a two-way power).
zh: 解释行动者如何能有意地 ** 不 ** 做某事的早期尝试——不主张有意不作为与克制是行动——至少可追溯到 Ryle（1973）；赖尔论证：否定性的“行动”不是行动，而是他所谓的“行动路线”，这一范畴还包括“只洗冷水澡”这类一般政策。晚近，Alvarez（2013）论证：不作为与克制也能显现能动性，是“行动（有意地）的力是一种双向力”这一事实的推论——一种做或不做某事的力。于是，当我克制不驾驶我的车时，我显现能动性，不是通过从事一个行动，而是通过定案于 ** 不 ** 开它（对该观点的进一步辩护见 Steward 2012; 2020）。

en: 7.3 Intentional Omissions and the Causal Theory of Action
zh: 7.3 有意不作为与行动的因果理论

en: If we accept that omissions are absences, or at least that they are not events, the possibility of intentional omissions seem to present a challenge to the causal theory of action. After all, if agency can be manifested without any events being present, it is difficult to see how agency can be explained in the terms of the standard story of action (that is, in terms of the causal history of the bodily movements that manifest our agency). Hornsby (2004) argues that the failure of the standard causal theory to account for omissions is symptomatic of its more general failure to locate the agent in an account of intentional action that reduces agency to causal connections between non-agential happenings.
zh: 如果我们接受不作为是缺席，或至少它们不是事件，那么有意不作为的可能似乎对行动的因果理论构成挑战。毕竟，如果能动性可以在没有任何事件在场的情况下显现，就很难看出如何能以行动标准故事的术语——即以显现我们能动性的身体移动之因果史的术语——解释能动性。Hornsby（2004）论证：标准因果理论无法说明不作为，是它更一般失败的症状——它无法在一种把能动性还原为非行动者性发生之间的因果联系的有意行动说明中安放行动者。

en: There are at least two ways in which causal theorists try to answer these charges. One possibility is to argue that even though intentional omissions are absences, what makes them intentional is that facts about their causal history are analogous to the facts about causal history that make “positive actions” instances of agency (Clarke 2010; 2014)[^clark-2010][^clarke-2010]. On this view, just as positive actions are caused by an intention, intentional omissions are cases in which the non-obtaining of a certain event is similarly explained by an intention. However, Sartorio (2009) argues that intentional omissions pose a serious challenge even to this broader understanding of the standard causal theory of action. Sartorio argues that intentional omissions are often not best explained by other events (such as the formation of an intention), but by the *non-occurrence* of certain events (the best explanation of why I omitted to help my friend move might be that I *omitted* to form the intention to help them, rather than that I did form the intention not to help them). Another strategy to make omissions compatible with the standard causal theory is to try to show that omissions are events, while avoiding the questionable view that the omission must be identified with what the agent intentionally did at the time of the omission (Payton 2021)[^payton-2021].
zh: 因果理论家至少有两种方式回应这些指控。一种是论证：即便有意不作为是缺席，使它们成为有意的东西，是其因果史的事实与使“积极行动”成为能动性实例的因果史事实类似（Clarke 2010; 2014）[^clark-2010][^clarke-2014]。按这种看法，正如积极行动由意图引起，有意不作为是这样的情形：某个事件的不发生被类似地由一个意图解释。然而，Sartorio（2009）论证：有意不作为甚至对这一较宽泛的标准行动因果理论的理解构成严重挑战。Sartorio 论证：有意不作为往往不是被其他事件（如意图的形成）最好地解释，而是被某些事件的 ** 不发生 ** 解释（我没有帮朋友搬家的最好解释，可能是 ** 不作为地没有 ** 形成帮助他们的意图，而不是我形成了不帮助他们的意图）。使不作为与标准因果理论相容的另一策略，是试图表明不作为是事件，同时避免“不作为必须与行动者在不作为时有意做的事相认同”这一可疑的看法（Payton 2021）[^payton-2021]。

en: 8. Animal Action
zh: 8 动物行动

en: From the start, our focus has been on the intentional actions of fully developed rational agents. However, this raises the question: what about other beings, such as (non-human) animals? Can they act? If so, do they act in the same way as fully developed humans do? (Similar questions arise for children and robots, but our focus shall be on the growing literature on animal agency.)
zh: 从一开始，我们的焦点就是充分发展的理性行动者的有意行动。然而，这引出问题：其他存在者——如（非人的）动物——呢？它们能行动吗？如果能，它们与我们完全发展的人类以同样的方式行动吗？（类似的问题也出现在儿童与机器人身上，但我们的焦点是日益增长的关于动物能动性的文献。）
