en: Judah Abrabanel
zh: 犹大·莱昂·阿布拉瓦内尔 Abrabanel, Judah (Aaron Hughes)

en: **First published Fri Dec 2, 2005; substantive revision Wed Jun 8, 2022**
zh: **首次发表于 2005 年 12 月 2 日；2022 年 6 月 8 日实质修订。**

en: Judah Abrabanel (ca. 1465–after 1521), also known as Leone Ebreo, is an important transitional figure in the history of Jewish philosophy. Common to any transitional figure, however, is the problem of contextualization. In the case of Judah Abrabanel, do we regard him as the last of the medieval Jewish philosophers or the first of the early modern ones? His work, for example, is certainly in conversation with a number of themes found in Renaissance Platonism and Humanism. Yet at the same time he freely draws upon the cosmology and metaphysics of his Jewish and Islamic predecessors.
zh: 犹大·阿布拉瓦内尔（Judah Abrabanel，约 1465–1521 年后），又称 Leone Ebreo（莱昂·埃布雷奥），是犹太哲学史上一位重要的过渡人物。但凡过渡人物，都绕不开如何定位（语境化）的问题：就犹大·阿布拉瓦内尔而言，我们该把他看作中世纪犹太哲学的殿军，还是早期现代哲学的先锋？例如，他的著作确实与文艺复兴柏拉图主义和人文主义的诸多主题对话；但同时，他又自由地取用于其犹太与伊斯兰先驱的宇宙论和形而上学。

en: Abrabanel’s magnum opus, the *Dialoghi d’amore* (“Dialogues of Love”) belongs to the genre of the *trattato d’amore* (“treatise on love”) that was intimately connected to both the Renaissance and the development of the Italian vernacular. Although Abrabanel’s dialogue provides one of the genre’s most important philosophical discussions in this, it nonetheless is confined to its literary and stylized form. The work itself consists of three dialogues, with the third one providing the longest and most sustained philosophical discussion. Some contend that Abrabanel originally composed an introduction to the work and a fourth dialogue, neither of which survives.[^note-1] In essence, the *Dialoghi* offers the transcript of a conversation between two individuals, Philo and Sophia, two courtiers, who discourse on the nature of love as both a sensual and cosmic principle. Philo, the male character, is portrayed as an accomplished philosopher, and Sophia, the female character, as a student of philosophy. Despite this, Sophia is not just a convenient textual strategy, but becomes a character in her own right, someone who significantly contributes to the philosophical unfolding of the work. Moreover, many of the dialogic exchanges that take place between Philo and Sophia are very playful, with Philo, on one level, either answering Sophia’s questions about love or responding to her criticisms; yet, on another level, he physically desires Sophia and wishes to consummate this desire. Philo’s desire for Sophia, thus, reflects the same desire of God (the superior) for the world (the inferior). As a Renaissance artist, then, Abrabanel cleverly and artfully weaves the philosophical principles of love, beauty, and desire into the very literary structure of his *Dialoghi*.
zh: 阿布拉瓦内尔的代表作《爱的对话》（*Dialoghi d'amore*；下文简称《对话集》）属于 *trattato d'amore*（“爱的论著”）这一文类，后者与文艺复兴及意大利俗语的发展关系密切。尽管阿布拉瓦内尔的对话为该文类提供了最重要的哲学讨论之一，它仍受限于其文学化、风格化的形式。全书由三篇对话组成，第三篇给出了最长、最连贯的哲学讨论。有人主张阿布拉瓦内尔原本还为全书写了一篇导言和第四篇对话，但均未传世。[^note-1]本质上，《对话集》记录了两个人物——菲洛（Philo）与索菲亚（Sophia），两位廷臣——之间关于爱既是感官原理又是宇宙原理的对话。男性角色菲洛被描绘为一位造诣精深的哲学家，女性角色索菲亚则是哲学的学生。尽管如此，索菲亚并不只是一个方便的文本策略，而是成长为一个独立的人物，对全书的哲学展开做出了重要贡献。此外，菲洛与索菲亚之间的许多对话交换十分俏皮：在某一层面上，菲洛或在回答索菲亚关于爱的提问，或在回应她的批评；而在另一层面上，他在肉体上渴望索菲亚，并希望实现这一欲望。菲洛对索菲亚的欲望，因而映照出上帝（较高者）对世界（较低者）的同一种欲望。于是，作为一位文艺复兴艺术家，阿布拉瓦内尔巧妙而精湛地把爱、美与欲望的哲学原理编织进《对话集》的文学结构本身。

en: 1. Life and Works
zh: 1 生平与著作

en: There exists a large debate in the secondary literature concerning the place and role of Jews in Renaissance culture. One group envisages a synthesis between Jewish culture on the one hand, and the ideals of the Renaissance on the other.[^note-2] Jews, according to this interpretation, could quite easily remain Jewish while still sharing in the values and culture of non-Jewish society. Another group, however, maintains that such a synthesis is historically untenable because Jews remained a small, persecuted minority left to the whims of various local governments.[^note-3] These two approaches leave us with radically different conceptions of Renaissance Jewish philosophers. According to the first approach, a Jewish intellectual could quite easily partake of the ideals and categories of Renaissance Humanism and Neoplatonism. According to the second approach, however, such a synthesis could never occur, and, as a result, most Renaissance Jewish thinkers were more indebted to the legacy of Maimonides than the various trajectories of Renaissance thought. A more productive approach, however, exists between these two: The Italian Renaissance provided certain elite Jews with new literary genres, intellectual categories, and educational ideals with which to mine the depths of their tradition.
zh: 关于犹太人在文艺复兴文化中的地位与角色，二手文献中存在大量争论。一派设想犹太文化与文艺复兴理想之间的综合。[^note-2]按这种解读，犹太人可以相当容易地一边保持犹太身份，一边分享非犹太社会的价值与文化。另一派则主张这种综合在历史上站不住脚，因为犹太人始终是一个受迫害的少数群体，任凭各地政府摆布。[^note-3]这两种进路给我们留下了截然不同的文艺复兴犹太哲学家形象。按第一种进路，一位犹太知识分子可以相当容易地分享文艺复兴人文主义与新柏拉图主义的理想与范畴。按第二种进路，这种综合绝无可能发生，因而多数文艺复兴犹太思想家更多受惠于迈蒙尼德的遗产，而非文艺复兴思想的各条轨迹。然而，在这两者之间存在一种更有成效的进路：意大利文艺复兴为某些精英犹太人提供了新的文学文类、智识范畴与教育理想，使他们得以挖掘自身传统的深处。

en: 1.1 Life
zh: 1.1 生平

en: Judah Abrabanel was born in Lisbon, Portugal, sometime between 1460 and 1470. He was the firstborn of Don Isaac Abrabanel (1437–1508), who was an important philosopher in his own right. In addition to their intellectual skills, the Abrabanel family played an important role in international commerce, quickly becoming one of the most prominent families in Lisbon.
zh: 犹大·阿布拉瓦内尔约于 1460 至 1470 年间生于葡萄牙里斯本。他是唐·伊萨克·阿布拉瓦内尔（Don Isaac Abrabanel，1437–1508）的长子，后者本身就是一位重要的哲学家。除智识才能外，阿布拉瓦内尔家族在国际商业中扮演重要角色，很快成为里斯本最显赫的家族之一。

en: Despite the conservative tendencies in the thought of his father, Don Isaac insured that his children received educations that included both Jewish and non-Jewish subjects. Rabbi Joseph ben Abraham ibn Hayoun, the leading rabbinic figure in Lisbon, was responsible for teaching religious subjects (e.g., Bible, commentaries, and halakhic works) to Judah and his brothers. As far as non-Jewish works and subjects were concerned, Judah, like most elite Jews of the fifteenth century, would have been instructed in both the medieval Arabo-Judaic tradition (e.g., Maimonides, Averroes), in addition to humanistic studies imported from Italy.[^note-4]
zh: 尽管父亲的思想偏保守，唐·伊萨克仍确保子女接受包含犹太与非犹太科目的教育。里斯本最领先的拉比人物约瑟夫·本·亚伯拉罕·伊本·哈永拉比（Rabbi Joseph ben Abraham ibn Hayoun）负责给犹大及其兄弟们教授宗教科目（如圣经、注释书与律法著作）。至于非犹太著作与科目，犹大如十五世纪多数精英犹太人一样，接受了中世纪阿拉伯-犹太传统（如迈蒙尼德、阿威罗伊）以及自意大利输入的人文主义研究的训练。[^note-4]

en: By profession, Judah was a doctor, one who had a very good reputation and who served the royal court. In 1483, his father was implicated in a political conspiracy against Joao II, the Duke of Braganza, and was forced to flee to Seville, in Spain, with his family. Shortly after his arrival, undoubtedly on account of his impressive connections and diplomatic skills, Isaac was summoned to the court of Ferdinand and Isabella, where he was to become a financial advisor to the royal family. Despite his favorable relationship with them, Isaac was unable to influence them to rescind their famous edict of expulsion—calling on all Jews who refused to convert to Christianity—to depart from the Iberian Peninsula.
zh: 犹大的职业是医生，声望极好，服务于宫廷。1483 年，其父涉嫌卷入一场针对国王若昂二世的政治阴谋（布拉干萨公爵案），被迫携全家逃往西班牙塞维利亚。抵达后不久——无疑凭借其令人印象深刻的人脉与外交才能——伊萨克被召入斐迪南与伊莎贝拉的宫廷，成为王室的财政顾问。尽管与他们关系良好，伊萨克仍未能说服他们撤销那道著名的驱逐令——要求所有拒绝皈依基督教的犹太人离开伊比利亚半岛。

en: Judah seems also to have been well connected at the Spanish court and was one of the physicians who attended the royal family. After the edict of expulsion had been issued, Ferdinand and Isabella requested that he remain in Spain. To do this, however, he still would have had to convert to Christianity. Yet, in order to try and keep Judah in Spain, a plot was hatched to kidnap his firstborn son, Isaac ben Judah. Judah, however, discovered the plot and sent his son, along with his Christian nanny, on to Portugal, where he hoped to meet up with them. Upon hearing that a relative of Isaac Abrabanel had re-entered Portugal, Joao II had the young boy seized and forcefully converted to Christianity. It is uncertain whether or not Judah ever saw or heard from his son again. In a moving poem, entitled *Telunah ‘al ha-zeman* (“The Travails of Time”), he writes:
zh: 犹大在西班牙宫廷似乎也有很好的关系，是服侍王室成员的医生之一。驱逐令颁布后，斐迪南与伊莎贝拉要求他留在西班牙。然而为此他仍须皈依基督教。而为了设法把犹大留在西班牙，有人密谋绑架他的长子伊萨克·本·犹大。犹大发现了这一阴谋，把儿子连同其基督徒保姆一起送往葡萄牙，希望在那里与他们汇合。听到伊萨克·阿布拉瓦内尔的亲属重新进入葡萄牙后，若昂二世将这个男孩抓捕并强行皈依基督教。犹大是否再见过或听说过他的儿子，不得而知。在一首题为《时代的苦难》（*Telunah ʼal ha-zeman*）的感人诗篇中，他写道：

en: Time with his pointed shafts has hit my heart and split my guts, laid open my entrails, landed me a blow that will not heal knocked me down, left me in lasting pain… He did not stop at whirling me around, exiling me while yet my days were green sending me stumbling, drunk, to roam the world… He scattered everyone I care for northward, eastward, or to the west, so that I have no rest from constant thinking, planning— and never a moment’s peace, for all my plans.[^note-5]
zh: 时间用其利箭射中我的心、劈开我的脏腑，敞开我的内里，给我一记无法愈合的打击，将我击倒，使我陷入持久的痛苦……他没有停止将我翻转，在我年岁尚青时放逐我，让我踉跄、醉酒、在世界各处流浪……他把我珍爱的每一个人驱散到北方、东方或西方，使我在不断的思考与筹划中不得安宁——我的一切计谋没有一刻安息。[^note-5]

en: Like many of those Jews who refused to convert, Judah and his immediate family, including his father, made their way to Naples. There, Ferdinand II of Aragon, the king of Naples, warmly welcomed the Abrabanel family, owing to its many contacts in international trade. In 1495, however, the French took control of Naples, and Judah was again forced to flee, first to Genoa, then to Barletta, and subsequently to Venice. It seems that he also traveled around Tuscany, and there is some debate as to whether or not he actually met the famous Florentine Humanist, Giovanni Pico della Mirandola (it seems unlikely that he did). In 1501, after the defeat of the French in Naples, he was invited back to be the personal physician of the Viceroy of Naples, Fernandez de Córdoba. Among all of these peregrinations, Judah found the time to write (but not publish) his *magnum opus*, the *Dialoghi d’amore*. He seems to have died sometime after 1521. Other than these basic facts, we know very little of the life of Judah Abrabanel.
zh: 与许多拒绝皈依的犹太人一样，犹大与他的直系亲属（包括其父）前往那不勒斯。那不勒斯国王阿拉贡的斐迪南二世因阿布拉瓦内尔家族在国际贸易中的诸多人脉而热情欢迎他们。然而 1495 年，法国人占领那不勒斯，犹大再次被迫逃亡，先到热那亚，再到巴列塔，随后到威尼斯。他似乎还周游了托斯卡纳；至于他是否真的见过著名的佛罗伦萨人文主义者乔瓦尼·皮科·德拉·米兰多拉，尚有争论（似乎不太可能）。1501 年，法军在那不勒斯战败后，他被邀请回来担任那不勒斯总督费尔南德斯·德·科尔多瓦的私人医生。在这些辗转迁徙中，犹大抽出时间写作（但未出版）其代表作《爱的对话》。他似乎卒于 1521 年之后的某个时候。除了这些基本事实，我们对犹大·阿布拉瓦内尔的生平所知甚少。

en: Especially enigmatic are the last years of his life, between 1521 when he was requested to give medical attention to Cardinal San Giorgio until 1535 when Mariano Lenzi published the *Dialoghi* posthumously in Rome. There is some evidence that Judah moved to Rome near the end of his life; some suggest that he fell in with a Christian group of Neoplatonists. Indeed, the 1541 edition of the work mentions that Judah converted to Christianity (*dipoi fatto christiano*). This, however, seems highly unlikely as (1) it is not mentioned in the first edition, the one on which all subsequent editions and translations were based, and (2) there is no internal evidence in the *Dialoghi* to suggest this. In fact, one of the characters in the work implies the exact opposite, stating that “all of us believe in the sacred Mosaic law” (*noi tutti che crediamo la sacre legge mosaica*).[^note-6] It seems, then, that either a careless or over-zealous editor inserted the phrase “*dipoi fatto christiano*” into a later edition of the *Dialoghi*.
zh: 尤其令人费解的是他生命的最后几年：从 1521 年他应邀为圣乔治枢机主教提供医疗服务，直到 1535 年马里亚诺·伦齐在罗马出版其遗作《对话集》。有证据表明犹大在生命末期移居罗马；有人认为他加入了一个基督教新柏拉图主义团体。事实上，1541 年版提到犹大皈依了基督教（*dipoi fatto christiano*）。但这极不可能，因为 (1) 初版——所有后续版本与译本的底本——没有提到此事；(2) 《对话集》没有任何内证支持这一点。事实上，书中一个角色暗示了恰好相反的立场，说“我们所有人都信仰神圣的摩西律法”（*noi tutti che crediamo la sacre legge mosaica*）。[^note-6]因此，似乎要么是一位粗心或过于热心的编辑把 *dipoi fatto christiano* 这一短语插进了《对话集》的某个后期版本。

en: 1.2 Works
zh: 1.2 著作

en: The only major work that we possess of Judah Abrabanel is the *Dialoghi d’amore*. There is some debate as to when the work was actually written. Many point to the year 1501–1502 owing to a phrase in the third book: “According to the Jewish tradition, we are in the year 5262 from the beginning of creation” (*Siamo, secondo la veritá ebraica, a cinque milia ducento sessanta due del principio de la creazione*).[^note-7] The year 5262 of the Jewish calendar corresponds to 1501–1502 of the Gregorian calendar. Yet, manuscripts other than that based on the 1535 edition have the date of 5272 (i.e., 1511–1512). This is significant because many who argue that the *Dialoghi* could not possibly have been written in Italian point to the fact that Judah would not have been fluent in Italian. Yet, if we assume the 1511–1512 date to be correct this would place him in Italy for close to twenty years, more than enough time to gain proficiency in Italian (especially given the fact that he would have already known at least one Spanish vernacular and, as a physician, Latin).
zh: 我们掌握的犹大·阿布拉瓦内尔唯一的主要著作是《爱的对话》。关于这部著作实际的写作时间存在争论。许多人指向 1501–1502 年，因为第三卷中有一句话：“按犹太传统，我们从创世之初至今是 5262 年”（*Siamo, secondo la veritá ebraica, a cinque milia ducento sessanta due del principio de la creazione*）。[^note-7]犹太历 5262 年对应公历 1501–1502 年。然而，基于 1535 年版之外的手稿有 5272 年（即 1511–1512 年）的日期。这一点很重要，因为许多主张《对话集》不可能用意大利语写成的人，指出犹大不会流利地使用意大利语。但如果我们假定 1511–1512 年的日期正确，这将把他在意大利的时间推到接近二十年——足以精通意大利语（尤其考虑到他已经至少通晓一种西班牙俗语，而作为医生还通晓拉丁语）。

en: We also know that Judah wrote poetry (see the poem quoted above). In addition to his biographical poem, he also composed poetic introductions to three of his father’s last works: *Rosh Amanah, Zevach Pesach*, and *Nachalat Avot.*
zh: 我们还知道犹大写过诗（见上文引述的诗）。除了这首传记诗之外，他还为父亲最后三部著作写了诗体导言：《Rosh Amanah》《Zevach Pesach》与《Nachalat Avot》。

en: Finally, we possess a letter dating to 1566 from one Amatus Lusitanus, a physician who wrote that he attended to a patient by the name of Judah “who was the grandson of the great Platonic philosopher, known as Judah or Leon Abrabanel, who gave to us the most beautiful dialogues on love.” Further in this letter, he mentions that Judah also composed a work entitled *De Coeli Harmonia* (“On the Harmony of the Spheres”) and that, according to the introduction, he dedicated it to the “divine Pico della Mirandola.” Unfortunately, this work has not survived. If he dedicated to Pico as the letter indicates, it would most likely have been composed before the *Dialoghi* and also, based on the title, it would have been composed in Latin.
zh: 最后，我们有一封写于 1566 年的信，来自医生阿马图斯·卢西塔努斯（Amatus Lusitanus），他写道他诊治过一位名叫犹大的病人，“他是那位伟大的柏拉图主义哲学家——人称犹大或莱昂·阿布拉瓦内尔——的孙子，他给了我们最美的关于爱的对话。”信中还提到犹大写过一部题为《论天体的和谐》（*De Coeli Harmonia*）的著作，并按其导言将它献给“神圣的皮科·德拉·米兰多拉”。遗憾的是，这部著作没有传世。如果按信中所说他把它献给了皮科，那么它最可能写于《对话集》之前；且按标题看，它应是拉丁文写成的。

en: 1.3 *Dialoghi d’amore* and the Question of Language
zh: 1.3 《爱的对话》与语言问题

en: The central question concerning the language of the *Dialoghi*’s composition is: How could a Jewish refugee from Portugal show such facility with Italian, let alone the Tuscan dialect, since Judah seems to have spent very little time in Tuscany?[^note-8] Those who argue for a Latin original point to the fact that (1) he was a physician and would have known Latin, and (2) a phrase by Yosef Shlomo Delmedigo (1591–1655) in his *Mikhtav Ahuz* suggesting that he was going to translate Judah’s work from Latin. Those who argue for a Hebrew original point to another phrase, this time by Claudio Tolemei (1492–1556), a non-Jew, which states that Judah composed his treatise in *sua lingua* (“his own language”). Although, as others have pointed out, such a phrase could quite easily refer to “his own style.”
zh: 围绕《对话集》写作语言的核心问题是：一个来自葡萄牙的犹太难民怎么可能对意大利语——遑论托斯卡纳方言——如此娴熟，因为犹大似乎在托斯卡纳待过的时间很短？[^note-8]主张拉丁语原本的人指出：(1) 他是医生，应当懂拉丁语；(2) 约瑟夫·所罗门·德尔梅迪戈（Yosef Shlomo Delmedigo，1591–1655）在《Mikhtav Ahuz》中的一段话暗示他将把犹大的著作从拉丁语翻译过来。主张希伯来语原本的人则引用另一位——非犹太人——克劳迪奥·托勒梅伊（Claudio Tolemei，1492–1556）的话，说犹大用 *sua lingua*（“他自己的语言”）撰写了这部论著。不过正如他人指出的，这样的措辞也很容易指“他自己的风格”。

en: However, given the evidence, an Italian original for the work seems most likely since (1) all the manuscripts, including Mariano Lenzi’s edition of 1535, are in Italian; (2) it seems that Judah had lived in Italy for close to twenty years by the time that he wrote the *Dialoghi* (more than enough time for someone to gain an intimate knowledge of Italian, especially someone proficient in Latin and Spanish vernaculars); (3) neither later Jewish authors, e.g., Azaria de’Rossi,[^note-9] nor non-Jewish authors, e.g., Tullia d’Aragona,[^note-10] had any reason to suspect that it was written in a language other than Italian; (4) if we assume the later date of 1511–1512, many non-Tuscan Italian authors of this period called for the adoption of Tuscan as a literary language, owing primarily to the fact that this was the language of Petrarch (1304–1374) and Boccaccio (1313–1375);[^note-11] and, (5) as for the question of the Tuscan dialect of the work, many Italian printers of the early sixteenth century “Tuscanized” Italian according to set criteria.[^note-12]
zh: 然而，根据现有证据，意大利语原本的可能性最大，因为 (1) 所有手稿——包括伦齐 1535 年的版本——都是意大利语的；(2) 到写作《对话集》时，犹大似乎已在意大利居住了近二十年（对精通意大利语来说绰绰有余，尤其对通晓拉丁语和西班牙俗语的人）；(3) 后来的犹太作家（如 Azaria de'Rossi）[^note-9]与非犹太作家（如 Tullia d'Aragona）[^note-10]都没有理由怀疑它不是用意大利语写的；(4) 如果我们假定较晚的 1511–1512 年日期，这一时期许多非托斯卡纳的意大利作家呼吁采用托斯卡纳语作为文学语言，主要因为这是彼特拉克（1304–1374）和薄伽丘（1313–1375）的语言；[^note-11]以及 (5) 至于该著作的托斯卡纳方言问题，十六世纪初的许多意大利印刷商按既定标准将意大利语“托斯卡纳化”。[^note-12]

en: Moreover, many Jewish authors in the fifteenth- and sixteenth-centuries increasingly resorted to Romance vernaculars in order to attract a Jewish audience (including *conversos* and ex-*conversos*), which no longer understood Hebrew. In sixteenth-century Italy, larger trends in rhetoric and the use of language increasingly led to the creation of the ideal of a pure Italian language. In this regard, Judah becomes an important transitional thinker in the encounter between Judaism and the Italian Renaissance. Whereas his father, Don Isaac, could still adapt humanistic themes to his Hebrew writings, which were still primarily in conversation with medieval thought,[^note-13] increasingly in Judah’s generation the only way to engage in a full-scale examination of the universal tendencies associated with Humanism was to write in the vernacular.
zh: 此外，十五和十六世纪的许多犹太作家越来越多地使用罗曼语俗语，以吸引已不再懂希伯来语的犹太听众（包括 *conversos* 与前 *conversos*）。在十六世纪的意大利，修辞与语言使用的更大趋势日益导向纯正意大利语理想的形成。在这方面，犹大成为犹太教与意大利文艺复兴相遇中的一位重要的过渡思想家。他的父亲唐·伊萨克尚能把人文主义主题适配到仍主要与中世纪思想对话的希伯来文著作中，[^note-13]而在犹大的世代，对人文主义所关联的普遍倾向做全面考察的唯一方式，日益是使用俗语写作。

en: Finally, the very genre of the *Dialoghi*, that of the *trattato d’amore* (“treatise on love”), was the product of the Italian vernacular of the late fifteenth and early sixteenth centuries. When, for example, Judah discusses the concept of love as a universal or cosmic principle he draws upon, as will be clearer below, a particular vocabulary and set of concepts that only make sense when contextualized within this already existing discourse.[^note-14]
zh: 最后，《对话集》的文类本身——*trattato d'amore*（“爱的论著”）——就是十五世纪末和十六世纪初意大利俗语的产物。例如，当犹大讨论爱作为普遍或宇宙原理的概念时，他取用的是——如下文将更清楚看到的——一套特定的词汇与概念集合，只有将其置于这一已然存在的论说传统中才有意义。[^note-14]

en: 2. Faith, Reason, and Myth
zh: 2 信仰、理性与神话

en: Two features that are new in Judah’s work and, thus, serve to differentiate his thought from that of his Jewish and Islamic predecessors are: (1) his almost complete lack of concern with the venerable antagonism between faith and reason, and (2) his interest in elucidating the concomitant intersection between Greek myth and Judaism.
zh: 犹大著作中有两个新特征使其思想区别于其犹太与伊斯兰先驱：(1) 他几乎完全不关心信仰与理性之间由来已久的对抗；(2) 他关注阐明随之而来的希腊神话与犹太教的交汇。

en: The tension between faith and reason had been at the heart of medieval Jewish philosophy. This became especially pronounced in post-Maimonidean philosophy, which witnessed the radicalization of a number of principles (e.g., eternality of the universe, denial of bodily resurrection), and which threatened to undermine traditional religious belief. This led to a *Kulturkampf* between those who thought that non-Jewish learning (i.e., philosophy) had a valid role to play in the Jewish curriculum versus those who claimed that such “foreign” works led to apostasy. The reverberations of these conflicts, known collectively as the “Maimonidean controversies,” were severe.
zh: 信仰与理性之间的张力一直是中世纪犹太哲学的核心。这在后迈蒙尼德哲学中变得尤为突出——后者见证了若干原则的激进化（如宇宙的永恒、否定身体复活），威胁到传统宗教信仰。这导致了一场 *Kulturkampf*（文化斗争）：一派认为非犹太学问（即哲学）在犹太课程中有合法地位，另一派则声称这类“外来”著作导致叛教。这些冲突的反响——统称“迈蒙尼德之争”——是严重的。

en: The antagonism between faith and reason is immediately palpable in the thought of Judah’s father, who constantly tried to uphold traditional Jewish belief against what he considered to be the onslaught of philosophical radicalism. Yet, in the thought of Judah this “conflict” between the hitherto venerable antagonists virtually disappears. The question we have to ask, then, is why? The most likely reason is to be located in the notion of *sophia perennis*, which played an important role in the thought of Florentine humanists. According to this doctrine, there exists a unity to all knowledge irrespective of its source. As a result, the rationalism of philosophy could quite easily be reconciled with that of revelation because both were regarded as articulating the same truth. Evidence of this may be seen in Judah’s frequent citation of biblical passages to support philosophical principles and *vice versa*. Furthermore, because Judah is primarily unconcerned with the antagonism between faith and reason, he becomes one of the first Jewish philosophers to ignore esotericism (viz., that philosophical truths must be kept from the unenlightened) as a philosophical principle. For him, traditional esoteric topics, such as metaphysics, now become part and parcel of the beautiful and dramatic unfolding of God’s beauty in the universe, and such topics are open to all (including women, as the character of Sophia demonstrates).
zh: 信仰与理性之间的对抗在犹大父亲的思想中立刻可以感受到：他不断试图维护传统犹太信仰，抵御他所认为的哲学激进主义的冲击。然而，在犹大的思想中，这对迄今可敬的对手之间的“冲突”几乎消失了。我们必须追问：为什么？最可能的原因应定位于 *sophia perennis*（永恒智慧）的观念——它在佛罗伦萨人文主义者的思想中扮演重要角色。按这一学说，一切知识不论其来源如何都存在统一性。结果，哲学的理性主义可以很容易地与启示的理性主义调和，因为二者被认为阐明了同一真理。这方面的证据可见于犹大频繁引用圣经段落来支持哲学原则，反之亦然。此外，因为犹大主要不关心信仰与理性之间的对抗，他成为最早忽略秘传主义（即哲学真理必须对未启蒙者保密）作为哲学原则的犹太哲学家之一。对他来说，传统的秘传主题——如形而上学——现在成为上帝之美在宇宙中美丽而戏剧性展开的组成部分，对所有人（包括女性，如索菲亚这一角色所展示的）开放。

en: Further evidence of Judah’s use of the concept of *sophia perennis* may be witnessed in his orientation towards ancient Greek myth. The “rediscovery” of ancient Greek and Roman literature was one of the hallmarks of the Renaissance, and in the thought of Judah we certainly see this, only now with a distinctly Jewish “twist.” On one level, he wants to show that there exists a fundamental identity between Greek myth and the teachings of the Torah. Yet, on a deeper level he wants to argue that the Greeks ultimately derived their teachings from the ancient Israelites and subsequently corrupted them.[^note-15] For instance, Judah argues that Plato studied among the ancient Israelites in Egypt,[^note-16] and that Plato’s myth of the Androgyne, found in the *Symposium*, is actually a Greek plagiarism of a Jewish source:
zh: 犹大使用 *sophia perennis* 概念的进一步证据，见于他对古希腊神话的取向。“重新发现”古希腊和罗马文献是文艺复兴的标志之一，在犹大的思想中我们确实看到了这一点，只是现在带有一个鲜明的犹太“转折”。在某一层面上，他想表明希腊神话与《托拉》的教导之间存在根本的同一性。在更深的层面上，他想论证希腊人的教导最终承袭自古代以色列人，并随后将其败坏。[^note-15]例如，犹大论证柏拉图曾在埃及的古代以色列人中间学习，[^note-16]而柏拉图在《会饮篇》中提出的阴阳人神话实际上是对犹太文献的希腊剽窃：

en: Sophia: The story is beautiful and ornate (*la favola è bella e ornata*), and it is impossible not to believe that it signifies some philosophical beauty (*bella filosofia*), more especially since it was composed by Plato himself, in the *Symposium*, in the name of Aristophanes. Tell me, therefore, Philo what is the allegory? Philo: The myth was handed down by earlier writers than the Greeks—in the sacred writings of Moses, concerning the creation of the first human parents, Adam and Eve…it was from [Moses] that Plato took his myth, amplifying and polishing it after Greek oratory, thus giving a confused account of Hebrew matters (*facendo in questo una mescolanza inordinate de le cose ebraiche*).[^note-17]
zh: 索菲亚：这个故事美丽而华美（*la favola è bella e ornata*），不可能不相信它意味着某种哲学之美（*bella filosofia*），尤其因为它出自柏拉图本人之手，在《会饮篇》中以阿里斯托芬的名义创作。那么告诉我，菲洛，这个寓意是什么？ 菲洛：这个神话由比希腊人更早的作者传下来——在摩西的神圣著作中，关于最初人类父母亚当和夏娃的创造……柏拉图正是从［摩西］那里取用了他的神话，按希腊修辞术加以扩充和打磨，从而对希伯来事物给出了一种混杂的说明（*facendo in questo una mescolanza inordinate de le cose ebraiche*）。[^note-17]

en: Judah seeks to accomplish at least two things with passages such as this. First, he claims, polemically, that the Jewish tradition, especially its mythopoeic tradition, is the source of all subsequent literary and philosophical streams of western civilization. Secondly (and this is less evident in the above passage than in other ones), he tries to wrest Christian-centric interpretations of biblical passages (e.g., the Garden of Eden and the concept of original sin), including those offered by thinkers such as Ficino and Pico della Mirandola,[^note-18] away from what he considers to be the original intentionality of the text. Rather, he claims that the Jewish version or interpretation of such texts is actually more in keeping with the spirit of the Renaissance than those offered by Christians. The corollary of this is that any individual, Jewish or Gentile, should quite easily be able to accept equally the truths of Judaism and those of philosophy.[^note-19]
zh: 犹大试图通过这样的段落完成至少两件事。第一，他论战性地主张：犹太传统——尤其是其神话创作传统——是西方文明所有后续文学与哲学流派的源头。第二（这一点在上文段落中不如在其他段落中明显），他试图把基督教中心的对圣经段落的解释（如伊甸园与原罪概念）——包括费奇诺和皮科·德拉·米兰多拉等思想家提出的解释——[^note-18]从他认为是文本本源意图的东西中剥离。毋宁说，他主张，犹太版的或对这类文本的犹太解释，实际上比基督徒提供的更符合文艺复兴的精神。其推论是：任何人，无论犹太人还是非犹太人，都应当能同样容易地接受犹太教的真理和哲学的真理。[^note-19]

en: 3. Beauty and Love
zh: 3 美与爱

en: In the thought of Judah Abrabanel, the concepts of beauty (*bellezza*) and love (*amore*) become technical terms through which he examines virtually every traditional philosophical issue. Frequently, however, his discussion of one of these terms is predicated on the existence of the other; as a result, beauty and love are inseparable in the *Dialoghi*, undoubtedly mirroring Judah’s understanding of the way in which these two principles operate in the universe. The intimate relationship between these two principles may be witnessed in his definition of beauty as that “which delights the mind that recognizes it and moves it to love” (*dilettando l’animo col suo conoscimento, il muove ad amare*).[^note-20] Without Beauty, in other words, the intellect is unable to desire something outside of itself and, thus, it is effectively unable to cognize. Judah subsequently argues that the lower senses (i.e., taste, smell or touch) cannot grasp Beauty; only the higher senses (e.g., sight and hearing) can—in addition, of course, to the imagination and the intellect.[^note-21] Moreover, since Beauty is mirrored throughout the universe, physical objects (notes, melodies, etc.) both participate in and point the way towards this incorporeal Beauty:
zh: 在犹大·阿布拉瓦内尔的思想中，美（*bellezza*）与爱（*amore*）的概念成为他考察几乎所有传统哲学问题的技术性术语。然而，他对其中一个术语的讨论常常以另一个的存在为前提；因此，美与爱在《对话集》中不可分离，这无疑映照出犹大对这两个原理在宇宙中运作方式的理解。这两个原理之间的密切关系可见于他对美的定义：“那因其被认识而愉悦心灵、并推动心灵去爱的东西”（*dilettando l'animo col suo conoscimento, il muove ad amare*）。[^note-20]没有美，换言之，理智就无法渴望自身之外的东西，因而实际上无法认知。犹大随后论证，较低级的感觉（即味觉、嗅觉或触觉）无法把握美；只有较高级的感觉（如视觉和听觉）才能——此外当然还有想象力和理智。[^note-21]而且，由于美映照在整个宇宙中，物理对象（音符、旋律等）既参与又指向这一无形的美：

en: Beauty is only found in the objects of sight (*oggetti del viso*), such as beautiful forms and shapes and beautiful pictures, the perfect symmetry of the parts with the whole, well-proportioned limbs, beautiful colors and clear light, the sun, the moon and the stars, and the heavens in all their splendor. This grace exists in objects of sight by reason of their spiritual nature, and it is the custom to enter through the clear and spiritual eyes, to delight our soul and move it to a love of such an object; and this is what it is that we call beauty. It is also found in objects of hearing, such as beautiful oratory, voices, speech, song music, consonance, proportion and harmony. For in the spiritual nature of these things is found grace which moves the soul to delight and to love through the medium of the spiritual sense of hearing. Thus grace and beauty are found among beautiful things that are endowed with a spiritual nature (*sensi spirituali*).[^note-22]
zh: 美只存在于视觉的对象之中（*oggetti del viso*），如美丽的形状与形式、美丽的图画、部分与整体的完美对称、匀称的肢体、美丽的色彩与清澈的光、太阳、月亮和星辰，以及壮丽的天穹。这种优雅存在于视觉对象之中，归因于其精神性质；习惯上经由清澈的精神之眼进入，愉悦我们的灵魂并推动它去爱这样的对象；这就是我们所说的美。它也存在于听觉的对象之中，如美丽的演说、声音、言语、歌曲、音乐、协和、比例与和谐。因为在这些东西的精神性质中找到了优雅，它通过精神听觉的中介推动灵魂去愉悦和去爱。因此，优雅与美存在于具有精神性质的美丽事物之中（*sensi spirituali*）。[^note-22]

en: Based on this and other passages, Judah argues that it is primarily by means of the beauty of created things that the individual is able to apprehend and move towards incorporeal or spiritual Beauty. Love is what is ultimately responsible for directing the soul and the intellect of the individual to increasingly spiritual matters.
zh: 基于这一段和其他段落，犹大论证：主要借受造物之美，个体才能领会并走向无形或精神的美。爱最终负责把个体的灵魂与理智导向越来越精神化的事物。

en: 4. Philosophy of Beauty
zh: 4 美的哲学

en: 4.1 The Elevation of Rhetoric, Aesthetics, and the Imagination
zh: 4.1 修辞学、美学与想象力的提升

en: We witness the further departure of Judah’s thought from that of his predecessors when we examine his discussion of rhetoric and aesthetics. Medieval Aristotelians tended to locate rhetoric in the *trivium* (which also included logic and dialectic), and, thus, as propaedeutic to “higher” sciences such as metaphysics. In the Renaissance, however, eloquence was equated with wisdom, and the good rhetorician had to be proficient in all branches of human knowledge. This led many Jewish Renaissance thinkers to examine not only the classical authors (e.g., Cicero and Quintilian), but also to mine the Bible for its use of language and style. Whereas Maimonides and other Jewish Aristotelians had been interested in biblical rhetoric as a means to reproduce imaginative representations of philosophical truths to those unlearned in philosophy, Renaissance thinkers held that rhetoric was the art form *par excellence*, one that enabled the individual to command respect in public life.[^note-23]
zh: 考察犹大关于修辞学与美学的讨论时，可以进一步看到他的思想与其先驱的分离。中世纪亚里士多德倾向于把修辞学置于 *trivium*（还包括逻辑与辩证法）中，因而作为“更高”科学（如形而上学）的入门准备。而在文艺复兴中，雄辩被等同于智慧，好的修辞家必须精通人类知识的一切分支。这使得许多犹太文艺复兴思想家不仅考察古典作家（如西塞罗和昆体良），还从圣经中挖掘其语言与风格的运用。迈蒙尼德和其他犹太亚里士多德主义者曾将圣经修辞学作为一种手段，向未学过哲学的人再现哲学真理的想象性表征；而文艺复兴思想家则认为修辞学是 *par excellence* 的艺术形式，使个人能够在公共生活中赢得尊重。[^note-23]

en: Furthermore, following Maimonides (e.g., *Guide* I.2), many medieval thinkers envisaged beauty as contingent upon consensus and not a matter of the intellectual faculty. In the Renaissance, by contrast, beauty was elevated to an ideal that, *inter alia*, moved the intellect, by means of desire, to either perfect that which exists below it or to be perfected by that above. This principle was subsequently shared by philosophers, poets, and visual artists, and, quite frequently, there existed a fluid line separating these professions.
zh: 此外，跟随迈蒙尼德（如《迷途指津》I.2），许多中世纪思想家设想美取决于共识而非理智官能。而在文艺复兴中，美被提升为一种理想，它尤其通过欲望推动理智，去完善其下之物或被其上者完善。这一原则随后被哲学家、诗人和视觉艺术家共享，而且经常存在将这些职业分隔开的流动界线。

en: This elevation of rhetoric and aesthetics in the Renaissance led to a subsequent interest in the imagination, a faculty frequently mistrusted, but often deemed necessary to medieval political philosophy. Mistrusted because, following Plato’s critique, the imagination had the power to deceive and distort; yet, at the same time necessary because the imagination was the defining element of prophecy. (In medieval Aristotelianism, the prophet was regarded as a perfect philosopher with a perfected imaginative faculty to coin images for the uneducated masses.) Only now, because Judah was not particularly concerned with philosophical esotericism, the products of the imagination, i.e., images, were not to be appreciated on a pedagogical level alone, but more importantly on an aesthetic one. Following Ficino, Judah argues that the artist—more specifically, the artist’s imagination—becomes the vessel through which God speaks.[^note-24]
zh: 文艺复兴中修辞学与美学的这种提升，导致了对想象力的后续兴趣。想象力是一个经常不被信任、但在中世纪政治哲学中常被视为必要的官能。不被信任是因为，跟随柏拉图的批评，想象力有欺骗和扭曲的力量；但同时又是必要的，因为想象力是预言的定义性元素。（在中世纪亚里士多德主义中，先知被视为一个完美的哲学家，拥有为未受教育的大众铸造意象的完善想象官能。）只是现在，因为犹大并不特别关心哲学秘传主义，想象力的产物——即意象——不应仅在教学层面上被欣赏，更重要的是在美学层面上。跟随费奇诺，犹大论证：艺术家——更具体地说，艺术家的想象力——成为上帝借以言说的器皿。[^note-24]

en: 4.2 Cosmology and Metaphysics
zh: 4.2 宇宙论与形而上学

en: Although there exists an intimate connection between sensual and cosmic beauty it is by means of the latter that Judah frames his discussion of cosmology, ontology, and psychology. Beauty, to reiterate, is what inspires love and desire, and thereby connects all levels of the universe into an interlocking and organic relationship. The result is that everything, both sensual and intelligible, has the potential to image and reflect God’s beauty.
zh: 虽然感官美与宇宙美之间存在密切联系，但犹大是借后者来框架其宇宙论、存在论与心理学的讨论的。美，重申一下，是激发爱与欲望的东西，从而把宇宙的所有层次连接成一种相互锁定、有机的关系。其结果是：一切事物，无论感官的还是可理解的，都有可能映照和反映上帝的美。

en: Judah’s cosmology is a case in point. In the *Dialoghi* he presents two distinct accounts of the origin of the universe. This issue—viz., was the universe created or is it eternal—was one of the touchstones in the debate not only between philosophers and non-philosophers, but also among philosophers. At stake in these debates was God’s omnipotence and omniscience: If the world was created, then clearly God is transcendent to the world as both its Creator and Sustainer; if not, then God’s power to act is potentially curtailed by another principle’s eternality. In his discussion of these matters, Judah adopts two models: one based on Islamicate Neoplatonism and the other on the Plotinian triad.
zh: 犹大的宇宙论是一个例证。在《对话集》中他提出了关于宇宙起源的两种不同的说明。这一问题——宇宙是被创造的还是永恒的——不仅是哲学家与非哲学家之间论辩的试金石，也是哲学家之间论辩的试金石。这些辩论的利害是上帝的全能与全知：如果世界是被创造的，那么显然上帝超越于世界，既是创造者又是维系者；如果不是，那么上帝的行动力量就可能被另一个原则的永恒性所削减。在对这些问题的讨论中，犹大采纳了两种模型：一种基于伊斯兰世界的新柏拉图主义，另一种基于普罗提诺的三一体。

en: According to the first model, Judah argues—citing Ghazali, Avicenna and Maimonides—that God in His complete simplicity and “by the love of His infinite beauty produces out of Himself alone the first intelligence and mover of the first heaven” (*con l’amore de la sua immense bellezza immediate da sé sola la prima intelligenzia movtrice del primo cielo produce*).[^note-25] The first intelligence, in turn, contemplates (1) the beauty of its cause to produce the second intellect, and (2) its own beauty to produce the first heavenly sphere. This theory of emanation, based on the love of beauty,[^note-26] pervades the entire universe (both supra- and sub-lunar). The Active Intellect, the lowest of the ten heavenly intellects and associated with the sphere of the moon, becomes the intellect of the corporeal world. By contemplating its own beauty it produces the forms found in this world, and in contemplating the beauty of its cause, it produces human intellects. Following this, Judah offers a Plotinian account based on a celestial triad.[^note-27] He now distinguishes between three types of beauty that pervade the cosmos. The first is God *qua* the Source of beauty (*l’attore di bellezza*), the second is beauty itself (*bellezza*; i.e., intelligible beauty), and the third is the physical universe produced by this idea in the intellect of God (*il participante di bellezza*).[^note-28]
zh: 按第一种模型，犹大论证——引用安萨里、阿维森纳和迈蒙尼德——上帝以其完全的单纯性、“借对其无限之美的爱，从其自身独自产生第一天球的第一理智和第一推动者”（*con l'amore de la sua immense bellezza immediate da sé sola la prima intelligenzia movtrice del primo cielo produce*）。[^note-25]第一理智转而沉思 (1) 其原因的美以产生第二理智，(2) 自身的美以产生第一天球。这一基于对美的爱的流溢理论[^note-26]遍布整个宇宙（超月与月下）。主动理智——十个天球理智中最低的、与月球天球相联——成为物质世界的理智。通过沉思自身的美，它产生这个世界中的诸形式；通过沉思其原因的美，它产生人的理智。此后，犹大提供了一个基于天界三一体的普罗提诺式说明。[^note-27]他现在区分了遍在宇宙的三种类型的美。第一是上帝作为美的施予者（*l'attore di bellezza*），第二是美本身（*bellezza*，即可理解的美），第三是由上帝理智中的这一理念所产生的物理宇宙（*il participante di bellezza*）。[^note-28]

en: Judah subsequently uses the latter model, combined with kabbalistic embellishment, to interpret the first creation account in Genesis, where the physical world is now described as the offspring between God, the male principle, and intelligible beauty, now personified as a female.[^note-29] Corporeal beauty, according to this model, becomes the primogeniture of God’s love for His female consort, wisdom. Since this physical world is intimately connected to God, it cannot be negated. Rather, this world becomes necessary, and this is a leitmotiv that runs throughout the work, for humans to make physical beauty “spiritual in our intellect.”[^note-30] One must, in other words, orientate oneself towards sensible beauty in such a manner that one reverses the ontological chain.
zh: 犹大随后使用后一模型，结合喀巴拉的润饰，来解释《创世记》中的第一个创造叙事，其中物质世界现在被描述为上帝（男性原则）与可理解的美（现在被拟人化为女性）之间的后代。[^note-29]按此模型，物质美成为上帝对其女性配偶——智慧——之爱的长子。由于这个物理世界与上帝密切相关，它不能被否定。毋宁说，这个世界成为必要的——这是贯穿全书的主题——因为人类要使物质美“在我们的理智中精神化”。[^note-30]换言之，人必须以某种方式朝向感官之美定向，以致逆转存在论的链条。

en: 4.3 Psychology and Prophecy
zh: 4.3 心理学与预言

en: The above discussion is directly related to the way in which Judah’s envisages both psychology and prophecy. According to him, the five external senses divide into (1) those that are primarily material (*materiali*): touch (*tatto*), taste (*gusto*), and smell (*odorato*); and (2) those that are increasingly spiritual (*spirituali*): hearing (*per l’audito*) and sight (*per l’occhi*).[^note-31] It seems that only the latter are able to penetrate behind the purely physical so as to abstract the spiritual from the corporeal. Hearing, intimately connected to the Renaissance ideal of rhetoric, consists of the ability to discern “fine speeches, excellent reasoning, beautiful verses, sweet music, and beautiful and harmonious melodies.”[^note-32] Sight, ranked just above the faculty of hearing, owing to the primacy that Judah puts on vision, deals with “beautiful colors, regular patterns, and light in all its varied splendor.”[^note-33] The senses, thus, function hierarchically as a prolegomenon to any form of higher knowledge, with the imagination forming the threshold (*mezzo*) between the senses and the intellect.
zh: 上述讨论直接关系到犹大构想心理学与预言的方式。按他的看法，五种外部感觉分为 (1) 主要物质性的（*materiali*）：触觉（*tatto*）、味觉（*gusto*）和嗅觉（*odorato*）；和 (2) 日益精神性的（*spirituali*）：听觉（*per l'audito*）和视觉（*per l'occhi*）。[^note-31]似乎只有后者能够穿透纯粹的物质层，从有形之物中抽象出精神的东西。听觉——与文艺复兴的修辞学理想密切相关——包含辨别“优美的演说、出色的推理、美丽的诗篇、甜蜜的音乐、美丽而和谐的旋律”的能力。[^note-32]视觉——由于犹大赋予视觉的优先性而排在听觉之上——处理“美丽的色彩、规则的图案、以及各种壮丽的光”。[^note-33]因此，感觉作为任何更高级知识的先导按层级运作，而想象力构成感觉与理智之间的中介（*mezzo*）。

en: Central to the unfolding argument in the *Dialoghi* is the concept of ocular power (*forza oculare*). In the first dialogue, Judah describes two modes of apprehending spiritual matters. The first is through the faculty of sight and the second through the intellect.[^note-34] For the eye, like the intellect, is illumined by means of light, thereby establishing a relationship between the eye, the object seen, and the space that separates them.[^note-35] Just as the sun supplies light to the eye, the divine intellect illumines the human intellect during the act of intellection. It is light, then, that enables us to “comprehend all the beautiful shining objects of the corporeal world.”[^note-36] Sight becomes the model by which we engage the universe: it is what makes knowledge possible since it is only through vision of tangible particulars that we acquire knowledge of intelligibles.
zh: 《对话集》中展开论证的核心是目力（*forza oculare*）概念。在第一篇对话中，犹大描述了把握精神事物的两种模式：通过视觉官能和通过理智。[^note-34]因为眼睛如同理智一样被光照亮，从而在眼睛、被看见的对象和分隔它们的空间之间建立了一种关系。[^note-35]正如太阳为眼睛提供光，神圣理智在理智活动中照亮人类理智。是光使我们能够“理解物质世界中所有美丽的发光对象”。[^note-36]视觉成为我们切近宇宙的模型：它使知识成为可能，因为只有通过对可感殊例的观看，我们才获得对可理解者的知识。

en: Judah subsequently distinguishes between three types of vision. The highest type is that of God’s visual apprehension of himself; following this is that associated with the angelic world, which sees God directly though not on equal terms; finally, there is human vision, which is the weakest of the three types and can only visualize the divine indirectly.[^note-37] The best that most humans can do in this world is to obtain knowledge of incorporeal essences through corporeal particulars. Judah does admit, though, that some special individuals are able to unite with the angelic world, which he describes as the Agent Intellect (*intelleto agente*). When such unification (*copulare*) occurs, the individual “sees and desires divine beauty as in a crystal or a clear mirror, but not directly” (*vede e desia la bellezza divine come in uno mezzo cristiallino, o sia chiaro specchio, ma non in se stessa immediate*).[^note-38] Judah refers to this act as prophecy. Like Maimonides, Judah claims that Moses did not prophesy through the imagination, but only through the intellect, which he nevertheless describes in highly visual terms as beholding “the most beautiful figure of God” (*la bellissima figura di Dio*).[^note-39]
zh: 犹大随后区分了三种视觉。最高类型是上帝对自身的视觉把握；其次是天使世界的视觉——直接看见上帝但非平等地；最后是人的视觉——三者中最弱的类型，只能间接地观想神圣。[^note-37]大多数人在这世界上所能做的最好之事，是通过有形殊例获得无形本质的知识。但犹大确实承认，某些特殊的个人能够与天使世界——他描述为主动理智（*intelleto agente*）——合一。当这种合一（*copulare*）发生时，个体“看见并渴望神圣之美，如在水晶或明镜中一般，而非直接地”（*vede e desia la bellezza divine come in uno mezzo cristiallino, o sia chiaro specchio, ma non in se stessa immediate*）。[^note-38]犹大将这种活动称为预言。与迈蒙尼德一样，犹大主张摩西不是通过想象力预言，而是仅通过理智——但他以高度视觉性的措辞将后者描述为直观“上帝的最美的形象”（*la bellissima figura di Dio*）。[^note-39]

en: In the third dialogue, Abrabanel further divides the human into a tripartite structure consisting of the body (*il corpo*), the soul (*l’anima*), and the intellect (*l’intelletto*).[^note-40] The soul, which I have interpreted as the imaginative faculty because of the properties assigned to it,[^note-41] is once again the intermediary (*mezzo*) between the body (and the senses) and the intellect.[^note-42] Although he does not come right out and define the functioning of the soul in any detail, he does claim that it is indispensable to the proper working of the body and the intellect. Moreover, it is this faculty that is in constant danger of being corrupted by unhealthy corporeal desire and, most importantly for the present, it is ultimately responsible for translating the corporeal into the incorporeal and *vice versa*. This soul, in turn,
zh: 在第三篇对话中，阿布拉瓦内尔进一步把人划分为三元结构：身体（*il corpo*）、灵魂（*l'anima*）与理智（*l'intelletto*）。[^note-40]灵魂——鉴于赋予它的性质，我将其解释为想象官能[^note-41]——再次是身体（及感官）与理智之间的中介（*mezzo*）。[^note-42]虽然他没有直接详细定义灵魂的运作，但他确实声称它对身体和理智的正常运作不可或缺。而且，正是这一官能始终面临被不健康的有形欲望败坏的危险；就当前而言最重要的是，它最终负责把有形者转译为无形者，反之亦然。这个灵魂，转而，

en: has two faces (*due faccie*) , like those of the moon turned towards the sun and the earth respectively, the one being turned towards the intellect above it, and the other toward the body below. The first face looking towards the intellect is the understanding with which the soul reasons of universals and spiritual knowledge, extracting the forms and intellectual essences from particular and sensible bodies (*estraendo le forme ed essenzie intellettuali da li particulari e sensibili corpi*)…the second face turned towards the body is sense, which is particular knowledge of corporeal things known … These two faces have contrary or opposed notions; and as our soul with its upper face or understanding makes the corporeal incorporeal (*l’incorporeo al corporeo*), so the lower face, or sensible cognition, approaching the objects of sense and mingling with them, draws the incorporeal to the corporeal.[^note-43]
zh: 有两副面孔（*due faccie*），如同月亮分别朝向太阳和地球的面孔：一副朝向其上的理智，另一副朝向其下的身体。朝向理智的第一副面孔是理解力，灵魂借此推理普遍性与精神知识，从殊例和可感的身体中提取形式与理智本质（*estraendo le forme ed essenzie intellettuali da li particulari e sensibili corpi*）……朝向身体的第二副面孔是感觉，即对被认识的有形事物的殊例知识……这两副面孔具有相反或对立的观念；正如我们的灵魂以其上面的面孔或理解力把有形者变为无形者（*l'incorporeo al corporeo*），下面的面孔或感官认知则接近感觉对象并与它们混合，把无形者拉向有形者。[^note-43]

en: 5. Philosophy of Love
zh: 5 爱的哲学

en: 5.1 Judah’s Recasting of Love as a Philosophical Principle
zh: 5.1 犹大将爱重构为哲学原理

en: The traditional philosophical notion of love, going back at least to the time of Plato, is that love results from the imperfection and privation of that which loves. One loves, in other words, what one does not possess (see, e.g., Plato, *Symposium* 200a-201e).[^note-44] Accordingly, that which is imperfect loves that which is perfect, and, that which is perfect (i.e., God) neither loves nor desires. Aristotle likewise claimed that that which is less perfect (e.g., slaves, children, wives and ruled) should have more love for that which is more perfect (e.g., freeborn, parents, husbands, and rulers) than *vice versa*. The First Cause, then, is loved but does not love. This discussion would predominate from Late Antiquity to the Middle Ages.
zh: 传统的哲学爱的观念至少可追溯到柏拉图时代：爱产生于爱者之不完善与匮乏。换言之，一个人爱的东西是自己不拥有的（如柏拉图《会饮篇》200a-201e）。[^note-44]因此，不完善者爱完善者，而完善者（即上帝）既不爱也不渴望。亚里士多德同样声称，较不完善者（如奴隶、儿童、妻子和被统治者）应当对较完善者（如自由人、父母、丈夫和统治者）有更多的爱，反之则不然。第一因被爱但不爱。这一讨论从古代晚期一直延续到中世纪。

en: Judah’s theory of love, by contrast, was intimately connected to the literary interests of humanism and the aesthetic sensibilities of Renaissance artists.[^note-45] As a consequence, Judah faults previous thinkers for (1) not ascribing love to God and (2) confining their discussion of love primarily to that between humans, thereby ignoring the dynamic role of God in relationships based on this principle. Using the name of Plato as a metonym for other philosophers, he is critical of this approach:
zh: 犹大的爱的理论与此形成对照，它与人文主义的文学兴趣和文艺复兴艺术家的审美感受力密切相关。[^note-45]结果是，犹大批评以前的思想家：(1) 没有把爱归于上帝，(2) 把爱的讨论主要限于人际关系，从而忽略了上帝在这一原理所建立的关系中的动态角色。以柏拉图之名作为其他哲学家的转喻，他批评这一进路：

en: Plato in his *Symposium* discusses only the kind of love that is found in men, which has its final cause in the lover but not in the beloved (*terminato ne l’amante ma non ne l’amato*), for this kind mainly is called love, since that which ends in the loved one is called friendship and benevolence (*ché quel che si termina ne l’amato si chiama amicizia e benivolenzia*). He rightly defines this love as a desire of beauty (*desiderio di bellezza*). He says that such love is not found in God, because that which desires beauty and doesn’t have it is not beautiful, and God, who is the highest beauty, does not lack beauty nor can he desire it, whence he cannot have love, that is, of such a kind (*Tale amore dice che non si truova in Dio, però che quel che desia bellezza non l’ha né è bello, e a Dio, che è sommo bello, non gli manca bellezza né la può desiare, onde non può avere amore, cioè di tal sorte*).[^note-46]
zh: 柏拉图在《会饮篇》中只讨论了在人中发现的爱的类型，其终极因在于爱者而非被爱者（*terminato ne l'amante ma non ne l'amato*），因为这种才主要被称为爱，而终于被爱者的那种被称为友谊和善意（*ché quel che si termina ne l'amato si chiama amicizia e benivolenzia*）。他正确定义这种爱为对美的欲望（*desiderio di bellezza*）。他说这种爱在上帝中不存在，因为渴望美而不拥有美的人不是美的，而上帝作为最高的美，不缺乏美，也不能渴望它，因此他不能拥有爱，即这种类型的爱（*Tale amore dice che non si truova in Dio, però che quel che desia bellezza non l'ha né è bello, e a Dio, che è sommo bello, non gli manca bellezza né la può desiare, onde non può avere amore, cioè di tal sorte*）。[^note-46]

en: Judah seeks to provide a corrective to this and, in the process, offer what he considers to be a more comprehensive theory of love. In particular, he intertwines love and beauty such that the lover of beauty seeks to unite with the source of beauty, something that the lover subsequently seeks to reproduce himself (the lover is always male, according to Judah because it is responsible for impregnating the passive and receptive female principle). This can take the form of God’s creation of the universe, the artist’s creation of a work of art, and the philosopher’s composition of a pleasing work of philosophy. In his discussion of love, Judah also departs from other Renaissance thinkers. Whereas Ficino had equated human love with sensual love between humans, Judah, drawing upon Maimonidean precedents, resignifies human love as, on one level, that which the intellect has for God.[^note-47]
zh: 犹大力图对此提供纠正，并在此过程中提供他所认为的更全面的爱的理论。特别是，他把爱与美交织在一起，使得美的爱者寻求与美的源头合一，而爱者随后力图复制这种爱（按犹大的说法，爱者总是男性，因为它负责使被动而接受性的女性原则受孕）。这可以采取上帝创造宇宙、艺术家创作艺术作品、或哲学家撰写令人愉悦的哲学著作的形式。在讨论爱时，犹大也偏离了其他文艺复兴思想家。费奇诺把人的爱等同于人际间的感官爱；而犹大借迈蒙尼德的先例，将人的爱重新意指为——在某一层面上——理智对上帝的爱。[^note-47]

en: Perhaps, Judah’s biggest departure from earlier thinkers is his ascription of love to God. Here, however, his discussion is not entirely new; rather, he picks up on a number of issues discussed in the work of Hasdai Crescas (ca. 1340–ca. 1410), the important critic of Aristotelianism and Maimonideanism. For Crescas, breaking from both the Platonic and Aristotelian positions, love need not be associated with privation or imperfection:
zh: 也许犹大与先前思想家最大的分歧，是他把爱归于上帝。但这里的讨论并非完全新颖；他承接了哈斯代·克雷斯卡斯（约 1340–约 1410）——亚里士多德主义和迈蒙尼德主义的重要批评者——著作中讨论的若干问题。对克雷斯卡斯而言，打破了柏拉图和亚里士多德的立场，爱不必与匮乏或不完善相联：

en: Inasmuch as it is known that God, may He be blessed, is the sources and fountain of all perfection, and in virtue of his perfection, which is His essence, He loves the good, as may be seen from His actions in bringing into existence the entire universe, sustaining it perpetually, and continuously creating it anew, and all be means of His simple will, it must necessarily be that the love of the good is an essential property of perfection. It follows from this that the greater perfection [of the lover] the greater will be the love and the pleasure in the desire.[^note-48]
zh: 既然已知上帝——愿祂受颂扬——是一切完善的源泉与泉涌，凭借其完善——即其本质——祂爱善，这从祂的行动中可见：使整个宇宙存在、永久维系之、不断重新创造之，这一切都借其单纯的意志；必然的结论是：对善的爱是完善的本质属性。由此推出：［爱者的］完善越大，爱与欲望中的愉悦就越大。[^note-48]

en: Love, for Crescas, is tantamount to God’s creative activity. In the third book of the *Dialoghi* Judah picks up this theme:
zh: 对克雷斯卡斯来说，爱等同于上帝的创造活动。在《对话集》第三卷中，犹大接过了这一主题：

en: Divine Love (*L’amor divino*) is the inclination (*tendenzia*) of God’s most beautiful wisdom toward the likeness of His own beauty, to wit, the universe created by Him, together with its return to union with His supreme wisdom; and His pleasure is the perfect union of His image with Himself (*la perfetta unione di sua immagine in se stesso*), and of His created universe with Himself as Creator.[^note-49]
zh: 神圣之爱（*L'amor divino*）是上帝最美的智慧朝向其自身美之肖像——即祂所创造的宇宙——的倾向（*tendenzia*），连同其向与祂的至高智慧合一的回归；而祂的愉悦是祂的肖像与祂自身的完美合一（*la perfetta unione di sua immagine in se stesso*），以及祂所创造的宇宙与作为创造者的祂自身的合一。[^note-49]

en: Judah’s subsequent discussion of love, however, departs significantly from either Crescas or other Renaissance thinkers. This is especially the case when it comes to Judah’s refusal to abnegate sensual love. Rather, he celebrates such love as the gateway to cosmic or spiritual love. Sensual love, for him, becomes that which orientates the individual towards the Divine. Unlike Crescas, however, Judah does not reject the Maimonidean concept of God as divine intellect. Furthermore, Judah’s discussion finds no homolog in the thought of Crescas or even Maimonides when it comes to the concept of God’s beauty.
zh: 犹大后续关于爱的讨论，显著地偏离了克雷斯卡斯或其他文艺复兴思想家。当他拒绝弃绝感官之爱时尤其如此。他反而颂扬这种爱是通往宇宙之爱或精神之爱的门户。感官之爱对他来说，成为使个体朝向神圣者定向的东西。与克雷斯卡斯不同，犹大并不拒绝迈蒙尼德将上帝作为神圣理智的概念。而且，犹大的讨论在上帝之美的概念上，在克雷斯卡斯甚至迈蒙尼德的思想中都找不到同源物。

en: 5.2 “The Circle of Love” (*il circulo degli amari*)
zh: 5.2 “爱的循环”（*il circulo degli amari*）

en: Near the end of the third dialogue, Judah introduces the “circle of love,” *il circulo degli amari*, as follows:
zh: 在第三篇对话的结尾处，犹大引入了“爱的循环”（*il circulo degli amari*）：

en: The circle of all things (*il circulo di tutte*) begins from their first origin, and passing successively through each thing in turn, returns to its first origin as to its ultimate end (*ultimo fine*), thus containing every degree of being in its circular form (*comprendendo tutti li gradi de le cose a modo circulare*), so that the point which is the beginning also comes to be the end. This circle has two halves (*due mezzi*), the first from the beginning to the point most distant from it, the mid-point, and the second from this mid-point to the beginning again.[^note-50]
zh: 万物的循环（*il circulo di tutte*）从它们的最初源头开始，依次经过每一物，回到其最初源头如同回到终极终点（*ultimo fine*），从而以其循环形式包含存在的每一层级（*comprendendo tutti li gradi de le cose a modo circulare*），使得作为起点的那个点同时也成为终点。这个循环有两个半圆（*due mezzi*），第一个从起点到离它最远的点即中点，第二个从这个中点回到起点。[^note-50]

en: This circle, in other words, begins with the divine, whose love creates and sustains the universe: “each degree of being with paternal love procreates its immediate inferior, imparting its being or paternal beauty to it, although in a lesser degree as is only fitting.”[^note-51] This emanative framework, the love of that which is more beautiful for that which is less beautiful, comprises the first half of the circle. Every thing in the universe exists on a hierarchical chain of being, from the pure actuality of the divine to the pure potentiality of prime matter. Just as the superior desires the perfection of the inferior, the inferior desires to unite with the superior. The first half of the circle spans from God to utter chaos, whereas, the second half of this circle works in reverse. It is the love of the inferior for the superior, predicated on the former’s privation and subsequent desire to unite with the superior.
zh: 换言之，这个循环始于神圣者——其爱创造并维系宇宙：“存在的每一层级以父爱的力量生育其直接的较低者，把它的存在或父性之美传递给它，尽管在较低程度上——这是唯一恰当的。”[^note-51]这一流溢框架——较美者对较不美者的爱——构成循环的前半部分。宇宙中的每一物都存在于存在的层级链上，从神圣者的纯粹现实到原初质料的纯粹潜能。正如较高者渴望较低者的完善，较低者渴望与较高者合一。循环的前半部分从上帝延伸至完全的混沌，而循环的后半部分反向运作。它是较低者对较高者的爱，以前者的匮乏及其随后与较高者合一的欲望为基础。

en: 6. The End of Human Life
zh: 6 人的终极目的

en: The *telos* of Judah’s system occurs when the intellect is “absorbed in the science of the Divine and of things abstracted from matter, rejoicing in and becoming enamored of the highest grace and beauty which is in the creator and artificer of all things, so that it attains its ultimate happiness.”[^note-52] Within this context, Judah employs a well-known and well-used metaphor in his discussion of the imaginative faculty, that of the mirror (*specchio*).[^note-53] In the medieval Islamicate philosophical tradition, following Plotinus, the mirror (Ar. *mir’â*), is frequently used as an image for the perfected soul, at whose vanguard resides the intellect.[^note-54] Just as the mirror reflects what is placed in front of it, the soul, in a state of perfection, reflects the higher principles of the universe. Early on in the *Dialoghi*, Philo asks Sophia, “Do you not see how the form of man is impressed on and received by a mirror, not as a complete human being, but within the limits of the mirror’s powers and capabilities, which reflect the figure only and not the essence.”[^note-55] Later, in dialogue three, he argues that it is through our own “intellectual mirror” that we apprehend the divine:
zh: 犹大体系的 *telos*（终极目的）出现在理智“沉浸于关于神圣者和从质料中抽象出来的事物的科学之中，欣喜于并迷恋那最高的优雅与美——那是万物创造者和匠人中的美——以致它达到其终极幸福”之时。[^note-52]在这一语境中，犹大在讨论想象官能时使用了一个众所周知且常用的隐喻：镜子（*specchio*）。[^note-53]在中世纪伊斯兰哲学传统中，跟随普罗提诺，镜子（阿语 *mirʼâ*）经常被用作完善灵魂的意象，理智居于其前锋。[^note-54]正如镜子反射放在它面前的东西，完善状态中的灵魂反映宇宙的更高原则。在《对话集》的早期，菲洛问索菲亚：“你难道没有看到人的形式如何被印在一面镜子上并被它接收，不是作为完整的人，而是在镜子之力与能力的限度之内，它只反映形象而不反映本质。”[^note-55]后来，在第三篇对话中，他论证我们正是通过自己的“理智之镜”来把握神圣：

en: It is enough for our intellectual mirror (*specchio intellettuale*) to receive and image (*figurare*) the infinite divine essence (*l’immensa essenzia divina*) according to the capacity of its intellectual nature; though there is a measureless gulf fixed between them, so far does its nature fall short of that of the object of its understanding.[^note-56]
zh: 我们的理智之镜（*specchio intellettuale*）按其理智本性的容量来接收并描画（*figurare*）无限的神圣本质（*l'immensa essenzia divina*）就足够了；尽管它们之间有不可度量的鸿沟，其本性远不及它所理解的对象的本性。[^note-56]

en: By corporealizing the spiritual and spiritualizing the corporeal, the intellect, in tandem with the imagination, enables individuals to gain knowledge of the divine world. Unlike Maimonides and other medieval Aristotelians who equated the natural world with impermanence and evil, Judah argues that this world is the natural receptacle of heavenly powers: “Hence earth is the proper and regular consort of heaven, whereof the other elements are but paramours. For it is upon the earth that heaven begets all on the greater part of its progeny.”[^note-57] In an interesting passage, Judah, like Maimonides before him, compares matter to a harlot.[^note-58] Yet, unlike Maimonides, he reaches a radically different conclusion. For Judah, “it is this adulterous love that beautifies the lower world with such wondrous variety of the fair-formed things.”[^note-59] In keeping with Judah’s claim that “the lower can be found in the higher,”[^note-60] this world becomes one gigantic mirror that reflects spiritual beauty, and in which one can grasp divine intelligibles.[^note-61] Just as Philo is enthralled by Sophia’s beauty, the individual, upon contemplating physical objects that are beautiful, apprehends the divine:
zh: 通过使精神者有形化、使有形者精神化，理智与想象力协同，使个体获得对神圣世界的知识。与迈蒙尼德和其他中世纪亚里士多德主义者把自然世界等同于无常与恶不同，犹大论证这个世界是天体力们的自然容器：“因此大地是天穹固有的常规配偶，其他元素不过是妻妾。因为正是在大地上，天穹生出其大部分后代。”[^note-57]在一个有趣的段落中，犹大像之前的迈蒙尼德一样，把质料比作娼妓。[^note-58]然而与迈蒙尼德不同，他得出了一个截然不同的结论。对犹大而言，“正是这种不贞的爱，以如此奇妙多样的美丽形式装饰了下界”。[^note-59]与犹大的主张——“较低者可以在较高者中被找到”——[^note-60]相一致，这个世界成为一面映照精神之美的巨大镜子，人们可以在其中把握神圣的可理解者。[^note-61]正如菲洛被索菲亚的美所迷住，个体在沉思美丽的物理对象时把握到神圣：

en: God has implanted His image and likeness in His creatures through the finite beauty imparted to them from His surpassing beauty. And the image of the infinite must be finite, otherwise it would not be a copy, but that of which it is the image. The infinite beauty of the Creator is depicted and reflected in finite created beauty like a beautiful face in a mirror and although the image is not commensurate with its divine pattern, nonetheless it will be its copy, portrait, and true likeness (*Si depinge e immagina la bellezza infinita del creatore ne la bellezza finita creata come una bella figura in uno specchio: non però commisura l’immagine il divino immaginato, ma bene gli sará simulacro similitudine e immagine*).[^note-62]
zh: 上帝通过从其超越之美中分予受造物的有限之美，将祂的形象与样式植入祂的受造物之中。无限的形像必定是有限的，否则它就不是形像，而是形像所本之源。创造者的无限之美被描绘和反映在有限的受造之美中，如一面镜中的美丽面孔；虽然形像与其神圣原型不相称，但它仍然是其摹本、肖像和真正的形像（*Si depinge e immagina la bellezza infinita del creatore ne la bellezza finita creata come una bella figura in uno specchio: non però commisura l'immagine il divino immaginato, ma bene gli sará simulacro similitudine e immagine*）。[^note-62]

en: It is ultimately the love of beauty in the soul of the individual, combined with the cognizance that one lacks it in its entirety, that moves not only the soul of the individual, but also the entire cosmos. Virtuous love, which Philo answers in response to Sophia’s fourth question concerning the parents of love, is the highest form of love and, significantly, one can have this for either corporeal or spiritual things. Indeed, Philo intimates that such virtuous love can only emerge from sensible phenomena:[^note-63]
zh: 最终，是个体灵魂中对美的爱——结合对其未整体拥有美的认知——推动的不仅是个体的灵魂，还有整个宇宙。德性之爱——菲洛用以回应索菲亚关于“爱的父母”之第四问的答案——是爱的最高形式；而且重要的是，无论对有形之物还是精神之物都可以怀有这种爱。事实上，菲洛暗示这种德性之爱只能从感官现象中产生：[^note-63]

en: When [the soul] perceives a beautiful person whose beauty is in harmony with itself, it recognizes in and through this beauty, divine beauty, in the image of which this person is also made.[^note-64]
zh: 当［灵魂］知觉到一个人，其美与自身之美和谐相称时，它在这种美之中并借这种美认识到神圣之美——这个人也是按这神圣之美的形象受造的。[^note-64]

en: The goal of Judah’s system is to ascend through this hierarchy, that gateway to which is the sensual enjoyment that one derives from physical objects. Only after this can one appreciate spiritual beauty, an appreciation of which culminates in basking in the divine presence. Judah discusses this process in the following manner:
zh: 犹大体系的目标是沿这一层级上升，通往其间的门户是从物理对象中获得的感官愉悦。只有在此之后才能欣赏精神之美，而对其的欣赏最终终结于沐浴在神圣临在之中。犹大以下列方式讨论这一过程：

en: We ought principally to love the higher forms of beauty separated from formless matter and gross corporeality (*amiamo le grandi bellezze separate da la deforme material e brutto corpe*) , such as the virtues and the sciences, which are ever beautiful and devoid of all ugliness and defect. Here again we may ascend through a hierarchy of beauty from the lesser to the greater (*ascendiamo per le minori a le maggiori bellezze*) and from the pure to the purest leading to the knowledge and love, not only of the most beautiful intelligences, souls and motors of the heavenly bodies, but also of the highest beauty and of the supremely beautiful, the giver of all beauty, life, intelligence and being. We may scale this ladder only when we put away earthly garments and material affection (*potremo fare quando noi abbandonaremo le vesti corporee e le passioni materiali*)…[^note-65]
zh: 我们应当首先爱那些从无形质料和粗笨形体中分离出来的高级的美（*amiamo le grandi bellezze separate da la deforme material e brutto corpe*），如诸德性与诸科学，它们永远美丽、毫无丑陋与缺陷。这里我们再次可以沿美的层级从较小的上升到较大的（*ascendiamo per le minori a le maggiori bellezze*），从纯粹的到最纯粹的，导向对最美的诸理智、诸灵魂和天体之推动者，以及对最高的美和至美的——一切美、生命、理智和存在的给予者——的认识和爱。只有当我们脱下尘世的衣裳和物质的执着（*potremo fare quando noi abbandonaremo le vesti corporee e le passioni materiali*）……我们才能攀登这个阶梯。[^note-65]

en: Even though the corporeal was, at the outset of this journey, indispensable; the higher one moves up the hierarchy the less important the material becomes. As far as the individual is concerned, the highest felicity resides in the union with God, which the Italian describes erotically as *felice coppulativa*:
zh: 尽管有形之物在旅程之初不可或缺，沿层级上升越高，物质就越不重要。就个体而言，最高的福祉在于与上帝的合一——意大利文以情爱的措辞将其描述为 *felice coppulativa*：

en: Because the love of the human soul is twofold, it is directed not only towards the beauty of the intellect, but also towards the image of that beauty in the body. It happens that at times the love of intellectual beauty is so strong that it draws the soul to cast off all affection for the body; thus the body and soul in man fall apart, and there follows the joyful death in union with the divine (*la morte felice coppulativa*).[^note-66]
zh: 因为人类灵魂的爱是双重的：它不仅指向理智的美，也指向身体中那美的形像。有时对理智之美的爱如此强烈，以致它吸引灵魂抛弃对身体的一切执着；于是人的身体与灵魂分离，随之而来的是与神圣合一的幸福之死（*la morte felice coppulativa*）。[^note-66]

en: 7. Reception History and Influence
zh: 7 接受史与影响

en: One of the most surprising features concerning the reception history of the *Dialoghi* is that a work of Jewish philosophy would subsequently become a European bestseller among non-Jews. In the years immediately following its Italian publication, the *Dialoghi* was translated into virtually every European vernacular. This popularity might be the result of the prominent role that grace (*grazia*) plays in the *Dialoghi* or the fact that Judah frequently stresses the interlocking relationship between the corporeal and the spiritual, something that seems to have resonated with contemporaneous Christian treatments of the incarnation in literary fiction.[^note-67]
zh: 《对话集》接受史中最令人惊讶的特征之一是：一部犹太哲学著作竟然成为非犹太人中的欧洲畅销书。在意大利出版后的最初几年里，《对话集》几乎被翻译成每一种欧洲俗语。这种流行可能是由于优雅（*grazia*）在《对话集》中扮演的突出角色，或犹大频繁强调有形与精神之间相互锁定的关系——这一点似乎与同时代基督教文学虚构中对道成肉身的处理产生共鸣。[^note-67]

en: This popularity of the work has led some to posit that Judah Abrabanel’s thought is epigonic, responsible for disseminating the thought of “great thinkers” such as Marsilio Ficino (1433–1499) and Giovanni Pico della Mirandola (1463–1494) to a wider audience. This essay’s point of departure, however, has been that the thought of Judah Abrabanel, while dependent upon certain features of these earlier thinkers, nevertheless makes significant departures from them in terms of his construction of an overarching system that revolves around the twin principles of love and beauty
zh: 这部著作的流行使一些人认为犹大·阿布拉瓦内尔的思想是模仿性的，只是把马西里奥·费奇诺（1433–1499）和乔瓦尼·皮科·德拉·米兰多拉（1463–1494）等“伟大思想家”的思想传播给更广大的读者。然而，本文的出发点一直是：犹大·阿布拉瓦内尔的思想虽然依赖于这些早期思想家的某些特征，但围绕爱与美这双重原则构造了一个全面的体系，从而对这些早期思想家做出了显著的偏离。

en: Paradoxically, the initial response of Jews to the *Dialoghi* was for the most part negative. Some of the earliest criticisms, especially those of Saul ha-Kohen Ashkenazi, fault Judah with rationalizing kabbalistic principles. Ashkenazi, in a letter to Don Isaac Abrabanel, criticizes Judah for his lack of philosophical esotericism, and for spending too much time on linguistic matters, such as riddles and eloquence. Such antagonism reflects the broader context of the Maimonidean controversies, in which philosophers sought to make philosophy known to a broader Jewish public often by means of dramatic dialogues or philosophical novels. Those opposed to the Aristotelian-Maimonidean paradigm of philosophy often blamed such treatises for weakening the faith of Jews by diminishing their commitment to the *halakhah* (law) and, thus, making them more susceptible to conversion. Despite such initial criticisms, however, subsequent generations stressed the interrelationship between Platonism and kabbalah on the one hand, and philosophy and aesthetics on the other. Notable individuals include Azariah de Rossi (d. ca. 1578) and Judah Moscato (d. ca. 1594).
zh: 吊诡的是，犹太人对《对话集》的最初反应大多是负面的。最早的批评——尤其是 Saul ha-Kohen Ashkenazi 的批评——指责犹大将喀巴拉原则理性化。Ashkenazi 在给唐·伊萨克·阿布拉瓦内尔的信中批评犹大缺乏哲学秘传主义，以及花太多时间在语言问题上如谜语和修辞。这种对抗反映了迈蒙尼德之争的更广语境：哲学家们试图通过戏剧性对话或哲学小说使哲学为更广的犹太公众所知，而反对亚里士多德-迈蒙尼德哲学范式的人则常常指责这类论著削弱了犹太人对 *halakhah*（律法）的承诺从而使他们更易皈依。尽管有这些最初的批评，后续世代强调了柏拉图主义与喀巴拉之间、以及哲学与美学之间的相互关系。著名人物包括 Azariah de Rossi（卒于约 1578 年）与 Judah Moscato（卒于约 1594 年）。

en: The actual influence that the *Dialoghi* would have on subsequent thinkers is more difficult to judge. Essentially, Judah adopted certain trajectories of medieval cosmology and psychology, combined them with Renaissance notions of beauty, and thereby created a full-blown aesthetics of Judaism. This led him to conceive of the universe as a living, dynamic structure, in which all levels share in a symbiotic and organic relationship. Unlike many of his medieval predecessors, he did not define this world, the world of form and matter, in terms of privation or its distance from the divine. On the contrary, he envisages this world as the arena wherein individuals encounter, through sensual particulars, the beauty and love of the divine. Abrabanel’s emphasis, like that of many of his Renaissance contemporaries, on aesthetics and the phenomenal world would eventually become an important dimension of 16th- and 17th -century natural philosophy. We do know, for example, that Baruch Spinoza had a copy of the *Dialoghi* in his library.
zh: 《对话集》对后续思想家的实际影响更难评估。本质上，犹大采纳了中世纪宇宙论和心理学的某些轨迹，把它们与文艺复兴的美学观念结合，从而创造了犹太教的成熟美学。这使他构想宇宙为一个活的、动态的结构，其中所有层级共享一种共生的有机关系。与他的许多中世纪先驱不同，他没有以匮乏或与神圣者的距离来定义这个形式与质料的世界。相反，他将这个世界设想为个体经由感官殊例遭遇神圣之美与爱的场所。阿布拉瓦内尔像他的许多文艺复兴同代人一样，对美学和现象世界的强调，最终成为十六、十七世纪自然哲学的一个重要维度。例如，我们知道巴鲁赫·斯宾诺莎的书库里有一册《对话集》。

en: [^note-11]: Of particular interest is Pietro Bembo (1470–1547) a contemporary of Judah Abrabanel, and someone who also wrote an important dialogue of love. In his *Prose della Volgar Lingua* (Padova: Liviana, 1955), Bembo made the case that Italian writers of his generation should write in Tuscan rather than in other dialects. Although he did not publish this work until 1525, he nevertheless wrote some time between 1497 and 1502 his *Gli Asolani*, itself a dialogue on love, in Italian, and which was subsequently published in 1505. This was one of the earliest examples of a prose work written in Italian. This, in turn, was intimately related to the emerging role of Tuscan nationalism. In this regard, also see Mario Sansone, *Da Bembo a Galiani: Il Dibattio sulla Lingua in Italia* (Bari: Adriatica, 1999), pp. 24–36.

en: Peter Abelard
zh: 彼得·阿伯拉尔 Abelard [Abailard], Peter (Peter King and Andrew Arlig)

en: **First published Tue Aug 3, 2004; substantive revision Fri Jul 31, 2026**
zh: **首次发表于 2004 年 8 月 3 日；2026 年 7 月 31 日实质修订。**

en: Peter Abelard (1079–21 April 1142) [‘Abailard’ or ‘Abaelard’ or ‘Habalaarz’ and so on] was the pre-eminent philosopher and theologian of the twelfth century. The teacher of his generation, he was also famous as a poet and a musician. Prior to the recovery of Aristotle, he brought the native Latin tradition in philosophy to its highest pitch. His genius was evident in all he did. He is, arguably, the greatest logician of the Middle Ages and is equally famous as the first great nominalist philosopher. He championed the use of reason in matters of faith (he was the first to use ‘theology’ in its modern sense), and his systematic treatment of religious doctrines are as remarkable for their philosophical penetration and subtlety as they are for their audacity. Abelard seemed larger than life to his contemporaries: his quick wit, sharp tongue, perfect memory, and boundless arrogance made him unbeatable in debate—he was said by supporter and detractor alike never to have lost an argument—and the force of his personality impressed itself vividly on all with whom he came into contact. His luckless affair with Héloïse made him a tragic figure of romance, and his conflict with Bernard of Clairvaux over reason and religion made him the hero of the Enlightenment. For all his colourful life, though, his philosophical achievements are the cornerstone of his fame.
zh: 彼得·阿伯拉尔（Peter Abelard，1079–1142 年 4 月 21 日）[“Abailard”或“Abaelard”或“Habalaarz”等写法]是十二世纪首屈一指的哲学家与神学家。他是他那一代人的导师，又以诗人与音乐家的身份闻名。在亚里士多德重新为人所知之前，他把拉丁本土哲学传统推向了顶点。他的天才在其所做的一切中显而易见。可以说，他是中世纪最伟大的逻辑学家，又同样以第一位伟大的唯名论哲学家著称。他倡导在信仰事务中运用理性（他是第一个在现代意义上使用“神学”一词的人），而他对宗教学说的系统处理，无论在其哲学穿透力与精微性上，还是在其大胆程度上，都令人瞩目。在同代人眼中，阿伯拉尔的人生比现实更传奇：他的机智、伶俐的口舌、完美的记忆与无边的傲慢使他在论辩中立于不败之地——支持者与反对者都说他从未输过一场论辩——而他的人格力量鲜明地印在所有与他接触过的人身上。他与爱洛依丝（Héloïse）不幸的爱情使他成为浪漫传奇中的悲剧人物，他与克莱尔沃的贝尔纳（Bernard of Clairvaux）就理性与宗教的冲突使他成为启蒙运动的英雄。尽管他一生多彩，他的哲学成就才是其盛名的基石。

en: 1. Life and Works
zh: 1 生平与著作

en: 1.1 Life
zh: 1.1 生平

en: Abelard’s life is relatively well-known. In addition to events chronicled in the public record, his inner life is revealed in his autobiographical letter *Historia calamitatum* [“The Story of My Troubles”] and in his famous correspondence with Héloïse.
zh: 阿伯拉尔的生平相对为人熟知。除了公共记录所载的事件之外，他的内心生活揭示于他的自传体书信《劫余录》（*Historia calamitatum*[“我的灾难的故事”]）以及他与爱洛依丝的著名通信之中。

en: Abelard was born into the lesser nobility around 1079 in Le Pallet, a small town in Brittany near Nantes. He received early training in letters, and took to his studies with enthusiasm; his later writings show familiarity with Cicero, Horace, Juvenal, Ovid, Lucan, Seneca, and Vergil. Abelard eventually renounced his inheritance, including its attendant knighthood, to pursue philosophy. He did so by travelling to study with well-known philosophers, most notably Roscelin and William of Champeaux.
zh: 阿伯拉尔约于 1079 年出生在南特附近布列塔尼小镇勒帕莱（Le Pallet）的下层贵族家庭。他早年受文字训练，满怀热忱地投入学业；其后期著作显示他熟悉西塞罗、贺拉斯、尤维纳利斯、奥维德、卢坎、塞内卡与维吉尔。阿伯拉尔最终放弃了包括随附骑士身份在内的继承权，投身哲学。为此他游学四方，追随著名哲人学习，最著名的是洛色林（Roscelin）与尚波的威廉（William of Champeaux）。

en: During the first years of the twelfth century, Abelard felt confident enough to set himself up as a lecturer, first at Melun and then at Corbeil, competing mainly with William of Champeaux (Paris) for students and reputation. The strain proved too much—Abelard’s health failed, and he returned to Brittany for several years.
zh: 十二世纪的最初几年，阿伯拉尔已有足够的自信开坛讲学，先在默伦，后在科尔贝伊，主要与（巴黎的）尚波的威廉争夺学生与声望。这种紧张超出了他的承受——阿伯拉尔健康崩溃，回布列塔尼休养了数年。

en: Abelard returned to Paris sometime between 1108 and 1113 with his health restored and his ambition intact. He attended William of Champeaux’s lectures, and entered into debate with William over the problem of universals. According to Abelard’s report, he bested his teacher in debate, and gained his reputation as a dialectician of note, teaching at several schools. Around 1113 Abelard decided to study theology; he sought out the most eminent teacher of theology of his day, Anselm of Laon (not to be confused with Anselm of Canterbury), and became his student. It was not a good choice: Anselm’s traditional methods did not appeal to Abelard, and, after some back-and-forth, Abelard returned to Paris to continue on his own. It would be the last time he studied with anyone.
zh: 1108 至 1113 年间的某个时候，阿伯拉尔康复归来、雄心不减地回到巴黎。他听了尚波的威廉的课，并就共相问题与威廉展开论辩。据阿伯拉尔自述，他在论辩中胜过了老师，赢得了知名辩证法家的名声，在好几所学校执教。约 1113 年，阿伯拉尔决定学习神学；他找到了当时最负盛名的神学教师拉昂的安瑟伦（Anselm of Laon，不要与坎特伯雷的安瑟伦混淆），拜入门下。这不是个好选择：安瑟伦的传统方法不合阿伯拉尔的胃口，几番往来之后，阿伯拉尔回到巴黎自行研究。这是他一生最后一次师从他人。

en: Upon returning to Paris, Abelard became scholar-in-residence at Notre Dame, a position he held until his romantic entanglement with Héloïse led to his castration, at which point he entered the Benedictine monastery of Saint Denis and Héloïse entered the convent of Argenteuil. After his recovery, Abelard resumed teaching at a nearby priory, primarily on theology and in particular on the Trinity. His method of philosophical analysis was seen as a direct challenge to more traditional approaches, and a synod, convened in Soissons to examine Abelard’s writings, condemned them and required Abelard to make a public avowal of faith, an experience he found humiliating; shortly afterwards he was allowed to settle in a wild and uninhabited section of land, to devote himself to contemplation.
zh: 回到巴黎后，阿伯拉尔成为圣母院的驻院学者，一直做到他与爱洛依丝的恋情导致他被阉割为止；此后他进入圣但尼本笃会修道院，爱洛依丝进入阿让特伊女修院。康复之后，阿伯拉尔在附近的一座小修道院恢复讲学，主要讲神学，尤其是三位一体。他的哲学分析方法被看作对更传统进路的直接挑战，一次在苏瓦松召开的主教会议审查了阿伯拉尔的著作，对其加以谴责，并要求阿伯拉尔公开表明信仰——这段经历令他倍感羞辱；不久之后，他被准许定居于一片荒无人烟的土地，潜心静观。

en: It was not to be. Abelard says that poverty forced him to resume teaching. He and the students who flocked to him in droves constructed an oratory named the Paraclete, where he continued to write, teach, and research. This idyll came to an end around 1126, when Abelard accepted an invitation to become abbot of the monastery of Saint Gildas de Rhuys in Brittany; shortly afterwards he handed over the Paraclete to Héloïse and the other nuns, whose convent had been expropriated. Abelard found the monks of Saint Gildas difficult and obstructive—even dangerous—and he claims that there were several attempts on his life while in residence. During this period he wrote the *Historia calamitatum* and corresponded with Héloïse.
zh: 然而事与愿违。阿伯拉尔说，贫穷迫使他恢复讲学。成群结队涌向他的学生们与他一起建起了一座名为“天主圣神”（Paraclete）的小堂，他在那里继续写作、教学与研究。这一田园牧歌约于 1126 年结束：阿伯拉尔接受了邀请，出任布列塔尼圣吉尔达-德-吕伊斯修道院院长；不久之后，他把天主圣神小堂交给爱洛依丝与其他因女修院被征收而无处安身的修女。阿伯拉尔发现圣吉尔达的修士难缠而掣肘——甚至危险——他声称在任内遭遇过好几次谋害。在此期间他写下了《劫余录》，并与爱洛依丝通信。

en: By the mid-1130s Abelard was given permission to return to Paris (retaining his rank as abbot) and to teach in the schools on the Mont Ste.-Genevieve. It was during this time that his theological treatises were brought to the attention of Bernard of Clairvaux, who objected to some of Abelard’s conclusions as well as to his approach to matters of faith. After some inconclusive attempts to resolve their differences, Abelard asked the archbishop of Sens to arrange a public dispute between himself and Bernard on 3 June 1140, to settle their disagreements. Bernard initially refused the invitation on the grounds that one should not debate matters of faith, but then accepted it and, unknown to Abelard, arranged to convene another commission of enquiry to review Abelard’s works on suspicion of heresy. When Abelard discovered that there was no debate but instead a kangaroo court, he refused to take part, announcing his intention to appeal to the Pope directly. He walked out of the proceedings and began travelling to Rome. The Council condemned nineteen propositions it claimed to find in his works and adjourned. Bernard launched a successful campaign petitioning the Papal Court before Abelard was out of France; a letter from the Pope upholding the decision of the Council of Soissons reached Abelard while he was at Cluny; Abelard was ordered to silence. By all accounts Abelard complied immediately, even meeting peacefully with Bernard in reconciliation. Peter the Venerable, the abbot of Cluny, wrote to the Pope about these matters, and the Pope lifted Abelard’s sentence. Abelard remained under the protection of Peter the Venerable first at Cluny, then at St. Marcel, as his health gradually deteriorated. Abelard died on 21 April 1142. His body was interred at the Paraclete, and today is (with Héloïse) in Père Lachaise cemetery in Paris.
zh: 到 1130 年代中期，阿伯拉尔获准返回巴黎（保留院长衔），在圣热纳维耶芙山上各学校讲学。正是在这一时期，他的神学论著进入了克莱尔沃的贝尔纳的视野，贝尔纳反对阿伯拉尔的某些结论以及他处理信仰事务的方式。在几番无果的调和尝试之后，阿伯拉尔请求桑斯大主教在 1140 年 6 月 3 日安排他与贝尔纳公开论辩，以解决分歧。贝尔纳起初以信仰事务不可论辩为由拒绝邀请，随后又接受了，并在阿伯拉尔不知情的情况下安排召集另一个审查委员会，以异端嫌疑复审阿伯拉尔的著作。当阿伯拉尔发现根本没有论辩、有的只是一个私设公堂时，他拒绝出席，宣布将直接向教皇上诉。他退出程序，动身前往罗马。会议谴责了据称见于其著作的十九条命题后休会。在阿伯拉尔还未走出法国时，贝尔纳就发起了一场成功的请愿运动，向教廷陈情；教皇维持苏瓦松会议决定的书信送达时，阿伯拉尔正在克吕尼；他被令禁言。众口一词的说法是：阿伯拉尔立即服从了，甚至与贝尔纳平静会面、达成和解。克吕尼院长可敬者彼得（Peter the Venerable）就这些事务致信教皇，教皇解除了对阿伯拉尔的判决。阿伯拉尔先在克吕尼、后在圣马塞尔，一直处于可敬者彼得的庇护之下，健康每况愈下。阿伯拉尔卒于 1142 年 4 月 21 日。他的遗体安葬于天主圣神小堂，今天（与爱洛依丝一起）在巴黎拉雪兹神父公墓。

en: Abelard’s students were active as kings, philosophers, poets, politicians, theologians, and monks; they include three popes and several heads of state. Explicit references to Abelard’s thinking in the later Middle Ages are few, likely because of the cloud cast by the verdict of the Council of Soissons, but it is clear that he had a seminal influence on twelfth-century philosophy and perhaps on later fourteenth-century speculation as well.
zh: 阿伯拉尔的学生们身为国王、哲人、诗人、政治家、神学家与修士，都很活跃；其中包括三位教皇与数位国家元首。中世纪后期对阿伯拉尔思想的显式引用很少，这大概是苏瓦松会议判决投下的阴影所致，但可以清楚看到，他对十二世纪哲学有发轫之功，或许对十四世纪晚期的思辨也有影响。

en: 1.2 Works
zh: 1.2 著作

en: The dates of composition and even the number of Abelard’s writings remain largely obscure and a matter of controversy among scholars. One reason for this is that Abelard constantly revised and rewrote, so that several distinct versions of a given work might be in circulation; another reason is that several of his writings might represent ‘teaching notes’ constantly evolving in courses and seminars. Hence it is not clear that ‘date of composition’ is a well-defined notion when applied to the body of Abelard’s work that we now possess. Apart from Abelard’s correspondence, which can be dated with relative precision, Abelard’s extant work falls into three categories.
zh: 阿伯拉尔著作的成书年代乃至篇目数量，在学者中间仍大半晦暗不明、聚讼纷纭。原因之一是阿伯拉尔不断修改与重写，同一部著作的几个不同版本可能同时在流传；另一原因是他的若干著作也许只是“教学讲义”，在课程与研讨中不断演变。因此，“成书年代”这个概念用于我们现在掌握的阿伯拉尔著作，是否 well-defined，并不清楚。除了可以相对精确断年的书信之外，阿伯拉尔传世的著作分为三类。

en: The first category consists of Abelard’s works on *dialectic*—works concerned with logic, philosophy of language, metaphysics, and philosophy of mind. His two masterworks are:
zh: 第一类是阿伯拉尔的 **辩证法** （dialectic）著作——涉及逻辑、语言哲学、形而上学与心灵哲学的著作。他的两部代表作是：

en: - *Logica* ‘*ingredientibus*’, “Logic” (starting with the words ‘To those beginning…’). - *Dialectica*, “Dialectic.”
zh: - *Logica* ‘*ingredientibus*’，即“逻辑”（以“致初学者……”起首）。 - 《辩证法》（*Dialectica*）。

en: Both of these works follow the pattern of the *logica vetus*, the “old logic” inherited from antiquity: Porphyry’s introduction to Aristotle, the *Isagoge*; Aristotle’s *Categories* and *On Interpretation*; Boethius’s *Introduction to the Categorical Syllogism*, *Categorical Syllogisms*, *Hypothetical Syllogisms*, *On Topical Difference*, and *On Division*. Abelard’s works cover the material presented in the old logic, though they do so in different ways. His *Logica* ‘*ingredientibus*’ is a close textual commentary on the old logic, though only some of it survives, namely the commentaries on the *Isagoge*, the *Categories*, *On Interpretation*, and *On Topical Differences*; his *Dialectica* is an independent treatise on dialectic that treats the same material thematically, though neither the beginning (covering the *Isagoge* and the start of the *Categories*) nor the ending (on division and definition) have been preserved. In addition, there are four lesser works on dialectic:
zh: 这两部著作都遵循承自古代的 **旧逻辑** （logica vetus，即“旧逻辑”）的格局：波爱修斯的亚里士多德导论《Isagoge》（《导论》）；亚里士多德的《范畴篇》与《解释篇》；波爱修斯的《论范畴三段论》、《范畴三段论》、《假言三段论》、《论论题区分》与《论划分》。阿伯拉尔的著作覆盖旧逻辑所传授的材料，但方式各异。他的 *Logica* ‘*ingredientibus*’是旧逻辑的逐字逐句注疏，不过只有一部分传世，即对《Isagoge》、《范畴篇》、《解释篇》与《论论题区分》的注疏；他的《辩证法》是一部独立论辩专著，按主题处理同样的材料，不过其开头（覆盖《Isagoge》与《范畴篇》开头部分）与结尾（论划分与定义）都没有保存下来。此外还有四部次要的辩证法著作：
