en: - *Introductiones parvulorum*, “Introductory Logic.” - *Logica* ‘*nostrorum petitioni sociorum*’, “Logic” (starting with the words ‘At the request of our friends…’). - *Tractatus de intellectibus*, “A Treatise on Understandings.” - *Sententiae secundum Magistrum Petrum*, “Master Peter’s Views.”
zh: - *Introductiones parvulorum*，即“初阶逻辑”。 - *Logica* ‘*nostrorum petitioni sociorum*’，即“逻辑”（以“应我们朋友们之请……”起首）。 - *Tractatus de intellectibus*，即“论理解”。 - *Sententiae secundum Magistrum Petrum*，即“彼得师父的学说”。

en: The first of these is a series of elementary commentaries on the old logic (though again not completely preserved); their simple level has led some scholars to think they must come from early in Abelard’s career, others to deny that they are Abelard’s work at all. Second, the *Logica* ‘*nostrorum petitioni sociorum*’ is something of a work-in-progress: it assumes knowledge of Abelard’s earlier *Logica* ‘*ingredientibus*’ and discusses advanced points not dealt with there, but for long stretches it is also a straightforward paraphrase of or commentary on Porphyry’s *Isagoge*; it has textual parallels with some of Abelard’s other works and shows some knowledge of theology. The third work deals with concepts, or ‘understandings’, from both the point of view of logic (roughly as providing the meanings of terms) and from the point of view of the philosophy of mind (as vehicles for mental content). The last work may be no more than a report of some of Abelard’s lectures, and is concerned with logical and metaphysical puzzles about wholes and parts.
zh: 第一部是对旧逻辑的系列初级注疏（同样没有完整传世）；其浅易的程度使一些学者认为它们必出自阿伯拉尔早期，另一些学者则否认它们是阿伯拉尔的作品。其次，*Logica* ‘*nostrorum petitioni sociorum*’多少算一部进行中的作品：它预设读者已知阿伯拉尔早先的 *Logica* ‘*ingredientibus*’，讨论后者未涉及的进阶要点，但在很长的篇幅里它也只是对波爱修斯《Isagoge》的直白转述或注疏；它与阿伯拉尔的其他著作有文本平行之处，并显示出一些神学知识。第三部著作从逻辑的视角（大致是提供词项的意义）与心灵哲学的视角（作为心灵内容的载体）处理概念或“理解”。最后一部著作也许不过是对阿伯拉尔若干讲演的记录，处理的是关于整体与部分的逻辑与形而上学难题。

en: The second category consists of Abelard’s works on ethics:
zh: 第二类是阿伯拉尔的伦理学著作：

en: - *Ethica seu Scito teipsum*, “Ethics, or, Know Yourself.” - *Collationes*, “Conversations” a.k.a. *Dialogus inter Philosophum, Iudaeum, et Christianum*, “The Dialogue of a Philosopher with a Jew and a Christian”.
zh: - 《伦理学：认识你自己》（*Ethica seu Scito teipsum*）。 - 《对话集》（*Collationes*），又名《哲人、犹太人与基督徒之间对话》（*Dialogus inter Philosophum, Iudaeum, et Christianum*）。

en: The *Ethics* offers an analysis of moral worth and the degree of praise or blame that should attach to agents and their actions; it breaks off at the beginning of the second book. The *Conversations* is a pair of debates (among characters who appear to Abelard in a dream) over the nature of happiness and the supreme good: the Philosopher, who claims to follow only natural reason, first debates with the Jew, who follows the Old Law; the Philosopher then debates the Christian, who defends Christian ethics from a philosophical point of view. Abelard also wrote a slight work of practical advice for his son:
zh: 《伦理学》分析了道德价值以及应归于行动者及其行动的褒贬程度；它在第二卷开篇处中断。《对话集》是两场辩论（在阿伯拉尔梦中显现的人物之间），讨论幸福与至善的本性：自称只遵循自然理性的哲人先与遵循旧律的犹太人辩论；然后哲人与从哲学立场为基督教伦理辩护的基督徒辩论。阿伯拉尔还写过一部给儿子的浅白的实用建议之作：

en: - *Carmen ad Astralabium*, “Poem for Astralabe.”
zh: - 《致阿斯特拉拉布诗》（*Carmen ad Astralabium*）。

en: Moral advice and edifying sentiments are found in this series of distichs.
zh: 一系列对句中载有道德劝告与砥砺情操的箴言。

en: The third category consists of Abelard’s works of philosophical theology. His three main works are devoted to a philosophical analysis of the Trinity, the several versions representing successive stages of his thought and his attempts at orthodoxy (each rewritten several times):
zh: 第三类是阿伯拉尔的哲学神学著作。他的三部主要著作致力于对三位一体的哲学分析，几个版本代表他思想的先后阶段与他趋近正统的努力（每一部都重写过多次）：

en: - *Theologia* ‘*summi boni*’. “Theology” (that begins with the words ‘The highest good…’). - *Theologia christiana*, “Christian Theology.” - *Theologia* ‘*scholarium*’, “Theology” (that begins with the words ‘In the schools…’).
zh: - *Theologia* ‘*summi boni*’，即“神学”（以“至善……”起首）。 - 《基督徒神学》（*Theologia christiana*）。 - *Theologia* ‘*scholarium*’，即“神学”（以“在学校里……”起首）。

en: The first version of the *Theology* seems to have been the work condemned at the Council of Soisssons, the last the work condemned at the Council of Sens. In addition to these three works, in which problems in philosophical theology are treated thematically, Abelard also wrote several commentaries:
zh: 《神学》的第一版似乎就是在苏瓦松会议上被谴责的著作，最后一版则是在桑斯会议上被谴责的著作。除了这三部按主题处理哲学神学问题的著作之外，阿伯拉尔还写了几部注疏：

en: - *Expositio orationis dominicae*, “Analysis of the Lord’s Prayer.” - *Expositio symboli Apostolorum*, “Analysis of the Apostle’s Creed.” - *Expositio fidei in symbolum Athanasii*, “Analysis of Faith in the Athanasian Creed.” - *Hexaëmeron*, “Commentary on *Genesis* 1–2:25.” - *Commentaria in Epistolam Pauli ad Romanos*, “Commentary on St. Paul’s Letter to the Romans.”
zh: - *Expositio orationis dominicae*，即“《主祷文》解析”。 - *Expositio symboli Apostolorum*，即“《使徒信经》解析”。 - *Expositio fidei in symbolum Athanasii*，即“阿塔纳修信经中的信仰解析”。 - 《创世六日》（*Hexaëmeron*），即“《创世记》1–2:25 注疏”。 - 《致罗马人书注》（*Commentaria in Epistolam Pauli ad Romanos*），即“圣保罗《致罗马人书》注疏”。

en: The first three commentaries are brief, but Abelard’s discussions of the first verses of *Genesis* and of Paul’s letter are extensive and detailed (the latter also relevant to Abelard’s ethical theory). Abelard also took up questions about faith and reason in a short work:
zh: 前三部注疏简短，但阿伯拉尔对《创世记》头几节与保罗书信的讨论广泛而详密（后者也与阿伯拉尔的伦理理论相关）。阿伯拉尔还在一部短篇著作中处理了信仰与理性的问题：

en: - *Soliloquium*, “Soliloquy.”
zh: - 《独语录》（*Soliloquium*）。

en: This brief inner dialogue, modelled on Augustine’s *Soliloquies*, has “Peter” talking things over with “Abelard.” Theological questions of a more practical nature were raised by Héloïse in a series of questions she asked on her behalf and on behalf of the nuns of the Paraclete:
zh: 这篇短小的内心对话仿效奥古斯丁的《独语录》，让“彼得”与“阿伯拉尔”对谈。更具实践性质的神学问题，由爱洛依丝代表她自己以及天主圣神小堂的修女们提出的一系列问题带出：

en: - *Problemata Heloïssae cum Petri Abaelardi solutionibus*, “Héloïse’s Problem-List (with Abelard’s Solutions).”
zh: - 《爱洛依丝问题集（附阿伯拉尔解答）》（*Problemata Heloïssae cum Petri Abaelardi solutionibus*）。

en: Practical issues are also addressed in Abelard’s sermons, hymns, and lamentations (*planctus*). Finally, Abelard composed an extremely influential theological work that contains no theoretical speculation at all:
zh: 阿伯拉尔的布道文、赞美诗与哀歌（*planctus*）也处理实际问题。最后，阿伯拉尔还写成了一部影响极大、却全无思辨的神学著作：

en: - *Sic et non*, “For and Against.”
zh: - 《是与否》（*Sic et non*）。

en: Abelard assembles a series of 158 questions, each of which is furnished with patristic citations that imply a positive answer (*sic*) to the question and other patristic citations implying a negative answer (*non*). Abelard does not attempt to harmonize these apparently inconsistent remarks, but in his preface he lays down rules for proper hermeneutic investigation: look for ambiguity, check the surrounding context, draw relevant distinctions, and the like.
zh: 阿伯拉尔汇集了 158 个问题，每一个都配有暗示肯定回答（*sic*）的教父引文与其他暗示否定回答（*non*）的教父引文。阿伯拉尔并不试图调和这些表面不一致的说法，而是在序言中定下正当释经探究的规则：查歧义、看上下文、作相关区分，等等。

en: Abelard’s students and disciples also record many of his views, though this material has yet to be explored carefully. There are references in Abelard’s extant works to other works we do not have: *Grammatica*, “Grammar”; *Rhetorica*, “Rhetoric”; a commentary on *Ezekiel* written at the beginning of his studies in theology; and others. It is possible some of these works may yet be found.
zh: 阿伯拉尔的学生与追随者也记录了他的许多观点，但这批材料尚未得到仔细清理。阿伯拉尔传世著作中提到我们已佚的其他著作：《语法》（*Grammatica*）；《修辞学》（*Rhetorica*）；一部他初学神学时写的《以西结书》注疏；等等。其中有些著作或许还能被发现。

en: 2. Metaphysics
zh: 2 形而上学

en: Abelard’s metaphysics is the first great example of nominalism in the Western tradition. While his view that universals are mere words (*nomina*) justifies the label, nominalism—or, better, irrealism—is the hallmark of Abelard’s entire metaphysics. He is an irrealist not only about universals, but also about propositions, events, times other than the present, natural kinds, relations, wholes, absolute space, hylomorphic composites, and the like. Instead, Abelard holds that the concrete individual, in all its richness and variety, is more than enough to populate the world. Abelard preferred reductive, atomist, and material explanations whenever possible; he devoted a great deal of effort to pouring cold water on the metaphysical excesses of his predecessors and contemporaries.
zh: 阿伯拉尔的形而上学是西方传统中唯名论的第一个伟大范例。虽然“共相只是词（*nomina*）”这一观点配得上唯名论的标签，但唯名论——或者更准确地说，非实在论——是阿伯拉尔整个形而上学的标志。他不仅对共相持非实在论立场，对命题、事件、当下以外的时间、自然类、关系、整体、绝对空间、形质复合体等等都是如此。相反，阿伯拉尔认为，具体个体以其全部的丰富性与多样性，已经足以充满世界。只要可能，阿伯拉尔偏好还原的、原子论的与唯物的解释；他把大量心力用于给他前辈与同代人的形而上学夸大之词泼冷水。

en: Abelard defends his thesis that universals are nothing but words by arguing that ontological realism about universals is incoherent. More exactly, he holds that there cannot be any real object in the world satisfying Boethius’s criteria for the universal, namely something present as a whole in many at once so as to constitute their substance (i.e. to make the individual in which it is present what it is). Hence, Abelard concludes, universality is not an ontological feature of the world but a semantic feature of language.
zh: 阿伯拉尔为“共相不过是无所谓的话”这一论题辩护的方式，是论证共相的实在论是不融贯的。更精确地说，他主张世界中不可能有任何实在对象满足波爱修斯的共相判准，即“同时整体地内在于多个事物，从而构成其实体”（也就是使内在于其中的个体成为其所是）的东西。因此阿伯拉尔得出结论：普遍性不是世界的存在论特征，而是语言的语义特征。

en: Suppose universals were things in the world, so that one and the same item is completely present in both Socrates and an ass at the same time, making each to be wholly an animal. Abelard points out that then the same thing, *animal*, will be simultaneously rational (due to its role in constituting the species *human being*) and irrational (due to its role in constituting the species *ass*). But then contraries are simultaneously present in the same thing as a whole, which is impossible.
zh: 假设共相是世界中的事物，同一个东西同时完全内在于苏格拉底和一头驴，使二者都完全是动物。阿伯拉尔指出，那么同一个东西“动物”将同时是理性的（因其在构成“人”这个种中的角色）又是无理性的（因其在构成“驴”这个种中的角色）。但这样一来，相反者就同时整体地内在于同一个东西之中——这是不可能的。

en: To the rejoinder that rationality and irrationality are not actually present in the same thing, Abelard offers a twofold reply. First, he rejects the claim that they are present only potentially. Each species is actually informed by a contrary, and the genus is actually present in each as a whole; hence it is actually informed by one contrary in one species and by the other in the other; since it is wholly one and the same in each, it is therefore actually informed by contraries, and the contradiction results. Second, Abelard undertakes to establish that contraries will be present not merely in the genus but even in the selfsame individual. For Socrates is (an) animal, and so is Brunellus the Ass; but by transitivity—since each is wholly and completely *animal*—Socrates is Brunellus, and hence both rational and irrational. Put a different way, each is essentially an animal, and furthermore essentially rational and essentially irrational.
zh: 对于“理性与无理性实际上并不内在于同一东西”这一反驳，阿伯拉尔给出双重回应。第一，他拒绝“它们只是潜在地内在于其中”的主张。每个种都实际地被一个相反者所塑造，而属又实际地整体内在于每一个种；因此它实际地被一个相反者在一个种中塑造，又被另一个相反者在另一个种中塑造；既然它在每一个种中都是完全同一个东西，它就实际地被相反者所塑造，矛盾随之而来。第二，阿伯拉尔进而要确立：相反者不仅内在于属，甚至内在于同一个个体之中。因为苏格拉底是（一个）动物，布鲁努斯驴也是；但由传递性——由于各自都完全彻底地是“动物”——苏格拉底就是布鲁努斯，因而既是理性的又是无理性的。换个说法：每一个都本质上是动物，而且本质上是理性的，又本质上是无理性的。

en: If we object to this last piece of reasoning, on the grounds that individuals are unique in virtue of their non-essential features, Abelard replies that this view “makes accidents prior to substance.” That is, the objection claims that individual things are individual in virtue of features that contingently characterize them, which confuses things with their features.
zh: 如果我们基于个体因非本质特征而各不相同来反对这最后一步推理，阿伯拉尔答曰：这种看法“使偶性先于实体”。也就是说，该反驳主张个体事物凭借偶然刻画它们的特征而是个体，这混淆了事物与事物的特征。

en: Prospects are no better for realism if the universal is identified not with a single thing but with a collection of things. Abelard points out that collections are posterior to their parts, and, furthermore, the collection is not shared among its parts in the way a universal is said to be common to many. Nor does it help to try to identify the universal with the individual in some fashion, for example in claiming that Socrates *qua* human is taken as the universal *human being*; Abelard argues that if the universal really is the individual, then we are stuck with the consequence that either individuals such as Socrates are common to many, or there are as many universals as there are individuals, each of which is absurd.
zh: 如果共相不是被认作单一事物，而是被认作一批事物的集合，实在论的前景也好不了多少。阿伯拉尔指出，集合后于其部分，而且集合并不像据说的共相对于多个事物是共同的（common）那样，为各部分所共享。试图以某种方式把共相等同于个体也无济于事，例如主张“作为人的苏格拉底”被当作“人”这个共相；阿伯拉尔论证，如果共相真的是个体，那么我们就被套进这样的后果：要么苏格拉底这样的个体为多个事物所共有，要么有多少个体就有多少共相——两者都是荒谬的。

en: Abelard concludes that universality is merely linguistic, not a feature of the world. More precisely, Abelard holds that common nouns (such as ‘animal’), verbs, and negative names (such as ‘not-Socrates’) are correctly predicable of many, and so count as universals. These terms are semantically general, in that their sense applies to more than one thing, but they do not thereby name some general thing; instead, they distributively refer to each of the individuals to which the term applies. For example, the term ‘animal’ has the sense *living substance*, which is inherently general, and it refers to each individual animal since each is a living substance—as Abelard puts it, since each has the status of being a living substance. But this is to leave the domain of metaphysics for semantics; see the discussion of Abelard‘s philosophy of language in Section 4.
zh: 阿伯拉尔得出结论：普遍性只是语言性的，不是世界的特征。更精确地说，阿伯拉尔认为通名（如“动物”）、动词与否定名（如“非苏格拉底”）可以正确地述谓多个主词，因此算作共相。这些词项在语义上是一般的：它们的意涵适用于多于一个的东西，但并不因此命名某个一般的东西；相反，它们分布地（distributively）指称该词项适用于每一个个体。例如，“动物”这个词的意涵是“活的实体”，这意涵天然是一般的，它指称每一个动物个体，因为每一个都是活的实体——用阿伯拉尔的话说，因为每一个都具有“作为活的实体”的身份。但这已是离开形而上学、进入语义学的领域了；关于阿伯拉尔语言哲学的讨论见第 4 节。

en: Abelard maintains that everything in the world apart from God and angels is either form, matter, or a composite of form and matter. The matter of something is that out of which it is made, whether it persists in the finished product (as bricks in a house) or is absorbed into it (as flour in bread). Ultimately, all material objects are composed of the four elements earth, air, fire, and water, but they do not retain their elemental forms in most combinations. In general, the form of a material object just is the configuration of its material parts: “We call the form strictly what comes from the composition of the parts.” The form of a statue, for example, is its shape, which is no more than the arrangement of its matter—the curve of the nose, the size of the eyes, and so on. Forms are therefore *supervenient* on matter, and have no ontological standing independent of it. This is not to deny that forms exist, but to provide a particular explanation of what it is for a form to inhere in a given subject, namely for that subject to have its matter configured in a certain way. For example, the inherence of shape in the statue just is the way in which its bronze is arranged. Hence material things are identical with what they are made of—with one exception: human beings, whose forms are their immaterial (and immortal) souls. Strictly speaking, since human souls are capable of existence in separation form the body, they are not forms after all, though they act as substantial forms as long as they are joined to the body.
zh: 阿伯拉尔主张，世界中除上帝与天使之外的每一物，要么是形式，要么是质料，要么是形式与质料的复合体。某物的质料是构成它的材料，无论它保留在成品中（如房子里的砖）还是被吸收进其中（如面包里的面粉）。最终，一切物质对象都由土、气、火、水四元素构成，但在大多数组合中它们并不保留其元素形式。一般而言，物质对象的形式就是其诸物质部分的配置：“我们严格地把形式称为出自诸部分之组合的东西。”例如，雕像的形式是它的形状，那不过是其质料的排布——鼻子的曲线、眼睛的大小，等等。因此形式 **随附** 于质料，没有独立于质料的存在论地位。这并不是否认形式存在，而是对“形式内在于一个给定主体”意味着什么给出一种特定解释：即该主体的质料按某种方式得到配置。例如，形状内在于雕像，就是它的青铜被安排的方式。因此，物质事物与构成它们的材料同一——只有一个例外：人，人的形式是其非物质（且不朽）的灵魂。严格说来，由于人的灵魂能够与身体分离存在，它们根本不是形式，尽管在与身体结合期间，它们充当实体形式。

en: Material composites of form and matter, humans excepted, are integral wholes made up of their discrete material parts as configured in a given way. Abelard countenances many types of integral wholes: collections, no matter how their members are selected; structured composites, whether naturally unified (such as Socrates and his limbs) or artificially unified (such as the walls, floor, and roof of a house); continuous quantities that are homogeneous material ‘substances,’ namely stuffs, such as water or gold; geometrical objects, such as lines, defined by the relative position of their parts; temporal wholes, such as a day and the hours that make it up. Most of these wholes are ontologically nothing beyond their material parts. Whether structured composites have any independent ontological standing depends on the status of their organizing forms.
zh: 除了人之外，形式与质料的物质复合体是由其分立的物质部分按给定方式配置而成的整全（integral）整体。阿伯拉尔承认多种类型的整全整体：集合，无论其成员如何选出；有结构的复合体，无论自然统一（如苏格拉底和他的四肢）还是人工统一（如房子的墙、地板与屋顶）；连续量，即同质的物质“实体”，也就是水或金之类的东西；几何对象，如由各部分相对位置定义的线；时间整体，如一天和构成它的诸小时。这些整体中的多数在存在论上不过是其物质部分。有结构的复合体是否具有独立的存在论地位，取决于其组织形式的地位。

en: Abelard’s theory of substantial integral wholes is not a pure mereology in the modern sense, since he holds that there are privileged divisions: just as a genus is properly divided into not just any species but its proximate species, so too the division of a whole must be into its principal parts. Intuitively, some wholes have a natural division that takes precedence over others; a sentence, for example, is divided into words, syllables, and letters, in precisely that order. According to Abelard, the principal parts of a whole are those whose conjunction immediately results in the complete whole. His intent seems to be that the nature of the composition (if any) that defines the integral whole also spells out its principal parts. A house consists of floor, walls, and roof put together in the right way. It is an open question whether each principal part (such as the wall) requires the existence of all of its subparts (every brick). The principal parts of a collection, for example, are just each of the members of the collection, whatever may be the case with any given member’s subparts; the principal parts of an aggregation are the members located in proximity to one another.
zh: 阿伯拉尔的实体整全整体理论不是现代意义上的纯粹分体论（mereology），因为他主张存在特权划分：正如属不是被划分为任意的种而是被划分为其邻近种，整体的划分也必须划分成其主要部分。直观地说，有些整体有一种优先于其他划分的自然划分；例如，一个句子依次被划分为词、音节与字母。按阿伯拉尔的说法，整体的主要部分是“它们的结合直接产生完整整体”的那些部分。他的意思似乎是：界定整全整体的组合方式（如果有）也同时给出了其主要部分。一座房子由地板、墙与屋顶按正确方式拼在一起。每一个主要部分（如墙）是否需要其所有子部分（每一块砖）的存在，是个悬而未决的问题。例如，集合的主要部分就是集合的每一个成员，无论任何给定成员的子部分如何；聚集（aggregation）的主要部分则是彼此邻近的成员。

en: Individuals have natures, and in virtue of their natures they belong to determinate natural kinds. But an individual’s nature is not something really shared with or common to other individuals; Abelard’s refutation of realism has shown that this is impossible. Instead, Abelard takes a natural kind to be a well-defined collection of things that have the same features, broadly speaking, that make them what they are. Why a given thing has some features rather than others is explained by how it got that way—the natural processes that created it result in its having the features it does, namely being the kind of thing it is; similar processes lead to similar results. On this reading, it is clear that natural kinds have no special status; they are no more than discrete integral wholes whose principle of membership is similarity, merely reflecting the fact that the world is divided into discrete similarity-classes of objects. Furthermore, such real relations of similarity are nothing themselves above and beyond the things that are similar. The division into natural kinds is, presumably, a ‘shallow fact’ about the world: matters could have been otherwise had God ordained them differently; fire might be cold, heavy bodies fall upwards, frogs reason. If these causal powers were different, then natural kinds might be different as well, or might not have been as sharply differentiated as they are now. Given how matters stand, natural kinds carve the world at its joints, but they are the joints chosen by God.
zh: 个体有其本性，凭其本性它们属于确定不变的自然类。但个体的本性并不是与其他个体实在地共享或共同的东西；阿伯拉尔对实在论的驳斥已经表明这是不可能的。相反，阿伯拉尔把自然类看成由具有（宽泛地说）相同特征的东西组成的一个边界分明的集合，这些特征使它们成为其所是。为什么一个给定的东西具有这样一些特征而非另一些，由它的来历解释——创造它的自然过程导致它具有这些特征，也就是成为它所属的那种东西；相似的过程导致相似的结果。按这一读法，自然类显然没有任何特殊地位；它们不过是成员资格原则为“相似性”的分立整全整体，只是反映世界被划分为分立的相似性类这一事实。而且，这类实在的相似关系本身也不高于、不外于那些相似的事物。自然类的划分大概只是关于世界的“浅层事实”：如果上帝另行安排，事情本可以是别样的；火可以是冷的，重的物体可以向上落，青蛙可以推理。如果这些因果能力不同，自然类也可能不同，或者不会像现在这样界限分明。就事情的实际情形而言，自然类在世界的关节处切割世界，但这些关节是上帝选定的关节。

en: 3. Logic
zh: 3 逻辑

en: Abelard was the greatest logician since Antiquity: he devised a purely truth-functional propositional logic, recognizing the distinction between *force* and *content* we associate with Frege, and worked out a complete theory of entailment as it functions in argument (which we now take as the theory of logical consequence). His logical system is flawed in its handling of topical inference, but that should not prevent our recognition of Abelard’s achievements.
zh: 阿伯拉尔是自古以来的最伟大逻辑学家：他设计了一种纯真值的命题逻辑，认识到我们与弗雷格联系在一起的“语气”（force）与“内容”（content）的区分，并构造了完整的蕴涵理论以处理它在论证中的运作（我们如今视之为逻辑后承理论）。他的逻辑系统在论题推理的处理上有缺陷，但这不应妨碍我们承认阿伯拉尔的成就。

en: Abelard observes that the same propositional content can be expressed with different force in different contexts: the content *that Socrates is in the house* is expressed in an assertion in ‘Socrates is in the house’; in a question in ‘Is Socrates in the house?’; in a wish in ‘If only Socrates were in the house!’ and so on. Hence Abelard can distinguish in particular the assertive force of a sentence from its propositional content, a distinction that allows him to point out that the component sentences in a conditional statement are not asserted, though they have the same content they do when asserted—‘If Socrates is in the kitchen, then Socrates is in the house’ does not assert that Socrates is in the kitchen or that he is in the house, nor do the antecedent or the consequent, although the same form of words could be used outside the scope of the conditional to make such assertions. Likewise, the distinction allows Abelard to define negation, and other propositional connectives, purely truth-functionally in terms of content, so that negation, for instance, is treated as follows: not-*p* is false/true if and only if *p* is true/false.
zh: 阿伯拉尔观察到，同一个命题内容可以在不同语境中以不同语气表达：内容“苏格拉底在房子里”在“苏格拉底在房子里”中以断言表达；在“苏格拉底在房子里吗？”中以提问表达；在“但愿苏格拉底在房子里！”中以愿望表达，如此等等。因此阿伯拉尔能够特别地把一个句子的断言语气与其命题内容区分开——这一区分使他得以指出条件句中的成分句并未被断言，尽管它们具有与被断言时相同的内容——“如果苏格拉底在厨房，那么苏格拉底在房子里”并没有断言苏格拉底在厨房或在房子里，前件与后件也没有；虽然同样的措辞在条件句辖域之外可以用来作出这样的断言。同样，这一区分使阿伯拉尔能够纯粹以真值函项的方式、按内容来定义否定与其他命题联结词，例如否定被处理为：not-*p* 为假/真，当且仅当 *p* 为真/假。

en: The key to the theory of argument, for Abelard, is found in *inferentia*, best rendered as ‘entailment’, since Abelard requires the connection between the propositions involved to be both necessary and relevant. That is, the conclusion—more exactly, the sense of the final statement—is required by the sense of the preceding statement(s), so that it cannot be otherwise. Abelard often speaks of the sense of the final statement being “contained” in the sense of the preceding statement(s), much as we speak of the conclusion being contained in the premisses. An entailment is complete (*perfecta*) when it holds in virtue of the logical form (*complexio*) of the propositions involved. By this, Abelard tells us, he means that the entailment holds under any uniform substitution in its terms, the criterion now associated with Bolzano. The traditional four figures and moods of the categorical syllogism derived from Aristotle, and the doctrine of the hypothetical syllogism derived from Boethius, are all instances of complete entailments, or as we should say, valid inference.
zh: 在阿伯拉尔看来，论证理论的关键在于 *inferentia*，最好译作“蕴涵”，因为阿伯拉尔要求所涉命题之间的联系既是必然的又是相关的。也就是说，结论——更确切地说，最后陈述的意涵——被前面陈述的意涵所要求，以至于不能是别样。阿伯拉尔常说最后陈述的意涵“包含”在前述陈述的意涵之中，就像我们说结论包含在前提中一样。蕴涵是完全的（*perfecta*），当它凭所涉命题的逻辑形式（*complexio*）成立。阿伯拉尔告诉我们，这意味着该蕴涵在其词项的任何一致替换下都成立——这一判准如今与博尔扎诺联系在一起。源自亚里士多德的直言三段论的传统四格与诸式，以及源自波爱修斯的假言三段论学说，都是完全蕴涵的实例，或者用我们的话说，有效推理。

en: There is another way in which conclusions can be necessary and relevant to their premisses, yet *not* be formally valid (not be a complete entailment). The necessary connection among the propositions, and the link among their senses, might be a function of non-formal metaphysical truths holding in all possible worlds. For instance, human beings are a kind of animal, so the consequence ‘If Socrates is a human being, Socrates is an animal’ holds of necessity and the sense of the antecedent compels that of the consequent, but it is not formally valid under uniform substitution. Abelard takes such incomplete entailments to hold according to the theory of the topics (to be forms of so-called topical inference). The sample inference above is validated by the topic “from the species”, a set of metaphysical relations one of which is expressible in the rule “Whatever the species is predicated of, so too is the genus” which grounds the inferential force of the entailment. Against Boethius, Abelard maintained that topical rules were only needed for incomplete entailment, and in particular are not required to validate the classical moods of the categorical and hypothetical syllogism mentioned in the preceding paragraph.
zh: 结论可以对其前提既必然又相关，却 **不是** 形式有效的（不是完全蕴涵），还有另一条路径。诸命题之间的必然联系、诸意涵之间的纽带，可能是非形式的形而上学真理在一切可能世界中成立的函数。例如，人是一种动物，所以“如果苏格拉底是人，苏格拉底是动物”这一后承必然成立，前件的意涵迫使后件的意涵，但它在一致替换下不是形式有效的。阿伯拉尔认为这类不完全蕴涵依论题论（theory of the topics）成立（属于所谓论题推理的形式）。上面的例子由“出自种”的论题验证，这是一组形而上学关系，其中之一可表达为规则“凡述谓种者亦述谓属”，它为该蕴涵的推理力提供根据。与波爱修斯相对，阿伯拉尔主张论题规则只有在不完全蕴涵中才需要，特别是并不需要它们来验证前一段提到的直言三段论与假言三段论的经典诸式。

en: Abelard spends a great deal of effort to explore the complexities of the theory of topical inference, especially charting the precise relations among conditional sentences, arguments, and what he calls “argumentation” (roughly what follows from conceded premisses). One of the surprising results of his investigation is that he denies that a correlate of the Deduction Theorem holds, maintaining that a valid argument need not correspond to an acceptable conditional sentence, nor conversely, since the requirements on arguments and conditionals differ.
zh: 阿伯拉尔花了大量精力探讨论题推理理论的种种复杂性，尤其是精确刻画条件句、论证与所谓“论证活动”（argumentation，粗略地说即从已承认的前提得出的东西）之间的确切关系。他的研究有一个令人惊讶的结果：他否认演绎定理的对应物成立，主张有效论证不必对应一个可接受的条件句，反之亦然，因为论证与条件句各自的要求不同。

en: In the end, it seems that Abelard’s principles of topical inference do not work, a fact that became evident with regard to the topic “from opposites”: Abelard’s principles lead to inconsistent results, a result noted by Alberic of Paris. This led to a crisis in the theory of inference in the twelfth century, since Abelard unsuccessfully tried to evade the difficulty. These debates seem to have taken place in the later part of the 1130s, as Abelard was about to become embroiled with Bernard of Clairvaux, and his attention was elsewhere.
zh: 归根结底，阿伯拉尔的论题推理原则似乎并不奏效，“出自相反者”的论题使这一点变得明显：阿伯拉尔的原则导致不一致的结果——巴黎的阿尔贝里克（Alberic of Paris）指出了这一点。这引发了十二世纪推理理论的危机，因为阿伯拉尔未能成功绕开这一困难。这些论辩似乎发生在 1130 年代后期，当时阿伯拉尔即将与克莱尔沃的贝尔纳纠缠不清，注意力在别处。

en: 4. Philosophy of Language
zh: 4 语言哲学

en: Much of Abelard’s philosophy of language is devoted to analyzing how a given expression or class of expressions function logically: what words are quantifiers, which imply negation, and the like, so that the logic described above may be applied. To do so, he relies on the traditional division, derived from Aristotle, that sees the main linguistic categories as *name*, *verb*, and their combination into the *sentence*.
zh: 阿伯拉尔的语言哲学很大程度上致力于分析给定表达式或一类表达式如何在逻辑上运作：哪些词是量词，哪些蕴含否定，等等，从而使上述逻辑得以应用。为此他依赖源自亚里士多德的传统划分：主要语言范畴是 **名称** （name）、**动词** （verb）以及二者组合成的 **句子** （sentence）。

en: Abelard takes names to be conventionally significant simple words, usually without tense. So understood there are a wide variety of names: proper and common names; adjectives and adverbs; pronouns, whether personal, possessive, reflexive, or relative; conventional interjections such as ‘Goodness!’; and, arguably, conjunctions and prepositions (despite lacking definite signification), along with participles and gerundives (which have tense). Abelard usually, though not always, treats compound names such as ‘street-sweeper’ reductively. Even so his list is not general enough to catalogue all referring expressions. In point of fact, much of Abelard’s discussion of the semantics of names turns on a particular case that stands for the rest: common names. These are at the heart of the problem of universals, and they pose particular difficulties for semantics.
zh: 阿伯拉尔把名称视为约定地有意义的简单词，通常没有时态。照此理解，名称五花八门：专名与通名；形容词与副词；代词——无论人称、物主、反身还是关系代词；约定感叹词如“老天！”；以及（尽管缺乏明确意指）连词与介词，还有分词与动形词（它们有时态）。阿伯拉尔通常（虽不总是）把“扫街的”这类复合名称还原处理。即便如此，他的清单还不够一般，无法涵盖所有指称表达式。事实上，阿伯拉尔关于名称语义学的讨论大多围绕一个代表其余的特例：通名。通名位于共相问题的核心，并给语义学带来特殊的困难。

en: When Abelard puts forward his claim that universality is only a linguistic phenomenon, so that universals are “nothing more than words,” he raises the objection that unless common names are the names of common items, they will be meaningless, and so his view is no better than that of his teacher Roscelin (who held that universals were mere mouth noises). In reply Abelard clearly draws a distinction between two semantic properties names possess: reference (*nominatio*), a matter of what the term applies to; and sense (*significatio*), a matter of what hearing the term brings to mind, or more exactly the informational content (*doctrina*) of the concept the word is meant to give rise to, a causal notion. A few remarks about each are in order.
zh: 当阿伯拉尔提出普遍性只是语言现象、共相“不过是词”的主张时，他遇到的反驳是：除非通名是共同项的名称，否则它们将毫无意义，于是他的观点不比他的老师洛色林高明多少（洛色林认为共相不过是嘴里的响声）。作为回应，阿伯拉尔明确区分了名称具有的两个语义属性：指称（*nominatio*），即词项适用于什么；与意涵（*significatio*），即听到该词所唤起的东西，更确切地说，该词旨在引起的概念的信息内容（*doctrina*）——一个因果概念。对二者各需稍作说明。

en: Names, both proper and common, refer to things individually or severally. A name is linked with that of which it is the name as though there were someone who devised the name to label a given thing or kind of thing, a process known as “imposition” (modelled on Adam’s naming the animals in Genesis 2:19), rather like baptism. This rational reconstruction of reference does not require the person imposing the name, the “impositor”, to have anything more than an indefinite intention to pick out the thing or kind of thing, whatever its nature may be:
zh: 专名与通名都个别地或分别地指称事物。名称与它作为名称的东西之间的联系，仿佛曾有人为标示一个给定事物或一类事物而设计了该名称——这一过程称为“命名”（imposition，仿效《创世记》2:19 中亚当为动物命名的做法），很像施洗。这种对指称的理性重构，并不要求“命名者”对挑出那个事物或那类东西怀有超出某种不确定意图的更多东西，无论其本性如何：

en: The inventor [of names] intended to impose them according to some natures or distinctive properties of things, even if he himself did not know how to think correctly upon the nature or distinctive property of a thing.
zh: 命名者打算按事物的某些本性或区分性属性来施加名称，即使他自己并不知道如何正确思考事物的本性或区分性属性。

en: A name “has a definition in the nature of its imposition, even if we do not know what it is.” Put in modern terms, Abelard holds a theory of *direct reference*, in which the extension of a term is not a function of its sense. We are often completely ignorant of the proper conceptual content that should be associated with a term that has been successfully imposed.
zh: 一个名称“在其命名的本性中有一个定义，即便我们不知道它是什么”。用现代术语说，阿伯拉尔持一种 **直接指称** （direct reference）理论：词项的外延不是其意涵的函数。对于一个成功施加的词项，我们常常对应当与之相联系的恰当概念内容一无所知。

en: A proper name—the name of a primary substance—signifies a concrete individual (*hoc aliquid*), picking out its bearer as personally distinct from all else. Therefore, proper names are semantically singular referring expressions, closely allied to indexicals, demonstratives, and singular descriptions (or descriptive terms). Common names, by contrast, are semantically allied with expressions that have what Abelard calls “plural signification”. On the one hand, common names are like plural nouns; the common name ‘man’ is grammatically singular but operates like the plural term ‘men’—each refers to every man, although the plural term signifies individuals as part of a collection, whereas the common name distributively refers to each individual. On the other hand, common names are like terms such as ‘trio’ or ‘pair’ in that they pick out a determinate plurality of individuals, but only on an occasion of use, since their extension is variable.
zh: 专名——第一实体的名称——意指一个具体个体（*hoc aliquid*），把它的承载者作为与一切其他东西个人性地区别开来的东西挑出。因此专名是语义上单称的指称表达式，与索引词、指示词与单称描述（或描述性词项）紧密同类。与此相对，通名在语义上与阿伯拉尔所谓“复数意指”（plural signification）的表达式同类。一方面，通名像复数名词；通名“人”在语法上是单数，却像复数词项“人们”那样运作——二者都指称每一个人，尽管复数词项把个体作为集合的部分来意指，而通名分布地指称每一个体。另一方面，通名又像“三人组”或“一对”这样的词项：它们挑出一个确定的个体复数，但只在使用的场合，因为它们的外延是可变的。

en: Thus a common name distributively refers to concrete individuals, though not to them *qua* individuals. Instead, it severally picks out those individuals having a given nature: ‘human being’ refers to Socrates and to Plato, in virtue of each of them being human. This is not a shared feature of any sort; Socrates just is what he is, namely human, and likewise Plato is what he is, namely human too. Abelard states his deflationary position clearly in his *Logica* ‘*ingredientibus*’:
zh: 因此通名分布地指称具体个体，但并非作为个体指称它们。它分别挑出具有给定本性的那些个体：“人”指称苏格拉底与柏拉图，凭借二者各自是人。这并不是任何意义上的共享特征；苏格拉底就是他所是的东西，即人，柏拉图也是他所是的东西，即人。阿伯拉尔在 *Logica* ‘*ingredientibus*’ 中把他的祛魅立场说得明明白白：

en: Now it seems we should stay away from accepting the agreement among things according to what is not any thing—it’s as though we were to unite in nothing things that now exist!—namely, when we say that this [human] and that one agree in the human status, that is to say: in that they are human. But we mean precisely that they are human and don’t differ in this regard—let me repeat: [they don’t differ] in that they are human, although we’re not appealing to any *thing* [in this explanation].
zh: 现在，看来我们应当避免按“不是任何东西”的东西来接受事物之间的同意——就好像我们要把现存的诸事物统一于无之中！——也就是说，当我们在说这一个[人]与那一个人在人的身份（status）上一致时，意思就是：他们都为人。但我们的意思恰恰是他们都为人、在这一点上没有差别——让我重复：[他们没有差别]在于他们为人，尽管我们并没有诉诸任何 **东西** [来作这一解释]。

en: Socrates and Plato are real; their agreement is real, too, but it isn’t to be explained by appealing to any thing—their agreement just is their each being human. From a metaphysical point of view they have the same standing as human beings; this does not involve any metaphysically common shared ingredient, or indeed appeal to any ingredient at all. That is the sense in which there is a “common reason” for the imposition of a common name.
zh: 苏格拉底与柏拉图是实在的；他们的一致也是实在的，但解释它不应诉诸任何东西——他们的一致就是他们各自为人。从形而上学观点看，他们作为人有相同的身份；这并不涉及任何形而上学上共享的成分，甚至根本不诉诸任何成分。这就是施加通名有其“共同理由”（common reason）的那层意思。

en: For all that signification is posterior to reference, names do have signification as well. Abelard holds that the signification of a term is the informational content of the concept that is associated with the term upon hearing it, in the normal course of events. Since names are only conventionally significant, which concept is associated with a given name depends in part on the psychological conditioning of language-users, in virtue of which Abelard can treat signification as both a causal and a normative notion: the word ‘rabbit’ ought to cause native speakers of English to have the concept of a rabbit upon hearing it. Abelard is careful to insist that the signification is a matter of the informational content carried in the concept—mere psychological associations, even the mental images characteristic of a given concept, are not part of what the word *means*. Ideally, the concept will correspond to a real definition that latches onto the nature of the thing, the way ‘rational mortal animal’ is thought to be the real definition of ‘human being’, regardless of other associated features (even necessary features such as risibility) or fortuitous images (as any mental image of a human will be of someone with determinate features). Achieving such clarity in our concepts is, of course, an arduous business, and requires an understanding of how understanding itself works (see the discussion of Abelard’s philosophy of mind in Section 5). Yet one point should be clear from the example. The significations of some names, such as those corresponding to natural-kind terms, are abstractions in the sense that they include only certain features of the things to which the term refers. They do not positively exclude all other features, though, and are capable of further determinate specification: ‘rational mortal animal’ as the content of the concept of ‘human being’ signifies all humans, whatever their further features may be—tall or short, fat or thin, male or female, and so on.
zh: 尽管意涵后于指称，名称确实也有意涵。阿伯拉尔认为，一个词项的意涵是听到它时通常情况下与之相联系的概念的信息内容。由于名称只是约定地有意义，哪个概念与给定名称相联系，部分地取决于语言使用者的心理条件；凭借这一点，阿伯拉尔可以把意涵既当因果概念又当规范概念处理：“兔子”这个词应当使英语母语者听到时产生兔子的概念。阿伯拉尔谨慎地坚持：意涵在于概念所携带的信息内容——单纯的心理联想，甚至某一概念特有的心理意象，都不是词 **意指** 的东西的一部分。理想情况下，概念将对应一个抓住事物本性的实在定义，就像“理性的有死的动物”被认为是“人”的实在定义那样，而不涉及其他相关特征（即使是像“会笑”这样必然的特征）或偶然的意象（任何关于人的心理意象都必然带有确定的外貌特征）。当然，在概念中达到这样的清晰是件艰难的事业，需要理解理解本身如何运作（见第 5 节关于阿伯拉尔心灵哲学的讨论）。不过从这个例子应当清楚一点：有些名称（如对应自然类词项的那些名称）的意涵是抽象意义上的意涵，即它们只包含词项所指称事物的某些特征。但它们并不正面排除所有其他特征，而能够得到进一步的确定规定：“理性的有死的动物”作为“人”这个概念的内容意指所有人，无论他们还有什么进一步的特征——高或矮，胖或瘦，男或女，等等。

en: What holds for the semantics of names applies for the most part to verbs. The feature that sets verbs apart from names, more so than tense or grammatical person, is that verbs have connective force (*vis copulativa*). This is a primitive and irreducible feature of verbs that can only be discharged when they are joined with names in the syntactically appropriate way, reminiscent of the ‘unsaturatedness’ of concepts in Frege. Sentences are made up of names and verbs in such a way that the meaning of the whole sentence is a function of the meaning of its parts. That is, Abelardian semantics is fundamentally compositional in nature. The details of how the composition works are complex. Abelard works directly with a natural language (Latin) that, for all its artificiality, is still a native second tongue. Hence there are many linguistic phenomena Abelard is compelled to analyze that would be simply disallowed in a more formal framework.
zh: 名称语义学的情况大多也适用于动词。动词区别于名称的特征——比时态或语法人称更重要——是动词有连接力（*vis copulativa*）。这是动词的一种初始的、不可还原的特征，只有当动词以句法上恰当的方式与名称结合时才能释放出来，令人想起弗雷格那里概念的“未饱和性”。句子由名称与动词构成，使得整个句子的意义是其部分意义的函数。也就是说，阿伯拉尔的语义学根本上是组合性的。组合如何运作的细节很复杂。阿伯拉尔直接与一门自然语言（拉丁语）打交道——这门语言纵有人工性，仍是一门母语式的第二语言。因此有许多语言现象阿伯拉尔不得不加以分析，而在更形式的框架里它们会被干脆排除。

en: For example, Abelard notes that most verbs can occur as predicates in two ways, namely as a finite verbal form or as a nominal form combined with an auxiliary copula, so that we may say either ‘Socrates runs’ or ‘Socrates is running’; the same holds for transitive predication, for instance ‘Socrates hits Plato’ and ‘Socrates is hitting Plato.’ Abelard argues that in general the pure verbal version of predication is the fundamental form, which explains and clarifies the extended version; the latter is only strictly necessary where simple verbal forms are lacking. (The substantive verb ‘is’ requires special treatment.) Hence for Abelard the basic analysis of a predicative statement recognizes that two fundamentally different linguistic categories are joined together: the name *n* and the simple verbal function *V*( ), combined in the well-formed sentence *V*(*n*).
zh: 例如，阿伯拉尔注意到多数动词可以以两种方式充当谓词，即作为限定动词形式，或作为名词形式加系词，所以我们既可以说“苏格拉底跑”也可以说“苏格拉底在跑”；及物述谓也是如此，如“苏格拉底打柏拉图”与“苏格拉底正在打柏拉图”。阿伯拉尔论证：一般而言，纯动词形式的述谓是基本形式，它解释并澄清扩展形式；后者只在缺乏简单动词形式时才严格必要。（实体动词“是”需要特殊处理。）于是对阿伯拉尔来说，对一个述谓陈述的基本分析认识到：两个根本不同的语言范畴被结合在一起——名称 *n* 与简单动词函项 *V*()，组合成合式的句子 *V*(*n*)。

en: Abelard argues that sentences (*propositiones*) must signify more than just the understandings of the constituent name and verb. First, a sentence such as ‘Socrates runs’ deals with Socrates and with running, not with anyone’s understandings. We talk about the world, not merely someone’s understanding of the world. Second, sentences like ‘If something is human, it is an animal’ are false if taken to be about understandings, for someone could entertain the concept *human* without entertaining the concept *animal*, and so the antecedent would obtain without the consequent. Third, understandings are evanescent particulars, mere mental tokenings of concepts. But at least some consequential sentences are necessary, and necessity can’t be grounded on things that are transitory, and so not on understandings. Sentences must therefore signify something else in addition to understandings, something that can do what mere understandings cannot. Abelard describes this as signifying what the sentence says, calling what is said by the sentence its *dictum* (plural *dicta*).
zh: 阿伯拉尔论证，句子（*propositiones*）必须意指的不只是成分名称与动词的理解。第一，“苏格拉底跑”这样的句子处理的是苏格拉底与跑步，而不是任何人的理解。我们谈论的是世界，而不只是某人对世界的理解。第二，“如果某物是人，它就是动物”这样的句子若被当作关于理解的句子就是假的，因为一个人可以具有“人”这个概念而不具有“动物”这个概念，于是前件成立而后件不成立。第三，理解是倏忽即逝的殊例，只是概念的心理例示（tokening）。但至少有些推论性的句子是必然的，而必然性不能奠基于倏忽之物，因此也不能奠基于理解。所以句子必须意指理解之外的某种东西，某种能做理解做不到的事情的东西。阿伯拉尔把它描述为句子所说出的东西，把句子所说的称为它的 **所言** （dictum，复数 dicta）。

en: To the modern philosophical ear, Abelard’s *dicta* might sound like propositions, abstract entities that are the timeless bearers of truth and falsity. But Abelard will have nothing to do with any such entities. He declares repeatedly and emphatically that despite being more than and different from the sentences that express them, *dicta* have no ontological standing whatsoever. In the short space of a single paragraph he says that they are “no real things at all” and twice calls them “absolutely nothing.” They underwrite sentences, but they aren’t real things. For although a sentence says something, there is not some thing that it says. The semantic job of sentences is to *say* something, which is not to be confused with naming or denoting some thing. It is instead a matter of proposing how things are, provided this is not given a realist reading. Likewise, the truth of true sentences is not a property inhering in some timeless entity, but no more than the assertion of what the sentence says—that is, Abelard adopts a deflationary account of truth. A sentence is true if things stand in the way it says, and things make sentences true or false in virtue of the way they are (as well as in virtue of what the sentences say), and nothing further is required. The sentence ‘Socrates runs’ is true because Socrates runs, which is all that can be said or needs to be said.
zh: 以现代哲学的耳朵听来，阿伯拉尔的 **所言** 可能听起来像命题——那些作为真假的超时间承载者的抽象实体。但阿伯拉尔绝不接受任何这类实体。他反复而强调地宣称：尽管所言不同于并多于表达它们的句子，**所言** 没有任何存在论地位。在短短一段话里，他说它们“根本不是实在的东西”，并两次称它们“绝对是虚无”。它们支撑着句子，但它们不是实在之物。因为句子虽然说出某事，却并没有某个它所说出的东西。句子的语义职责是 **说** 出某事，这不可与命名或指称某个东西相混淆。它说的是事物如何排列，只要这不被给予实在论的解读。同样，真句子的真不是内在于某个超时间实体的属性，而不过是断定了句子所说——也就是说，阿伯拉尔采纳了真理的紧缩（deflationary）说明。一个句子是真的，如果事物像它所说的那样排列；事物使句子为真或为假，凭借事物所是的方式（以及句子所说的内容），此外别无所求。“苏格拉底跑”是真的，因为苏格拉底在跑——能说的和需要说的就这么多。

en: 5. Philosophy of Mind
zh: 5 心灵哲学

en: Aristotelian philosophy of mind offers two analyses of intentionality: the conformality theory holds that we think of an object by having its very form in the mind, the resemblance theory that we do so by having a mental image in the mind that naturally resembles the object. Abelard rejects each of these theories and proposes instead an adverbial theory of thought, showing that neither mental images nor mental contents need be countenanced as ontologically independent of the mind. He gives a contextual explication of intentionality that relies on a linguistic account of mental representation, adopting a principle of compositionality for understandings.
zh: 亚里士多德的心灵哲学提供了对意向性的两种分析：符合论（conformality theory）主张我们通过在心灵中拥有对象的那个形式来思考对象；相似论（resemblance theory）主张我们通过在心灵中拥有一幅自然地相似于对象的心理意象来思考对象。阿伯拉尔拒绝这两种理论，代之以思想的副词论（adverbial theory），表明无论心理意象还是心理内容都无须被当作独立于心灵的存在者。他给出意向性的语境化阐发，依赖对心理表征的语言学说明，并对理解采纳组合性原则。

en: The first Aristotelian analysis takes understanding to be the mind’s acquisition of the form of the object that is understood, without its matter. For an understanding to be about some thing—say, a cat—is for the form of the cat to be in the mind or intellective soul. The inherence of the form in matter makes the matter to be a thing of a certain kind, so that the inherence of the form *cat* in matter produces an actual cat, whereas the (immaterial) inherence of the form *cat* in the mind transforms the mind into an understanding of a cat: the mind becomes (formally) identical with its object. Since the ‘aboutness’ of understanding is analyzed as the commonness or identity of form in the understanding and the thing understood, we may call this approach the *conformality theory* of understanding. This theory captures the intuition that understanding somehow inherits or includes properties of what is understood, by reducing the intentionality of understanding to the objective identity of the form in the mind and the form in the world.
zh: 第一种亚里士多德分析把理解当作心灵对被理解对象的形式的获得（无其质料）。一个理解关涉某物——比如说一只猫——就是猫的形式在心灵或理智灵魂之中。形式内在于质料使质料成为某一种类的东西：形式“猫”内在于质料产生一只实际的猫，而形式“猫”（非物质地）内在于心灵则把心灵转变为对一只猫的理解：心灵（形式地）等同于其对象。由于理解的“关涉性”（aboutness）被分析为理解与被理解者之间的形式的共同性或同一性，我们可以称这一进路为理解的 **符合论**。这一理论捕捉到了如下直觉：理解以某种方式继承或包含被理解者的性质，办法是把理解的意向性还原为心灵中的形式与世界中的形式的客观同一。

en: The second Aristotelian analysis takes understanding to be the mind’s possession of a concept that is a natural likeness of, or naturally similar to, that of which it is a concept. For an understanding to be about some thing, such as a cat, is for there to be an occurrent concept in the mind that is a natural likeness of a cat. The motivation for calling the likeness “natural” is to guarantee that the resemblance between the understanding and what is understood is objective, and that all persons have access to the same stock of concepts. (The conformality theory does this by postulating the objective existence of forms in things and by an identical process in all persons of assimilating or acquiring forms.) We may call this approach the *resemblance theory* of understanding: mental acts are classified according to the distinct degree and kind of resemblance they have to the things that are understood.
zh: 第二种亚里士多德分析把理解当作心灵对某概念的占有，该概念是被理解者的自然相似者（natural likeness），或自然地相似于被理解者。一个理解关涉某物（比如一只猫），就是心灵中存在一个现时的概念，它是猫的自然相似者。把这种相似称为“自然的”的动机，是保证理解与被理解者之间的相似是客观的，以及所有人都能进入同一概念库。（符合论靠设定形式在事物中的客观存在、靠所有人同化或获得形式的同一过程来做到这一点。）我们可以称这一进路为理解的 **相似论**：心理活动按它们与被理解者的相似性的程度与种类的不同来分类。

en: The resemblance theory faces well-known problems in spelling out the content of resemblance or likeness. For example, a concept is clearly immaterial, and as such radically differs from any material object. Furthermore, there seems to be no formal characteristic of a mental act in virtue of which it can non-trivially be said to resemble anything else. To get around these difficulties, mediaeval philosophers, like the British Empiricists centuries later, appealed to a particular kind of resemblance, namely pictorial resemblance. A portrait of Socrates is about Socrates in virtue of visually resembling Socrates in the right ways. And just as there are pictorial images that are about their subjects, so too are there mental images that are about things. These mental images, whether they are concepts or are contained in concepts, explain the way in which a concept is ‘about’ an object. For an understanding to be about a cat is for it to be or contain a mental image of a cat. The phenomenon of mental ‘aboutness’ is explicated by the more familiar case of pictorial aboutness, itself reduced to a real relation of resemblance.
zh: 相似论在阐明相似或类似的内涵时面临众所周知的困难。例如，概念显然是非物质的，因此与任何物质对象截然不同。此外，似乎不存在心理活动的任何形式特征，使之能够非平凡地被说成相似于任何别的东西。为了绕开这些困难，中世纪哲学家——就像几个世纪后的英国经验主义者——诉诸一种特殊的相似，即图像式的相似（pictorial resemblance）。苏格拉底的肖像之所以是关于苏格拉底的，是因为它在正确的方面视觉地相似于苏格拉底。正如存在关于其主体的图像，也存在关于事物的心理意象。这些心理意象——无论它们是概念还是包含在概念之中——解释了概念“关涉”对象的方式。一个理解关涉一只猫，就是它是或者包含一幅猫的心理意象。心理“关涉性”现象由更熟悉的图像关涉性（pictorial aboutness）来阐发，而后者本身被还原为相似性的实在关系。

en: Despite their common Aristotelian heritage, the conformality theory and the resemblance theory are not equivalent. The transformation of the mind through the inherence of a form is not necessarily the same as the mind’s possession of a concept. Equally, natural likeness or resemblance need not be understood as identity of form; formal identity need not entail genuine resemblance, due to the different subjects in which the form is embodied.
zh: 尽管有共同的亚里士多德渊源，符合论与相似论并不等价。通过形式的内在于身一个心灵的转变，未必就是心灵对一个概念的占有。同样，自然相似或相似不必理解为形式的同一；由于形式所寄身的主体不同，形式的同一不必蕴含真正的相似。

en: The standard way to reconcile the conformality theory and the resemblance theory is to take the mind’s possession of a concept to be its ability to transform itself through the inherence of a form, construing formal identity as natural likeness, where having a form in the mind that is identical to the form of the object understood just is to have a mental image of that very object.
zh: 调和符合论与相似论的标准方式，是把心灵对概念的占有当作心灵通过形式的内在于身而转变自身的能力，把形式的同一解读为自然相似：在心灵中拥有与被理解对象相同的形式，恰恰就是拥有那个对象的心理意象。

en: Abelard argues against conformality as follows. Consider a tower, which is a material object with a certain length, depth, and height; assume that these features compose its form, much as the shape of a statue is its form. According to Aristotelian metaphysics, the inherence of a form in a subject makes the subject into something characterized by that form, as for instance whiteness inhering in Socrates makes him something white. The forms of the tower likewise make that in which they inhere to be tall, wide, massive—all physical properties. If these forms inhere in the mind, then, they should make the mind tall, wide, and massive, an absurd conclusion: the mind “cannot extend itself in length or width.” Yet it is a cardinal thesis of the conformality theory that the mind has the identical form that is possessed by the external object, the tower, although the form of (say) length is by its very nature physical. Thus, Abelard concludes, conformality is incoherent.
zh: 阿伯拉尔对符合论的反对如下。考虑一座塔，它是一个具有一定长、宽、高的物质对象；假定这些特征构成它的形式，正如雕像的形状是它的形式。按亚里士多德形而上学，形式内在于主体使主体成为被该形式所刻画的东西，例如白内在于苏格拉底使他成为某种白的东西。塔的形式同样使它们所内在于其中的东西成为高的、宽的、庞大的——全是物理性质。那么，如果这些形式内在于心灵，它们就应当使心灵成为高的、宽的、庞大的——一个荒谬的结论：心灵“不能在长与宽上延伸自身”。然而符合论的核心论题恰恰是：心灵拥有与外部对象（塔）相同的形式，尽管（比如说）长度的形式按其本性是物理的。于是阿伯拉尔得出结论：符合论不融贯。

en: Abelard’s main objection to the resemblance theory is that mental images *qua* images, like any sign, are inert: they require interpretation. A sign is just an object. It may be taken in a significative role, though it need not be. Abelard notes that this distinction holds equally for non-mental signs: we can treat a statue as a lump of bronze or as a likeness. Mental images are likewise inert. For a sign to function significatively, then, something more is required beyond its mere presence or existence. But the resemblance theory doesn’t recognize the need to interpret the mental image as an image, and thereby mistakenly identifies understanding with the mere presence of a mental image in the mind. Abelard concludes that mental images have only an instrumental role in thought, describing them as “intermediary signs of things” (*intersigna rerum*). Intentionality derives instead from the act of attention (*attentio*) directed upon the mental image. Proof is found in the fact that that we can “vary the understanding” simply by attending to different features of the mental image: the selfsame image—say, a fig tree—can be used to think about this very fig tree, or trees in general, or plant life, or my lost love with whom I sat under it, or anything whatsoever. There is no intrinsic feature of the mental image in virtue of which it is about any given thing; if there were, Abelard notes, we could determine by inspection what a sign is about—but we can’t. Mental images, therefore, can’t explain the intentionality of understanding, because their role is merely instrumental. We think with them, and cannot avoid them; but they do not explain intentionality.
zh: 阿伯拉尔对相似论的主要反驳是：心理意象作为意象，与任何符号一样是惰性的：它们需要解释。符号只是一个对象。它可以被放进一个意指性的角色，但未必如此。阿伯拉尔指出，这一区分对非心理的符号同样成立：我们可以把一座雕像当作一块青铜，也可以当作一幅肖像。心理意象同样是惰性的。要让符号意指性地起作用，在它的单纯在场或存在之外还需要更多的东西。但相似论并不承认需要把心理意象解释为意象，从而错误地把理解等同于心理意象在心灵中的单纯在场。阿伯拉尔得出结论：心理意象在思想中只起工具性作用，他把它们描述为“事物的中介符号”（*intersigna rerum*）。意向性反而来源于指向心理意象的注意活动（*attentio*）。证明是：我们可以仅仅通过注意心理意象的不同特征来“改变理解”：同一幅意象——比如一棵无花果树——可以用来思考这棵无花果树本身，或一般的树，或植物生命，或我曾坐在树下倾诉的旧爱，或任何东西。心理意象没有任何内在特征使它关涉某个给定的东西；如果有，阿伯拉尔指出，我们本可以通过检视来确定一个符号是关于什么的——但我们不能。因此心理意象解释不了理解的意向性，因为它们的角色只是工具性的。我们用它们思考，也无法避开它们；但它们解释不了意向性。

en: Abelard draws the conclusion that intentionality is a primitive and irreducible feature of the mind, our acts of attending to things. Different acts of attention are intrinsically different from one another; they are about what they are about in virtue of being the kind of attention they are. Hence Abelard adopts what is nowadays called an *adverbial* theory of thought.
zh: 阿伯拉尔得出结论：意向性是心灵的一种初始而不可还原的特征，即我们注意事物的那些活动。不同的注意活动彼此内在地不同；它们关涉其所关涉的东西，凭的就是它们作为那种注意所是的样子。因此阿伯拉尔采纳了如今所谓的思想的 **副词论**。

en: Given that intentionality is primitive, Abelard adopts a contextual approach to mental content: he embeds these irreducible acts of attention in a structure whose articulation helps define the character of its constituent elements. The structure Abelard offers is linguistic, a logic of mental acts: just as words can be said to express thoughts, so too we can use the articulated logic of language to give a theory of understanding. In short, Abelard gives something very like a linguistic account of mental representation or intentionality. To this end he embraces a principle of compositionality, holding that what an understanding is about is a function of what its constituent understandings are about. The unity of the understanding of a complex is a function of its logical simplicity, which is characterized by the presence of what Abelard calls “a single dominant conjunction” (the logical operator of greatest scope). Hence the understanding of a complex may be treated as a complex of distinct understandings, aggregated in the same thought, with its (logical) structure flowing from the ‘dominant conjunction’ over the other logical operations governing its constituent understandings. Abelard’s acts of attention thus display the logical structure of the understanding they express, and thereby give the semantics of written or spoken language. Much of Abelard’s writings on logic and dialectic are given over to working out the details as a scheme for explicating mental content.
zh: 既然意向性是初始的，阿伯拉尔对心理内容采取一种语境化的进路：他把这些不可还原的注意活动嵌入一个结构，而该结构的展开帮助定义其构成要素的性质。阿伯拉尔提供的结构是语言性的，一种心理活动的逻辑：正如词语可以说表达思想，我们同样可以用语言的展开逻辑给出一个理解理论。简言之，阿伯拉尔给出的东西非常接近对心理表征或意向性的语言学说明。为此他接受一条组合性原则，主张一个理解所关涉的东西是其诸成分理解所关涉者的函数。复合理解的统一性是其逻辑简单性的函数，后者的特征在于阿伯拉尔所谓“单一主导联结”（the logical operator of greatest scope）的存在。于是复合的理解可以处理为不同理解的复合体，聚合在同一思想之中，其（逻辑）结构从主导联结流向支配其成分理解的其他逻辑操作。阿伯拉尔的注意活动因此展示出它们所表达的理解的逻辑结构，从而给出书面或口头语言的语义学。阿伯拉尔关于逻辑与辩证法的许多著述都用于把细节展开为阐明心理内容的方案。

en: 6. Ethics
zh: 6 伦理学

en: Abelard takes the rational core of traditional Christian morality to be radically *intentionalist*, based on the following principle: the agent’s intention alone determines the moral worth of an action. His main argument against the moral relevance of consequences turns on what contemporary philosophers often refer to as moral luck. Suppose two men each have the money and the intention to establish shelters for the poor, but one is robbed before he can act whereas the second is able to carry out his intention. According to Abelard, to think that there is a moral difference between them is to hold that “the richer men were the better they could become … this is the height of insanity!” Deed-centred morality loses any kind of purchase on what might have been the case. Likewise, it cannot offer any ground for taking the epistemic status of the agent into account, although most people would admit that ignorance can morally exculpate an agent. Abelard makes the point with the following example: imagine the case of fraternal twins, brother and sister, who are separated at birth and each kept in complete ignorance of even the existence of the other; as adults they meet, fall in love, are legally married and have sexual intercourse. Technically this is incest, but Abelard finds no fault in either to lay blame.
zh: 阿伯拉尔认为传统基督教道德的理性内核是彻底的 **意向主义** （intentionalist），基于如下原则：行动者的意图（intention）单独决定一个行动的道德价值。他反对后果之道德相关性的主要论证，落在当代哲学家常说的道德运气（moral luck）上。设想两个人都有钱、都有为穷人建立庇护所的意图，但一人在行动之前被抢劫，另一人得以实现其意图。按阿伯拉尔的看法，认为二者之间存在道德差别，就是认为“人越有钱就能变得越好……这是十足的疯狂！”以行动为中心的道德对“本来可能怎样”完全失去把握。同样，它也无法为考虑行动者的认识状态提供根据，尽管多数人会承认无知可以在道德上开脱行动者。阿伯拉尔用下面的例子说明这一点：设想一对龙凤胎，兄妹在出生时被分开，彼此连对方的存在都完全不知道；成年后他们相遇、相爱、合法结婚并发生性关系。严格说这是乱伦，但阿伯拉尔认为双方都无可指摘。

en: Abelard concludes that in themselves deeds are morally indifferent. The proper subject of moral evaluation is the agent, via his or her intentions. It might be objected that the performance or nonperformance of the deed could affect the agent’s feelings, which in turn may affect his or her intentions, so that deeds thereby have moral relevance (at least indirectly). Abelard denies it:
zh: 阿伯拉尔得出结论：行动（deed）本身在道德上是无关紧要的（indifferent）。道德评价的适当主体是行动者，经由其意图。有人可能反驳说：行动的做与不做会影响行动者的感受，这又会影响其意图，因此行动由此获得道德相关性（至少间接地）。阿伯拉尔否认这一点：

en: For example, if someone forces a monk to lie bound in chains between two women, and by the softness of the bed and the touch of the women beside him he is brought to pleasure (but not to consent), who may presume to call this pleasure, which nature makes necessary, a fault?
zh: 例如，如果有人强迫一个修士被绑着锁链躺在两个女人之间，由于床榻的柔软与身旁女人的触摸，他产生了快感（但没有表示同意），谁敢僭称这种自然使之必然的快感是一种罪过呢？

en: We are so constructed that the feeling of pleasure is inevitable in certain situations: sexual intercourse, eating delicious food, and the like. If sexual pleasure in marriage is not sinful, then the pleasure itself, inside or outside of marriage, is not sinful; if it is sinful, then marriage cannot sanctify it—and if the conclusion were drawn that such acts should be performed wholly without pleasure, then Abelard declares they cannot be done at all, and it was unreasonable (of God) to permit them only in a way in which they cannot be performed.
zh: 我们被构造得使快感的感觉在某些情形中不可避免：性交、享用美食，等等。如果婚姻中的性快感不是罪，那么快感本身——无论婚内婚外——就不是罪；如果它是罪，那么婚姻也无法使之神圣——而如果由此得出结论说这类行为应当完全无快感地进行，那么阿伯拉尔宣称它们根本无法进行，而且（上帝）只以一种无法进行的方式允许它们，是不合理的。

en: On the positive side, Abelard argues that unless intentions are the key ingredient in assessing moral value it is hard to see why coercion, in which one is forced to do something against his or her will, should exculpate the agent; likewise for ignorance—though Abelard points out that the important moral notion is not simply ignorance but strictly speaking negligence. Abelard takes an extreme case to make his point. He argues that the crucifiers of Christ were not evil in crucifying Jesus. (This example, and others like it, got Abelard into trouble with the authorities, and it isn’t hard to see why.) Their ignorance of Christ’s divine nature didn’t by itself make them evil; neither did their acting on their (false and mistaken) beliefs, in crucifying Christ. Their non-negligent ignorance removes blame from their actions. Indeed, Abelard argues that they would have sinned had they thought crucifying Christ was required and did *not* crucify Christ: regardless of the facts of the case, failing to abide by one’s conscience in moral action renders the agent blameworthy.
zh: 从积极方面说，阿伯拉尔论证：除非意图是评价道德价值的关键成分，否则很难解释为什么强制——某人被迫违反自己的意愿做某事——应当开脱行动者；无知也一样——不过阿伯拉尔指出，重要的道德概念不是单纯的无知，严格说而是疏忽（negligence）。阿伯拉尔用一个极端的例子来表明这一点。他论证：把基督钉上十字架的人在这样做时并无罪恶。（这个例子以及类似的例子给阿伯拉尔惹了当局的麻烦，原因不难想见。）他们对基督神性的无知本身并没有使他们成为恶人；他们基于（错误与失误的）信念把基督钉上十字架的行动也没有。他们非疏忽的无知使他们的行动免于罪责。的确，阿伯拉尔论证说：如果他们认为钉死基督是必须做的而 **没有** 钉死基督，他们反倒犯了罪：无论事实如何，在道德行动中不服从自己的良心就使行动者应受责备。

en: There are two obvious objections to Abelard’s intentionalism. First, how is it possible to commit evil voluntarily? Second, since intentions are not accessible to anyone other than the agent, doesn’t Abelard’s view entail that it is impossible to make ethical judgements?
zh: 对阿伯拉尔意向主义有两个明显的反驳。第一，怎么可能自愿地作恶？第二，既然意图除了行动者本人无人可达，阿伯拉尔的观点难道不意味着伦理判断是不可能的？

en: With regard to the first objection, Abelard has a twofold answer. First, it is clear that we often want to perform the deed and at the same time do not want to suffer the punishment. A man wants to have sexual intercourse with a woman, but not to commit adultery; he would prefer it if she were unmarried. Second, it is clear that we sometimes “want what we by no means want to want”: our bodies react with pleasure and desire independently of our wills. If we act on such desires, then our action is done “of” will, as Abelard calls it, though not voluntarily. There is nothing evil in desire: there is only evil in acting on desire, and this is compatible with having contrary desires.
zh: 关于第一个反驳，阿伯拉尔有双重的回答。第一，显然我们常常想做出那个行动，同时又不想承受惩罚。一个男人想与一个女人性交，但不想犯通奸罪；他更希望她未婚。第二，显然我们有时“想要我们绝不想要想要的东西”：我们的身体独立于我们的意志而产生快感与欲望。如果我们按这种欲望行动，那么我们的行动是“出于”意志（of will）——用阿伯拉尔的话说——尽管并非自愿（voluntary）。欲望本身并无罪恶：罪恶只在于按欲望行动，而这与怀有相反的欲望相容。

en: With regard to the second objection, Abelard grants that other humans cannot know the agent’s intentions—God, of course, does have access to internal mental states, and so there can be a Final Judgement. However, Abelard does not take ethical judgement to pose a problem. God is the only one with a right to pass judgement. Yet this fact doesn’t prevent us from enforcing canons of human justice, because, Abelard holds, human justice has primarily an exemplary and deterrent function. In fact, Abelard argues, it can even be just to punish an agent we strongly believe had no evil intention. He cites two cases. First, a woman accidentally smothers her baby while trying to keep it warm at night, and is overcome with grief. Abelard maintains that we should punish her for the beneficial example her punishment may have on others: it may make other poor mothers more careful not to accidentally smother their babies while trying to keep them warm. Second, a judge may have excellent (but legally impermissible) evidence that a witness is perjuring himself; since he cannot show that the witness is lying, the judge is forced to rule on the basis of the witness’s testimony that the accused, whom he believes to be innocent, is guilty. Human justice may with propriety ignore questions of intention. Since there is divine justice, ethical notions are not an idle wheel—nor should they be, even on Abelard’s understanding of human justice, since they are the means by which we determine which intentions to promote or discourage when we punish people as examples or in order to deter others.
zh: 关于第二个反驳，阿伯拉尔承认其他人无法知道行动者的意图——而上帝当然能进入内在心理状态，所以可以有末日审判。不过，阿伯拉尔并不认为伦理判断构成问题。上帝是唯一有裁断权的一方。然而这一事实并不妨碍我们执行人类正义的法规，因为按阿伯拉尔的看法，人类正义主要起示范与威慑作用。事实上阿伯拉尔论证：惩罚一个我们强烈相信并无恶意的行动者，甚至可以是正义的。他举了两个例子。第一，一位母亲夜里在给孩子保暖时不小心把孩子闷死了，她悲痛欲绝。阿伯拉尔主张我们应当惩罚她，为了她的惩罚可能对他人产生的有益示范：它可以使其他贫穷的母亲更小心，不要在孩子保暖时闷死他们。第二，一位法官可能有极好（但法律上不可采）的证据表明一个证人在作伪证；既然他无法证明证人在撒谎，法官只能依据证人的证词判处那个他相信是无辜的被告有罪。人类正义可以正当地忽略意图问题。既然存在神圣正义，伦理概念就不是空转的飞轮——即便按阿伯拉尔对人类正义的理解也不应当是：它们是我们决定在以儆效尤或威慑他人而惩罚人时，应当鼓励或阻抑哪些意图的手段。

en: There is a sense, then, in which the only certifiable sin is acting against one’s conscience, unless one is morally negligent. Yet if we cannot look to the intrinsic value of the deeds or their consequences, how do we determine which acts are permissible or obligatory? Unless conscience has a reliable guide, Abelard’s position seems to open the floodgates to well-meaning subjectivism.
zh: 于是，在某种意义上，唯一可判定的罪就是违背良心行事，除非一个人有道德疏忽。然而，如果我们不能看行动的内在价值或其后果，我们如何确定哪些行动是允许的或必须的？除非良心有可靠的向导，阿伯拉尔的立场似乎为善意的相对主义敞开了闸门。

en: Abelard solves the problem by taking obedience to God’s will—the hallmark of morally correct behaviour, and itself an instance of natural law—to be a matter of the agent’s intention conforming to a purely formal criterion, namely the Golden Rule (“Do to others as you would be done to”). This criterion can be discovered by reason alone, without any special revelation or religious belief, and is sufficient to ensure the rightness of the agent’s intention. But the resolution of this problem immediately leads to another problem. Even if we grant Abelard his naturalistic ethics, why should an agent care if his or her intentions conform to the Golden Rule? In short, even if Abelard were right about morality, why be moral?
zh: 阿伯拉尔解决这一问题的办法是：把服从上帝的意志——道德正确行为的标志，本身即自然法的一个实例——当作行动者的意图符合一个纯形式判准的事情，即黄金法则（“己所欲，施于人”）。这一判准单凭理性即可发现，不需要任何特殊启示或宗教信仰，并足以确保行动者意图的正确。但这一问题的解决立即引出另一个问题。即便我们承认阿伯拉尔的自然主义伦理学，行动者为什么要在乎其意图是否符合黄金法则？简言之，即便阿伯拉尔关于道德是对的，为什么要道德？

en: Abelard’s answer is that our happiness—to which no one is indifferent—is linked to virtue, that is, to habitual morally correct behaviour. Indeed, Abelard’s project in the *Collationes* is to argue that reason can prove that a merely naturalistic ethics is insufficient, and that an agent’s happiness is necessarily bound up with accepting the principles of traditional Christian belief, including the belief in God and an Afterlife. In particular, he argues that the Afterlife is a condition to which we ought to aspire, that it is a moral improvement even on the life of virtue in this world, and that recognizing this is constitutive of wanting to do what God wants, that is, to live according to the Golden Rule, which guarantees as much as anything can (pending divine grace) our long-term postmortem happiness.
zh: 阿伯拉尔的回答是：我们的幸福——没有谁对它无动于衷——与德性（virtue）相连，也就是与习惯性的道德正确行为相连。的确，阿伯拉尔在《对话集》中的方案，就是要论证理性可以证明：单纯自然主义的伦理学是不充分的，行动者的幸福必然与接受传统基督教信念的原则（包括对上帝与来世的信仰）绑在一起。他特别论证：来世是我们应当向往的境地，它是对今世德性生活的一种道德改进，而认识到这一点，就构成了想做上帝想做之事——即按黄金法则生活——的一部分，黄金法则（在圣宠降临之前）尽可能保证我们死后长期的光福（postmortem happiness）。

en: The Philosopher first argues with the Jew, who espouses a ‘strict observance’ moral theory, namely obedience to the Mosaic Law. One of the arguments the Jew offers is the Slave’s Wager (apparently the earliest-known version of Pascal’s Wager). Imagine that a Slave is told one morning by someone he doesn’t know whether to trust that his powerful and irritable Master, who is away for the day, has left instructions about what to do in his absence. The Slave can follow the instructions or not. He reasons that if the Master indeed left the instructions, then by following them he will be rewarded and by not following them he will be severely punished, whereas if the Master did not leave the instructions he would not be punished for following them, though he might be lightly punished for not following them. (This conforms to the standard payoff matrix for Pascal’s Wager.) That is the position the Jew finds himself in: God has apparently demanded unconditional obedience to the Mosaic Law, the instructions left behind. The Philosopher argues that the Jew may have other choices of action and, in any event, that there are rational grounds for thinking that ethics is not a matter of action in conformity to law but a matter of the agent’s intentions, as we have seen above.
zh: 哲人先与犹太人辩论。犹太人信奉一种“严格遵行”的道德理论，即服从摩西律法。犹太人提出的论证之一是奴隶的赌注（Slave's Wager，显然是已知最早的帕斯卡赌注版本）。设想一个奴隶某天早晨被一个他不知道该不该信任的人告知：他那位有权而暴躁、当日离家的主人留下了指示，说明他不在时该做什么。奴隶可以遵行指示，也可以不遵行。他推想：如果主人确实留下了指示，那么遵行者受赏，违者受重罚；而如果主人没有留下指示，他也不会因遵行而受罚，尽管可能因不遵行而受轻罚。（这符合帕斯卡赌注的标准收益矩阵。）犹太人的处境正是如此：上帝显然要求无条件服从摩西律法——那份留下的指示。哲人则论证：犹太人也许还有别的行动选择；而且无论如何，存在合理的根据认为，伦理不是合乎律法的行动问题，而是行动者意图的问题，如上文所见。

en: The Philosopher then argues with the Christian. He initially maintains that virtue entails happiness, and hence there is no need of an Afterlife since a virtuous person remains in the same condition whether dead or alive. The Christian, however, reasons that the Afterlife is better, since in addition to the benefits conferred by living virtuously, the agent’s will is no longer impeded by circumstances. In the Afterlife we are no longer subject to the body, for instance, and hence are not bound by physical necessities such as food, shelter, clothing, and the like. The agent can therefore be as purely happy as life in accordance with virtue could permit, when no external circumstances could affect the agent’s actions. The Philosopher grants that the Afterlife so understood is a clear improvement even on the virtuous life in this world, and joins with the Christian in a cooperative endeavour to define the nature of the virtues and the Supreme Good. Virtue is its own reward, and in the Afterlife nothing prevents us from rewarding ourselves with virtue to the fullest extent possible.
zh: 哲人继而与基督徒辩论。他起初主张德性蕴含幸福，因此不需要来世，因为德性之人无论生死都处于同一境地。但基督徒推论说：来世更好，因为除了有德生活所赋予的好处之外，行动者的意志不再受处境阻碍。在来世我们不再受制于身体，因而不受食物、居所、衣物之类物理必需的约束。行动者因此可以像符合德性的生活所允许的那样纯粹地幸福，而没有任何外部处境能影响行动者的行动。哲人承认如此理解的来世甚至比今世的有德生活明显更好，并与基督徒一道进入合作性的事业，去界定诸德性与至善的本性。德性是自身的回报，而在来世，没有什么能阻止我们以最大可能的程度用德性来自我酬报。

en: 7. Theology
zh: 7 神学

en: Abelard held that reasoning has a limited role to play in matters of faith. That he gave reasoning a role at all brought him into conflict with those we might now call *anti*-dialecticians, including his fellow abbot Bernard of Clairvaux. That the role he gave it is limited brought him into conflict with those he called “pseudo-dialecticians,” including his former teacher Roscelin.
zh: 阿伯拉尔认为推理在信仰事务中只应扮演有限的角色。他给了推理一个角色，这一点就使他与我们如今可能称为 **反** 辩证法家（anti-dialecticians）的人冲突，包括他的同道院长克莱尔沃的贝尔纳。而他给推理的角色是有限的，这又使他与自称“伪辩证法家”（pseudo-dialecticians）所贬斥的人冲突——包括他昔日的老师洛色林。

en: Bernard of Clairvaux and other anti-dialecticians seem to have thought that the meaning of a proposition of the faith, to the extent that it can be grasped, is plain; beyond that plain meaning, there is nothing we can grasp at all, in which case reason is clearly no help. That is, the anti-dialecticians were *semantic realists* about the plain meaning of religious sentences. Hence their impatience with Abelard, who seemed not only bent on obfuscating the plain meaning of propositions of the faith, which is bad enough, but to do so by reasoning, which has no place either in grasping the plain meaning (since the very plainness of plain meaning consists in its being grasped immediately without reasoning) or in reaching some more profound understanding (since only the plain meaning is open to us at all).
zh: 克莱尔沃的贝尔纳与其他反辩证法家似乎认为：信仰命题的意义，就其可把握的程度而言，是直白的；在直白含义之外，我们根本无法把握任何东西，在这种情况下理性显然无用。也就是说，反辩证法家对宗教句子的直白意义持 **语义实在论** 立场。因此他们对阿伯拉尔的不耐烦：阿伯拉尔似乎不仅一心要搅浑信仰命题的直白意义——这已经够糟了——还要用推理来搅浑，而推理既无助于把握直白意义（直白意义的直白恰恰在于无须推理即可直接把握），也无助于达到某种更深邃的理解（因为只有直白意义对我们敞开）。

en: Abelard has no patience for the semantic realism that underlies the sophisticated anti-dialectical position. Rather than argue against it explicitly, he tries to undermine it. From his commentaries on scripture and dogma to his works of speculative theology, Abelard is first and foremost concerned to show how religious claims can be understood, and in particular how the application of dialectical methods can clarify and illuminate propositions of the faith. Furthermore, he rejects the claim that there is a plain meaning to be grasped. Outlining his method in the Prologue to his *Sic et non*, Abelard describes how he initially raises a question, e.g. whether priests are required to be celibate, and then arranges citations from scriptural and patristic authorities that at least seem to answer the question directly into positive and negative responses. (Abelard offers advice in the Prologue for resolving the apparent contradictions among the authorities using a variety of techniques: see whether the words are used in the same sense on both sides; draw relevant distinctions to resolve the issue; look at the context of the citation; make sure that an author is speaking in his own voice rather than merely reporting or paraphrasing someone else’s position; and so on.) Now each authority Abelard cites seems to speak clearly and unambiguously either for a positive answer to a given question or for a negative one. If ever there were cases of plain meaning, Abelard seems to have found them in authorities, on opposing sides of controversial issues. His advice in the Prologue amounts to saying that sentences that seem to be perfect exemplars of plain meaning in fact have to be carefully scrutinized to see just what their meaning is. Yet that is just to say that they do not have plain meaning at all; we have to use reason to uncover their meaning. Hence the anti-dialecticians don’t have a case.
zh: 阿伯拉尔对支撑这种精致的反辩证立场的语义实在论没有耐心。他不与之正面论辩，而是设法挖它的墙脚。从他对圣经与教义的注疏到他的思辨神学著作，阿伯拉尔首先关注的是表明宗教主张如何能够被理解，尤其是辩证方法的运用如何能够澄清与照亮信仰命题。此外，他拒绝“存在一个可把握的直白意义”的主张。阿伯拉尔在《是与否》的序言里概述了他的方法：他先提出一个问题，例如司铎是否必须独身，然后把经文与教父权威中至少看起来直接回答该问题的引文，分成肯定与否定两方排开。（阿伯拉尔在序言里给出了化解权威之间表面矛盾的各种技巧：看两边的词是否在同一个意义上使用；作相关区分以解决问题；看引文的语境；确认作者是以自己的声音说话，而不只是转述或复述他人的立场；等等。）现在，阿伯拉尔所引的每一个权威，就一个给定问题或肯定或否定，都显得说得清楚明白、毫不含糊。如果世上有直白意义的范例，阿伯拉尔似乎在有争议问题的对立方权威中找到了它们。他在序言中的建议等于说：那些看似直白意义完美典范的句子，其实必须仔细审查才能弄清它们的意义究竟是什么。而这恰恰等于说它们根本不具有直白意义；我们必须用理性去揭示它们的意义。于是反辩证法家并没有道理。

en: There is a far more serious threat to the proper use of reason in religion, Abelard thinks (*Theologia christiana* 3.20):
zh: 阿伯拉尔认为，对宗教中理性的正当使用有一个严重得多的威胁（《基督徒神学》3.20）：

en: Those who claim to be dialecticians are usually led more easily to [heresy] the more they hold themselves to be well-equipped with reasons, and, to that extent more secure, they presume to attack or defend any position the more freely. Their arrogance is so great that they think there isn’t anything that can’t be understood and explained by their petty little lines of reasoning. Holding all authorities in contempt, they glory in believing only themselves—for those who accept only what their reason persuades them of, surely answer to themselves alone, as if they had eyes that were unacquainted with darkness.
zh: 那些自称辩证法家的人，越是自认为装备了充分的理由，就越容易被引向[异端]，并且在那程度上更加有恃无恐，更加放肆地进攻或防守任何立场。他们的傲慢如此之大，以致认为没有什么不能被他们那点可怜的推理所理解与解释。他们藐视一切权威，只相信自己而沾沾自喜——因为只接受理性说服的人，分明只回答自己，就像他们的眼睛从不认识黑暗。

en: Such pseudo-dialecticians take reason to be the final arbiter of all claims, including claims about matters of faith. More exactly, Abelard charges them with holding that (a) everything can be explained by human reason; (b) we should only accept what reason persuades us of; (c) appeals to authority have no rational persuasive force. Real dialecticians, he maintains, reject (a)–(c), recognizing that human reason has limits, and that some important truths may lie outside those limits but not beyond belief; which claims about matters of faith we should accept depends on both the epistemic reliability of their sources (the authorities) and their consonance with reason to the extent they can be investigated.
zh: 这样的伪辩证法家把理性当作一切主张的最终裁判，包括关于信仰事务的主张。更确切地说，阿伯拉尔指责他们主张：(a) 一切都可由人类理性解释；(b) 我们只应接受理性所说服的；(c) 诉诸权威没有任何理性的说服力。他主张，真正的辩证法家拒绝 (a)–(c)，承认人类理性有限，而某些重要真理也许在这些界限之外，却不在信仰之外；关于信仰事务的哪些主张我们应当接受，既取决于其来源（诸权威）的认识可靠性，也取决于在其可被考察的范围内它们与理性的协调。

en: Abelard’s arguments for rejecting (a)–(c) are sophisticated and subtle. For the claim that reason may be fruitfully applied to a particular article of faith, Abelard offers a particular case study in his own writings. The bulk of Abelard’s work on theology is devoted to his dialectical investigation of the Trinity. He elaborates an original theory of identity to address issues surrounding the Trinity, one that has wider applicability in metaphysics. The upshot of his enquiries is that belief in the Trinity is rationally justifiable since as far as reason can take us we find that the doctrine makes sense—at least, once the tools of dialectic have been properly employed.
zh: 阿伯拉尔为拒绝 (a)–(c) 给出的论证精致而细密。对于“理性可以有成果地应用于某条信仰条款”的主张，阿伯拉尔在自己的著述中给出了一个个案研究。阿伯拉尔神学著作的大部分，都用于对三位一体作辩证考察。他阐发了一种原创的同一性理论来处理围绕三位一体的种种问题，这一理论在形而上学中有更广的适用性。他探究的结论是：对三位一体的信仰在理性上可证成，因为就理性所能到达之处，我们发现该教义讲得通——至少在辩证工具得到恰当运用之后。

en: The traditional account of identity, derived from Boethius, holds that things may be either generically, specifically, or numerically the same or different. Abelard accepts this account but finds it not sufficiently fine-grained to deal with the Trinity. The core of his theory of identity, as presented in his *Theologia christiana*, consists in four additional modes of identity: (1) essential sameness and difference; (2) numerical sameness and difference, which Abelard ties closely to essential sameness and difference, allowing a more fine-grained distinction than Boethius could allow; (3) sameness and difference in definition; (4) sameness and difference in property (*in proprietate*). Roughly, Abelard’s account of essential and numerical sameness is intended to improve upon the identity-conditions for things in the world given by the traditional account; his account of sameness in definition is meant to supply identity-conditions for the features of things; and his account of sameness in property opens up the possibility of there being different identity-conditions for a single thing having several distinct features.
zh: 传统的同一性说明源自波爱修斯：事物可以在属上、种上或数目上相同或不同。阿伯拉尔接受这一说明，但认为它不够细密，不足以处理三位一体。他在《基督徒神学》中呈现的同一性理论的核心，在于四种增补的同一样式：(1) 本质上的同与异；(2) 数目上的同与异——阿伯拉尔把它与本质的同异紧密相连，作出比波爱修斯更细的区分；(3) 定义上的同与异；(4) 属性上的同与异（in proprietate）。大致说来，阿伯拉尔关于本质同异与数目同异的说明，意在改进传统说明给出的世间事物的同一性条件；他关于定义同异的说明，意在为事物的诸特征提供同一性条件；他关于属性同异的说明，则开辟了这样的可能：同一个事物具有几个不同特征时，可以有不同组的同一性条件。

en: Abelard holds that two things are *the same in essence* when they are numerically the same concrete thing (*essentia*), and essentially different otherwise. The Morning Star is essentially the same as the Evening Star, for instance, since each is the selfsame planet Venus. Again, the formal elements that constitute a concrete thing are essentially the same as one another and essentially the same as the concrete thing of which they are the formal constituents: Socrates is his essence (Socrates is what it is to be Socrates). The corresponding general thesis does not hold for parts, however. Abelard maintains that the part is essentially different from the integral whole of which it is a part, reasoning that a given part is completely contained, along with other parts, in the whole, and so is less than the quantity of the whole.
zh: 阿伯拉尔主张，两个事物 **在本质上相同** （same in essence），当它们是数目上同一个具体事物（*essentia*）；否则本质上不同。例如晨星本质上与昏星相同，因为二者都是同一个行星金星。再如，构成一个具体事物的诸形式成分，彼此本质相同，并与它们作为形式成分的那个具体事物本质相同：苏格拉底就是他的本质（苏格拉底就是作为苏格拉底之所是）。不过，相应的普遍论题对部分并不成立。阿伯拉尔主张，部分与它作为部分之整全整体本质不同，理由是：一个给定的部分与其他部分一起被完全包含在整体之中，因而小于整体的量。

en: Numerical difference does not map precisely onto essential difference. The failure of numerical sameness may be due to one of two causes. First, objects are not numerically the same when one has a part that the other does not have, in which case the objects are essentially different as well. Second, objects are numerically different when neither has a part belonging to the other. Numerical difference thus entails the failure of numerical sameness, but not conversely: a part is not numerically the same as its whole, but it is not numerically different from its whole. Thus one thing is essentially different from another when either they have only a part in common, in which case they are not numerically the same; or they have no parts in common, in which case they are numerically different as well as not numerically the same. Since things may be neither numerically the same nor numerically different, the question “How many things are there?” is ill-formed as it stands and must be made more precise, a fact Abelard exploits in his discussion of the Trinity.
zh: 数目差异并不与本质差异精确对应。数目同一的失败可能出于两个原因之一。第一，当一个对象具有另一个对象所没有的部分时，二者数目上不同，此时它们本质上也不同。第二，当二者都没有属于对方的任何部分时，它们数目上不同。因此数目差异蕴含数目同一的失败，但不反过来：部分与其整体数目上不同一，但它与整体也并非数目上不同。于是，一个事物与另一个事物本质不同，当：要么它们只有一个共同部分，此时它们数目上不同一；要么它们没有共同部分，此时它们数目上不同，而且也非数目同一。既然事物可以既非数目同一又非数目不同，“有多少东西？”这个问题照字面就是不合法的，必须进一步精确化——阿伯拉尔在讨论三位一体时利用了这一事实。

en: Essential and numerical sameness and difference apply directly to things in the world; they are extensional forms of identity. By contrast, sameness and difference in definition is roughly analogous to modern theories of the identity of properties. Abelard holds that things are *the same in definition* when what it is to be one requires that it be the other, and conversely; otherwise they differ in definition.
zh: 本质与数目的同异直接适用于世界中的事物；它们是外延性的同一形式。相比之下，定义上的同异大致类似现代的属性同一理论。阿伯拉尔主张，事物 **在定义上相同** （same in definition），当作为其中之一要求是另一个，反之亦然；否则定义上不同。

en: Finally, things are *the same in property* when they specify features that characterize one another. Abelard offers an example to clarify this notion.
